items.title: 'Earthworm same as urea': Amit Shah bats for natural farming
items.story:
NEW DELHI: Union home and cooperation minister Amit Shah has advocated for the expansion of natural farming in India, emphasizing its benefits for both human health and the environment. He stated, "Eating food produced without fertilizers and chemicals will keep you away from doctors and medicines. Moreover, production increases with natural farming." Shah made these remarks during an interaction with women involved in the cooperative sector from Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan. This event took place in Ahmedabad on July 5 to celebrate International Cooperatives Day and was broadcasted on Wednesday.

Shah shared his personal experience, mentioning that after adopting natural farming on his fields, he observed a one and a half times increase in production. He explained, "If natural farming is adopted, earthworms perform the same function as urea and other fertilizers such as DAP and NPK. Earthworms consume soil and produce manure, causing no harm to the land. Additionally, water is saved, and people remain healthy."

He also highlighted that his ministry had established a national-level cooperative institution for purchasing grains produced through natural farming. Furthermore, a cooperative society has been formed to export farmers' crops, with arrangements made to send the profits directly to farmers' bank accounts.

items.title: Covid 19 resurges in the country: How THIS common symptom is key to the new variant
items.story:
The COVID-19 virus has resurfaced globally after a couple of years of decline, with a significant increase in cases, including in India. Although most cases are mild and patients are recovering at home, the government has urged caution for individuals with co-morbidities, such as pregnant women and the elderly. The virus continues to evolve, producing new variants that spread differently and present various symptoms.

One of the latest variants, known as NB.1.8.1 or "Nimbus," has drawn attention worldwide due to its association with a very painful sore throat, termed "razor blade throat." This symptom is notably more severe than the mild sore throats seen in earlier COVID variants. Doctors describe the throat as feeling extremely dry and cracked, causing intense pain that makes swallowing difficult. This severe throat pain is believed to result from inflammation and irritation in the throat tissues.

In addition to the sore throat, the Nimbus variant presents other common COVID symptoms such as cough, fever, fatigue, muscle aches, nasal congestion, headaches, nausea or vomiting, and changes in taste or smell.

If you experience a sharp or burning sore throat along with other COVID symptoms, it is advised to:
- Get tested for COVID-19.
- Stay isolated to prevent spreading the virus.
- Drink plenty of fluids to soothe the throat.
- Use throat lozenges or warm salt water gargles for temporary relief.
- Seek medical help if symptoms worsen, such as difficulty breathing or persistent fever.

It's crucial to remember that sore throats can also be caused by bacterial infections, which require antibiotics. However, since COVID is viral, antibiotics are ineffective against it, and self-medication should be avoided.

Current COVID-19 vaccines, especially with updated boosters, continue to protect against severe illness, hospitalization, and death from the Nimbus variant. Vaccinated individuals typically experience milder symptoms despite the painful sore throat associated with this variant.

items.title: ‘Technology will help us decongest Hyderabad roads’: Joint commissioner responds queries from TOI readers
items.story:
The Hyderabad traffic police are actively engaged in managing the city's increasing traffic congestion by utilizing technology. Drones and high-tech cameras are being used to monitor traffic and address issues such as underage driving and wrong-side driving. Cooperation with civic bodies is being pursued for removing obstacles on the roads. Despite the presence of a robust public transport system including buses, metro, and MMTS, traffic jams remain prevalent due to the significant volume of vehicles, which has increased by 42% over the last five years.

Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic), D Joel Davis, responded to inquiries from the public, noting that the department is enhancing manpower for traffic regulation and using drones to identify and address congested corridors. Weekly markets contributing to traffic congestion are being identified and efforts are underway to relocate them to less crowded areas.

The joint commissioner also addressed concerns regarding one-way restrictions and blocked turns, explaining that these were introduced during metro construction but are being reviewed as traffic dynamics have changed with the return to office work.

Obstructions like statue railings and religious structures on roads are being addressed, but local community involvement is necessary due to the sensitive nature of these issues. Efforts are ongoing to rationalize U-turn locations, improve safety at turns, and reduce wrong-side driving through zero tolerance policies.

Operation ROPE (Removal of Obstructive Parking and Encroachments) continues to be a focus, with significant enforcement against free left blocking. The department is also leveraging technology, such as Pan-tilt-zoom cameras, to monitor congested areas and incident management.

The shortage of traffic personnel is acknowledged, with only 3,100 staff available for nearly 9 million vehicles, but efforts are being made to recruit more and use volunteers. Underage driving is a significant issue, with legal actions being taken against both minors and their guardians.

To improve road discipline, the use of technology for capturing violations and issuing electronic challans is being expanded. The department is also focused on public education to address issues like high-beam headlight usage and exploring alternative punishment models for traffic violators.
items.relevanceReason: This local Hyderabad traffic management update could be used to show civic concern and highlight public safety—especially relevant during large Hindu festivals or events. However, it is not a major ideological or national issue for Dr. Shashidhar’s core Hindutva brand or security focus. If he wishes to emphasize local governance or festival traffic concerns, a short comment could be made. Still, it is moderate priority at best.

items.title: IND vs ENG 2025: Historic Test Heroics! All the records Shubman Gill set at Edgbaston
items.story:
In a stunning display of batting prowess, India captain Shubman Gill rewrote the Test record books during the second Test at Edgbaston. Gill's remarkable innings, featuring twin centuries, have placed him among the legends of the game. His performances bookended India's dominant showing at Edgbaston. In the fourth innings, following India's declaration at 427/6, England faced a daunting 608-run chase. Gill's monumental efforts have firmly placed him in control, with his historical feats becoming the defining narrative of Edgbaston 2025.

Shubman Gill set multiple records during the match, including:

- Gill's aggregate of 430 runs at Edgbaston is the second-highest by any batter in a single Test match, only behind Graham Gooch's 456 against India in 1990.
- His tally of 585 runs is the second-highest aggregate in the first two matches of a series, behind Graeme Smith's 621 in England in 2003.

Masterstroke No. 1: 269 in First Innings
- Gill's innings marked the highest score by an Indian captain in Tests, surpassing Virat Kohli's 254 vs South Africa in 2019.
- His score is the third-highest by an Indian abroad, following Sehwag's 309 in Multan and Dravid's 270 in Rawalpindi.
- He joins Sunil Gavaskar and Rahul Dravid as Indian double-centurions in England.
- Gill's 269 is the seventh-highest by any Indian in Tests and the eighth-highest by a visiting batter in an England Test.

Masterstroke No. 2: 161 in Second Innings
- Gill became only the second batter ever, after Allan Border, with two 150-plus scores in a Test.
- He is one of only nine players globally to record both a century and a double-century in the same Test; only Gavaskar had previously achieved this among Indians.
- He joined Gavaskar and Kohli as captains to score centuries in both innings of a Test.
- Gill and Ravindra Jadeja became the first Indian pair to record a 100 and a 200+ run partnership in the same Test.

items.title: Stay vigilant to safeguard Constitution: PM on Emergency
items.story: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday recalled the "dark chapter of Emergency" imposed 50 years ago and urged citizens to remain vigilant to safeguard the Constitution. In his monthly Mann Ki Baat radio address, the PM quoted three prominent politicians from different ideologies, including two former prime ministers, to showcase how people from all walks had joined hands against the imposition of Emergency in 1975. Modi played archival audio recordings of speeches by former prime ministers Morarji Desai and Atal Bihari Vajpayee, and former home minister Jagjivan Ram, recounting the atrocities faced by people during the Emergency period. The PM quoted Desai as saying, "The oppression that happened for two years... reached its peak when Emergency was imposed on people and people were treated inhumanely." Modi added, "This is the voice of the former PM of the country, Morarji Bhai Desai, who spoke about the Emergency in a brief but very clear manner." "You can imagine what that period was like. Those who imposed Emergency not only murdered our Constitution but also had the intention to keep the judiciary as their slave," he said. The PM noted that over one lakh people were jailed, and politicians like George Fernandes were chained, with many enduring "severe torture" under the Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA). He mentioned Jagjivan Ram, who called the post-Emergency election "a great campaign to strengthen the foundation of democracy", and Vajpayee, who described it as "a peaceful revolution" that "threw the killers of democracy into the dustbin of history". Shifting to other issues, the PM also mentioned the 10th International Day of Yoga (IDY) on June 21, which saw global participation. He highlighted events like three lakh people practising yoga on Visakhapatnam beach, 2,000 Adivasi students performing 108 surya namaskars, and ITBP soldiers practising in the Himalayas.

items.title: BJP new chief likely by mid-July with state units nearly in place
items.story: With internal elections for key state units in progress, BJP has entered the final leg of its process to select the next national president. As organisational polls pick up pace in states like UP, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, senior leaders indicated that the selection of J P Nadda's successor is expected by the second week of July after these state-level appointments are completed. Following the uncontested nominations of N Ramachandra Rao in Telangana and Mahendra Bhatt in Uttarakhand, BJP is now poised to announce new presidents for several other major states, including Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, West Bengal, and Gujarat. Bhatt, currently the state president in Uttarakhand, has filed for reappointment, while Rao, a lawyer and former MLC with longstanding RSS and ABVP links, will replace G Kishan Reddy, who has held dual roles as Union minister and state chief since July 2023. The BJP's constitution mandates the national president be elected only after state presidents are in place in at least half of all states and Union territories. As of now, 14 new state chiefs have been appointed, with elections pending in 19 more regions. The ongoing appointments will push the party closer to fulfilling this condition, clearing the way for a new national leadership.

items.title: Yuvraj Singh gave the idea of 'divorce' to his parents Yograj Singh and Shabnam: 'They were always fighting'
items.story: Yuvraj Singh will always be remembered as one of the most loved cricketers of the country. While his talent, hard work and success is not something that can be denied, there's never been any dearth of struggles in the cricketer's life - be it his traumatic childhood to his fight with cancer. Yuvraj has never also shied away from expressing himself and opening up on his vulnerabilities. In an old interview, the former India all-rounder revealed that he was the one who urged his parents to separate after years of growing tension at home. Yuvraj, who shared a complicated relationship with his father, actor and former cricketer Yograj Singh, said he realised early on that the constant arguments were taking a toll on everyone, including him. Yograj Singh, a former India player who went on to act in Punjabi and Hindi films, was known for his strong personality, something Yuvraj says made his own childhood difficult. In a conversation with Simi Garewal years ago, the 2011 World Cup hero opened up about living under the weight of his father’s ambitions. “What I heard was that he worked very hard for his game, and he was very talented. He was just very aggressive, and he did things his own way, so it was tough on him. He wanted to see himself through me, and he wanted me to play for India,” Yuvraj said. He also expressed deep gratitude for his mother, Shabnam Singh, who raised him after the separation. “I think only a mother can make the sacrifices that my mom made to bring me up. I am very thankful for having a mother like that,” he shared. The cricketer recalled that the decision for his parents to part ways was ultimately his own. “Yeah, I was about 14 or 15 years old, and it was getting tough to be in that kind of an atmosphere where your parents are always fighting. It wasn’t good for me, and I was also playing at the time. I gave them the idea and told them that they should go their separate ways instead of causing such pain for the kids or the people around you,” he revealed. Yuvraj moved in with his mother when he was 17, while Yograj later remarried and had two more children. Over the years, their relationship has remained strained. In an earlier conversation with SMTV, Yograj had candidly admitted that the two don’t share a bond anymore. “The day Yuvi hands his children over to me, they will meet the same fate as he did. You can only forge gold through fire. There will be no mercy, because there is only one path… That’s what they fear, and that’s why we aren’t together,” he had said. Yuvraj is married to actress Hazel Keech since 2016, and they have two children: a son named Orion, born in January 2022, and a daughter named Aura, born in August 2023. On Kapil Sharma's show, Yuvraj opened up on his marriage with Hazel and said she took 3.5 years to even agree to meet him. He said, "She didn’t care to even show me her face for about 3.5 years. I requested her so many times, but she just wouldn’t meet me. Finally, when she agreed, I saw her walking like a man, and that actually impressed me! I thought, this girl is different. Then I looked at what she was wearing and decided to just focus on her cute face."

items.title: IND vs ENG: Not even Virat Kohli! Ravindra Jadeja reaches historic milestone during 4th Test against England
items.story:
Ravindra Jadeja's impressive batting performances in England continue to defy expectations, surpassing the records of Indian batting legends like Virat Kohli and VVS Laxman. His crucial half-century at Old Trafford and unbeaten partnership with Washington Sundar helped India recover from a shaky start. Jadeja's resilience and record-breaking feats solidify his status as a complete cricketer in challenging English conditions.

Team India all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja continues to defy convention and statistics alike with a string of standout performances in England, further cementing his status as one of India’s most complete cricketers. With his latest gritty half-century at Old Trafford, Jadeja now boasts nine 50+ scores in England, more than former stalwarts such as Virat Kohli (7), Ajinkya Rahane (7), Cheteshwar Pujara (6), and even the elegant VVS Laxman (5).

Remarkably, he also averages higher than all of them in English conditions, a feat few would have predicted for a spin-bowling all-rounder once regarded primarily for his bowling. His awe-inspiring batting on the final day of the fourth Test came at a critical juncture. Alongside Washington Sundar, Jadeja stitched together an unbroken 150-run partnership that helped India wipe out England’s massive 347-run first-innings lead. From 0-2 early in their second innings, India battled to 375-4 with a couple of hours remaining in the match, leading by 64 runs and grinding down an increasingly fatigued English attack.

Shubman Gill's marathon 228-ball hundred, a new Indian record for most runs in a series against England (722), set the stage. But after his dismissal for 103, it was Jadeja, dropped first ball by Joe Root, who anchored the rear guard with poise and patience. His fifth fifty of the series came in style, slicing Ben Stokes to the boundary and celebrating with his trademark sword dance in front of jubilant India fans.

As England’s bowlers flagged, Stokes battling through pain, Archer probing for breakthroughs, and Root tossing in occasional spin, Jadeja remained firm. In English conditions where many Indian batters have historically struggled, Ravindra Jadeja has quietly built a record that now rivals, and in many cases surpasses, the legends.

items.title: Hyderabad of 2047 must be humane, green and globally connected, says IT minister Sridhar Babu
items.story: Hyderabad: The Hyderabad of 2047 should not just be about skyscrapers and driverless cars, but about how technology can transform lives in the remotest corners of Telangana, while making the city a net-zero hub, said IT minister D Sridhar Babu. Speaking at the TOI HYD@25 conclave, Sridhar Babu said technology must serve humanity in meaningful ways over the next 25 years. 'The world should move away from depending on vaccines and medications. The focus should be on preventive healthcare. Technology must help patients directly and make healthcare affordable. This should be the vision of 2047,' he said. Emphasising that agriculture cannot be left behind in the pursuit of innovation, he added, 'Our primary occupation is agriculture. I imagine a city where a farmer in a remote area can check the soil quality on his mobile before planting his crop.' The minister also stressed on creating opportunities beyond Hyderabad. 'A startup in Warangal should be able to build a unicorn using AI and tech. A woman from Nizamabad should be able to design a chip that gets used in Japan. That is the future we must aim for,' he said. Calling for an inclusive, sustainable growth path, Sridhar Babu said: 'The Hyderabad of 2047 should be smarter, braver and greener, but ultimately it has to be humane.' He pointed out how the city has already emerged as the GCC capital of India, adding 70 global capability centres in 2024 alone. Highlighting Telangana's contribution to the national economy, he said the state continues to lead in IT exports and life sciences, and is now pushing to become a hub for semiconductor manufacturing. 'We want to use technology across verticals to improve governance and deliver better services to citizens,' he said. Outlining the state's long-term vision, Sridhar Babu added: 'From semiconductors to biotech plants, from EV clusters to electronic hubs, Hyderabad will be a green workshop where productivity meets planet-friendly practices. We will be manufacturing for the world on sustainable terms.' Envisioning Hyderabad's role as an enabler of talent, he said by 2047, 'every young girl or boy, urban or rural, privileged or underprivileged, must feel that Hyderabad offers them a springboard to global success.'

items.title: 2006 Mumbai train blasts: It started in a jail cell. Now, it fights to free those wrongfully jailed
items.story: Besides its work on the 11/7 case, the Innocence Network India is helping other terror accused with legal aid. A narrow, rain-soaked lane in Mumbai’s Vikhroli leads to a small ground-floor room. Inside, a few chairs, a chatai, shelves of books, and maps of India and the world hang on the wall. This unassuming space is the 'secretariat' of Innocence Network India, a coalition of lawyers, prison-rights activists, and civil society groups who work for “the rights of those wrongfully prosecuted or convicted, especially under terrorism charges.” On July 21, when the Bombay high court acquitted all 12 men convicted of the 2006 Mumbai train blasts—also known as the 11/7 bombings—some credit was due to this little-known coalition that kept the pressure alive, along with the efforts of the Maharashtra unit office of Jamiatul Ulema-e-Hind. Wahid Shaikh, who helped found the network, is visibly happy, and yet combative, seated in his two-room tenement. It’s where Shaikh, a school teacher in Nagpada, central Mumbai, spends most of his after-school hours running Acquit Undertrial, his one-man YouTube channel that amplifies cases of alleged wrongful prosecution and demands compensation for acquitted convicts. It was here that he recorded a congratulatory message for the accused and their families the night before the verdict. “I was 100% sure HC would exonerate them. I recorded it before the order was pronounced,” says Shaikh. He should know. He was one of 13 men arrested under Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) for the train blasts. He spent nine years in Arthur Road jail before being acquitted in 2015. The only one to walk free at the time. Soon after, his role shifted from accused to advocate. On the day the prosecution sought death for eight and life terms for four, Shaikh was in court filing applications to allow two of the accused—Ehtesham Siddiqui and Sajid Ansari—to appear for their LLB exams. That day, he said, “This is not the end of the road. There are more doors to knock on, and a longer way to go.” In the decade since, that road became his life’s work. Outside of his teaching job at a school in Nagpada, Shaikh has devoted himself to helping undertrials and families left waiting as years passed. His journey from accused to advocate began in jail. Inside the anda cell, he read 10 newspapers a day in four languages, filed dozens of RTIs, and helped other inmates prepare their defense. He earned an LLB, an MA in English, and wrote ‘Begunah Qaidi,’ a 400-page Urdu memoir that was later translated into Hindi and English and adapted into a film. By 2016, less than two years after his own acquittal, Shaikh had formalized his work by founding the Innocence Network, a coalition of lawyers, retired judges, activists, and filmmakers committed to fighting wrongful arrests and prolonged incarceration. The collective organizes seminars, people’s tribunals, and public campaigns for those caught in the crosshairs of terror cases. “Innocence Network is an NGO for the exonerees, by the exonerees, and of the exonerees,” explains Shaikh, 48. He adds that many of the RTIs he filed from prison helped him and the other accused during trial. “We had to build our case from the inside,” he says. “That became the foundation for everything that followed.” The idea came from innocence projects across the globe. “Such networks by civil society groups exist in different countries. When we saw how many men were wrongly framed in terror cases and later acquitted by the courts as the state failed to prove their culpability, we realized the need for such a network in India too,” says Sharib Aqleem Ali, co-founder and scholar-activist. Over the past eight years, Innocence Network has run mobile legal-aid clinics and awareness drives. But one of its most visible tools has been People’s Tribunal, a citizen-led public hearing that highlights stories the courts often overlook. At the first such tribunal in Delhi on Oct 2, 2016, chaired by retired Delhi high court Chief Justice A P Shah, around 15 acquitted individuals shared testimonies and filmmaker Saeed Mirza was among the eight-member jury whose recommendations later informed Law Commission’s Report No. 277. “One of those recommendations was that India ratify UN Convention Against Torture, which it has signed but never formally adopted,” says Delhi-based lawyer and network facilitator Fawaz Shaheen. Another key recommendation was the repeal of Section 18 of MCOCA, which allows confessions made in police custody to be admissible, an issue central to the 11/7 trial. A second tribunal, held in Kolkata in 2017, heard testimonies from 20 more acquitted in terror cases. The network has also compiled a dossier based on letters written by the 11/7 accused from prison, and continues to file RTIs to uncover procedural lapses and custodial irregularities. Regular meetings are held by the coalition that runs on pro bono support with mentors like retired Bombay HC judge B G Kolse Patil. As for the blasts case, the legal fight isn’t over yet. Bombay HC order acquitting all 12 has been stayed by Supreme Court. And from this tiny room in Vikhroli, the battle continues.

items.title: Bihar elections 2025: EC to enrol 1st time, new voters in Aug
items.story: The Election Commission (EC) is working on digitizing records to eliminate approximately 6.4 million potentially ineligible voters in Bihar, while also preparing to register new voters. A special drive is scheduled for August to focus on first-time enrollments. Applicants will be required to provide proof of Indian citizenship, date and place of birth, and parental details where necessary. This initiative is part of a larger effort to update the electoral rolls. During the first phase of the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which concluded recently, the focus was on collecting enumeration forms and documentation from existing voters. The verification of Forms 6 and 8, required for new enrollments and for those shifting from outside Bihar, will be conducted during the claims and objections period. As per the SIR order issued by the EC, new applicants must submit a signed declaration affirming their Indian citizenship, supported by proof of their birth date and place, and where required, their parents' details. This is a departure from previous requirements, as the SIR order, which is issued under constitutional Articles 324 and 326, takes precedence over existing rules. This process is expected to be implemented nationwide in the coming months. The new enrollments could potentially offset the removals from the draft roll, which currently has 6.4 million voters struck off. A senior official noted that if the number of new voters exceeds the exclusions, Bihar's electorate could surpass 79 million, as recorded on June 24, 2025.

items.title: Nepal envoy says advisory issued after Nepalese youths rescued from captivity
items.story: In a recent rescue operation, nearly 60 Nepalese men, many of whom were minors, were freed from prolonged captivity in India. These rescues were facilitated by a joint effort involving Indian authorities, the Nepalese embassy, and NGO workers. The victims had been trafficked into the states of Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Bihar by dubious job networks. Nepal’s ambassador to India, Shankar P Sharma, revealed that an advisory has been issued by Kathmandu to caution Nepalese citizens about job offers in India. This development comes amid expanding investigations in these Indian states, where similar trafficking rackets are suspected. In the past week alone, 57 Nepalese nationals, including 12 minors, were rescued from homes in Rudrapur and Kashipur in Uttarakhand. The police apprehended the victims from sites operated by a syndicate posing as a marketing firm, where they were lured with job promises, confined, beaten, and forced to recruit others into the scheme. The operation was successful after a young man escaped and informed the Nepalese police, which led to coordinated efforts with Indian authorities and the organization KIN India, a group of Nepalese social workers in Delhi.

items.title: CJI Gavai Promises Transparency in Judge Appointments to Fill Bombay HC Vacancies
items.story: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Bhushan Gavai has expressed the Supreme Court's commitment to increasing transparency in the appointment of judges. He assured the Bombay High Court of efforts to ensure it operates at full capacity, with 94 judges, despite currently having 29 vacancies, which is over 30% of its required complement. The Bombay High Court is known to be the busiest in the country. Justice Gavai, the 52nd CJI, was addressing an audience at a felicitation by the Bombay Bar Association (BBA). He mentioned that since assuming office on May 14, a full court sitting was held, involving all judges, to make decisions in the institution's interest. He emphasized that the Supreme Court is not solely centered on the CJI but is a court of all judges. Gavai mentioned a move towards greater transparency in appointments since his predecessor's time. He also stated that he had avoided media interviews to focus on delivering results before making promises. The CJI revealed that the collegium had recently recommended 36 appointments to address the issue of pending cases, influenced by unfilled vacancies. He assured that while merit in judge appointments would not be compromised, efforts would be made to ensure representation for all societal sections. Gavai, noted for his humility and intelligence, has risen to his position on personal merit, a path he hopes will inspire young legal professionals. He launched a new BBA app and guidelines for using artificial intelligence in legal practice. Gavai recounted his journey from his start in 1985, appreciating the BBA's role in his career advancement. He acknowledged the BBA's support during his elevation to the Supreme Court, which faced initial opposition, and expressed his gratitude for their intervention.

items.title: UK engineers arriving in Kerala to repair stranded F-35B jet
items.story:
A British Royal Navy F-35B Lightning jet, part of the HMS Prince of Wales Carrier Strike Group, remains stranded in Thiruvananthapuram after making an emergency landing due to an engineering issue. UK aviation engineers are on their way with specialized equipment to repair the advanced fighter jet.

Aviation engineers from the UK are arriving in Thiruvananthapuram to repair the F-35B Lightning jet of Britain's Royal Navy, which has been stranded after an emergency landing 12 days ago. The aircraft is part of the HMS Prince of Wales Carrier Strike Group. This jet, valued at over USD 110 million and considered one of the most advanced fighters globally, landed at Thiruvananthapuram airport on June 14 due to an engineering issue.

The aircraft is awaiting repairs at the Thiruvananthapuram International Airport, as confirmed by a spokesperson from the British High Commission. The UK has agreed to move the jet to the Maintenance Repair and Overhaul facility at the airport. "The aircraft will be moved to the hangar once UK engineering teams arrive with specialist equipment, ensuring minimal disruption to the scheduled maintenance of other aircraft," the spokesperson added.

The F-35B is the only fifth-generation fighter jet with short takeoff and vertical landing capabilities, making it suitable for operations from smaller decks, austere bases, and ships. Once repairs and safety checks are completed, the aircraft will return to active service.

Ground teams are working closely with Indian authorities to ensure safety and security measures are observed, and they extend their gratitude to the Indian authorities and Thiruvananthapuram International Airport for their continued support.

The aircraft couldn't return to HMS Prince of Wales due to adverse weather conditions. Engineers from the vessel assessed the aircraft and determined that support from UK-based engineering teams was necessary.

Shortly after the aircraft's emergency landing, the Indian Air Force offered all necessary support for the "rectification and subsequent return" of the jet. Earlier this month, the HMS Prince of Wales Carrier Strike Group conducted military drills with the Indian Navy.

In British service, the F-35 model, known simply as the 'Lightning,' is the short take-off and vertical landing (STOVL) variant designed for operations from short-field bases and air-capable ships.

items.title: Both engines shut down within secs of take-off: AI crash report
items.story: A preliminary report by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) into the crash of the Boeing Dreamliner 787-8 in Ahmedabad on June 12, which resulted in the deaths of at least 270 people, including 241 of the 242 on board, has been released. One of the key findings confirms that both engines of the plane shut down mid-air within seconds of take-off. According to the AAIB report, the plane reached a maximum speed of 180 knots at 8:08:42 UTC, and immediately the fuel cutoff switches for both engines transitioned from 'run' to 'cutoff'. In the cockpit voice recording, one pilot is heard asking the other why the engines were cut off, to which the other pilot responded that he did not do so. The report also states that both engines of the crashed AI plane have been retrieved, with certain components identified and quarantined for further examination. At this stage of the investigation, there are no recommended actions for Boeing 787-8 and/or GE GEnx-1B engine operators and manufacturers. Fuel samples taken from the bowsers and tanks used to refuel the aircraft were tested at the DGCA's lab and found satisfactory. Additionally, the AFT EAFR was substantially damaged and could not be downloaded through conventional means.

items.title: ‘Please, kisi tarah se bachalo, main lift mein fasa hoon’: A day after Karol Bagh fire, civil services aspirant, lab technician found dead; Vishal Mega Mart lacked fire clearance
items.story: A devastating fire at a Vishal Mega Mart in Delhi's Karol Bagh resulted in the deaths of two individuals: a civil services aspirant and a lab technician. The building lacked a fire safety certificate, prompting a police investigation into potential negligence. One victim sent a desperate message to his brother while trapped in an elevator, pleading for help due to suffocation. The fire was reported at 6.44pm, and despite rescue efforts, the bodies were recovered hours later. The incident has highlighted the lack of fire safety measures in the building.

items.title: Air corridor opens: Russia starts direct flights from Moscow to North Korea's Pyongyang; ties take off with monthly operations confirmed
items.story: Russia has initiated direct commercial flights between Moscow and Pyongyang, marking a significant step in strengthening ties with North Korea. The inaugural Nordwind Airlines flight departed Moscow on Sunday, with plans for monthly service. The first flight took off at 16:25 GMT from Moscow’s Sheremetyevo airport and is expected to reach Pyongyang in about eight hours. Although the number of passengers on board was not disclosed, the ticket price was set at 45,000 rubles, or approximately $570. According to Russia’s deputy transport minister, Vladimir Poteshkin, these flights are the first direct air link between the two capitals in over 70 years of diplomatic relations. The route will initially operate once a month, according to Russia’s transport ministry. The first return flight from Pyongyang to Moscow is scheduled for Tuesday. This development is part of a broader pattern of increasing engagement between the two countries. In addition to aviation links, train services between the countries resumed on June 17, and flights between Pyongyang and Russia’s Vladivostok restarted in 2023. The resumption of direct flights comes amid deepening military cooperation between Moscow and Pyongyang. North Korea has reportedly supplied weapons and troops to support Russia’s operations in Ukraine. Last year, North Korea confirmed it had deployed soldiers to fight alongside Russian forces, and the two nations signed a mutual defense pact. The newly resumed air link signals not only growing military coordination but also a push for broader economic and tourism ties between the heavily sanctioned nations.

items.title: 'Bina Parchi Bina Kharchi: PM Modi distributes over 51,000 appointments letters at 16th Rozghar Mela; launches new scheme for youth
items.story: Prime Minister Narendra Modi distributed over 51,000 appointment letters to newly recruited individuals during an online event for the 16th Rozgar Mela. A significant portion of these letters, over 40,000, are designated for the Ministry of Railways, with others being for health, postal services, and financial institutions. PM Modi highlighted his government's commitment to a merit-based hiring process free from corruption. He emphasized that jobs are now given without recommendations and bribes, under the motto 'Bina Parchi Bina Kharchi'. This initiative aims to employ the youth in various capacities contributing to national development, including national defense, health, financial inclusion, and industrial growth. Additionally, Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Jitendra Singh, mentioned that new recruits would have the option to undertake the 'Mission Karmayogi Prarambh' module to better prepare for their roles. PM Modi also announced a new Employment Linked Incentive scheme aimed at creating private sector jobs by providing Rs 15,000 as a contribution to the first salary of youth securing their first job in the private sector. The scheme is expected to create approximately 3.5 crore jobs with a budget allocation of around Rs 1 lakh crore.

items.title: ‘Boost to India’s defence’: DRDO successfully tests UAV-Launched Precision Missile ULPGM-V3; key features
items.story: India has successfully conducted flight trials of the UAV Launched Precision Guided Missile (ULPGM)-V3 in Andhra Pradesh. The Defence Minister Rajnath Singh applauded the achievement, stressing the readiness of the Indian industry to produce critical defense technologies. The trials took place at the National Open Area Range (NOAR) in Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh, and are considered a significant boost to India's defense capabilities. The ULPGM-V3, an extended-range variant also known as ULM-ER, was showcased at the Aero India 2025 show. This missile features passive homing with an imaging infrared seeker for both day and night operations, has a maximum range of 4 km during the day and 2.5 km at night, and is powered by a small dual-thrust solid propulsion unit. The missile is designed to engage various static and moving targets with multiple warhead options and is supported by a two-way datalink for communication. Adani and Bharat Dynamics Limited are key manufacturing partners, with DRDO leading the development and testing of the munitions. There are three known ULPGM variants: ULPGM V1 (baseline), ULPGM V2 (production variant, also known as ULPGM), and ULPGM V3 (extended-range variant, also referred to as ULM-ER), distinguished by enhancements in guidance systems, performance, and range.

items.title: RSS leader Hosabale calls for moral transformation to heal society and environment
items.story: RSS general secretary Dattatreya Hosabale emphasized the need to tackle both external and internal forms of pollution with equal seriousness. He stated that achieving a meaningful life today requires not only lifestyle changes but also a moral transformation in society. Hosabale made these remarks during a book launch event attended by environment minister Bhupender Yadav. Hosabale acknowledged Yadav's important insights on environmental challenges and agreed with his views. Hosabale highlighted two types of pollution - external, which can be addressed by changing lifestyles, and internal, which includes traits like corruption, arrogance, deceit, and laziness. He stressed that humans must protect themselves from internal pollution for life to be meaningful and successful. Hosabale also noted social divisions as part of the problem, emphasizing the need for mental and behavioral change. Environment minister Bhupender Yadav stressed the importance of balancing human-nature relationships, drawing on India's cultural traditions. He mentioned that the Paris Agreement respects cultural traditions that view the Earth as a mother. Yadav also referred to Mission LiFE, which promotes sustainable development and a balanced lifestyle. He stated that these ideas originate from India's philosophical traditions like 'vasudhaiva kutumbakam' (the world is one family) and 'sarve bhavantu sukhinah' (may all be happy). Yadav concluded that India's civilizational values continue to offer solutions to modern ecological challenges, and global frameworks are beginning to recognize these values.

items.title: Theatre legend Ratan Thiyam passes away at 77: Tributes pour in for the Manipuri maestro
items.story: Ratan Thiyam, one of India's most respected and admired theatre directors and playwrights, passed away at the age of 77. He died in the early hours of Wednesday at the Regional Institute of Medical Sciences in Imphal, after battling a long illness. His demise has created a significant void in Indian theatre, prompting tributes from various sectors. Ratan Thiyam was renowned for his visionary approach to theatre, where he skillfully blended Manipuri tradition with modern storytelling. His work was characterized by the use of folk tales, ancient texts, and real-world issues, making audiences ponder deeply. For his exceptional contributions, he was honored with numerous awards, including the Padma Shri in 1989. Upon his passing, emotional tributes poured in from political leaders, artists, and theatre enthusiasts. Former Manipur Chief Minister N Biren Singh expressed his condolences, highlighting Thiyam's dedication to his craft and his profound love for Manipuri culture. Governor of Manipur Ajay Kumar Bhalla also paid tribute, acknowledging Thiyam's invaluable contributions to Manipuri culture and theatre. Meghalaya Chief Minister Conrad K Sangma praised him for elevating the cultural identity of Manipur through his art. Thiyam's legacy is expected to continue inspiring future generations.

items.title: Urea supply sparks row between agri minister & state BJP chief
items.story: Hyderabad: Agriculture minister Tummala Nageswara Rao and BJP state president N Ramchander Rao were involved in a heated exchange on Sunday over the supply of urea to the state from the Centre. Speaking to the media in Gadwal, Ramchander Rao claimed that middlemen are being encouraged in Telangana to control urea distribution. He said that although the Centre supplied 12.3 lakh metric tonnes of urea, the state is reporting a shortage of 2.5 lakh metric tonnes. Challenging the Congress government to a public debate on the issue, he accused it of mismanaging the supply. In response, Minister Tummala Nageswara Rao countered that the state had actually received only 9.80 lakh metric tonnes of urea. 'How can the BJP state president make such statements without knowing the actual figures? It is unfair to mislead the farmers of the state,' he said. The minister also stated that several letters had been sent to the Centre requesting the required quantity of urea and urged the BJP not to politicise the issue. Ramchander Rao, in turn, alleged that the Revanth Reddy-led government was attempting to deflect attention from its own failures and inefficiencies by blaming the Centre, particularly with the local body elections approaching.

items.title: Headmaster held for sexual assault
items.story: In Tamil Nadu's Tirupattur district, a 56-year-old government school headmaster named K Bharath Ambedkar has been suspended and arrested on charges of sexually assaulting a class 5 student. This incident occurred shortly after his previous suspension for similar charges was revoked. According to police reports, Ambedkar arrived at the school in an inebriated state and proceeded to assault the girl by asking her to sit on his lap. Villagers visiting the school filmed the incident and filed a complaint with the district education office, leading to his suspension again by the district education officer. The case has brought significant attention due to the severity and repetition of the allegations against Ambedkar.

items.title: 'Bail rule, jail exception' principle forgotten in recent past, says CJI Gavai
items.story: Chief Justice of India B R Gavai expressed concern over the forgotten principle of "bail is the rule, jail is the exception," despite judicial integration. He highlighted his efforts in 2024 to reestablish this principle while granting bail in cases like Prabir Purkayastha, Manish Sisodia, and Kavita vs ED. Delivering the Justice V R Krishna Iyer Memorial Law Lecture in Kochi, the CJI said that although judicial pronouncements over the decades have integrated this norm, it has not been implemented in true spirit in recent years. Justice Gavai mentioned his happiness in having the opportunity to reiterate this legal principle in various cases in the previous year, 2024. He praised Justice Iyer's immense contribution in protecting the rights of marginalized communities. The Supreme Court (SC) in recent years passed a series of orders to protect the rights of undertrial prisoners and held that delay in trial and long incarceration were grounds to grant bail even in serious offenses under laws like the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). The CJI recalled Justice Iyer’s strong opposition to keeping undertrials in jail for long periods without trial. In an important ruling in August last year, the SC had held that the conventional idea of "bail is the rule, jail is an exception" should be applicable not only to offenses under the Indian Penal Code (IPC) but also to other offenses for which special statutes have been enacted, such as UAPA, if the conditions prescribed under that law are fulfilled. The SC had appealed to high courts and lower courts to be liberal in granting bail and not to hesitate in granting the relief in serious offenses if a case is made out for bail.

items.title: Vanished after one last call: What happened to Sneha Debnath? 19-year-old Tripura girl goes missing in Delhi; last seen near Signature Bridge
items.story:
NEW DELHI: Sneha Debnath, a 19-year-old student from Sabroom in South Tripura, has gone missing in New Delhi under mysterious circumstances, prompting swift intervention from the Tripura chief minister's office and a multi-agency search operation led by Delhi Police and the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), ANI reported.

Final call at 5:56 am, plan to meet friend falls through
Sneha, a student at Delhi University's Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, last contacted her family on July 7. She reportedly told her mother that she was going to accompany her friend Pitunia to Sarai Rohilla Railway Station. Her final phone call was made at 5:56 am that day. By 8:45 am, her phone had been switched off. The friend, Pitunia, later confirmed she had not met Sneha that morning as planned.

Cab driver reveals drop near Signature Bridge, no CCTV footage
In a disturbing revelation, a cab driver traced by the family stated he had dropped Sneha near Delhi's Signature Bridge, a location known for safety issues and limited CCTV surveillance, as per the report. The lack of footage has significantly hindered efforts to trace her movements.

Tripura CM's office calls for immediate action
The Tripura chief minister's office acknowledged the case in an official statement and said CM Manik Saha had directed police to take immediate and appropriate action. "The report of Miss Sneha Debnath, a resident of Sabroom, who has reportedly gone missing in New Delhi, has come to the notice of the chief minister's office," the statement read.

NDRF joins search, but no leads so far
On July 9, Delhi Police, assisted by the NDRF, launched a search within a 7-kilometre radius around Signature Bridge, but no concrete clues have emerged so far.

No bank activity, no belongings taken
The family, deeply distressed, noted that Sneha left without any belongings and hadn't withdrawn money in the last four months. Her bank account remains untouched.

Authorities have issued a public appeal for any information regarding Sneha's whereabouts. The investigation remains ongoing.

items.title: 8-year-old dies after pack of stray dogs attack in Hyderabad's Neredmet; locals raise alarm over repeated attacks, demand action
items.story: In a tragic incident, an eight-year-old boy named Prasad Jadhav died after being attacked by stray dogs in the Keshawanagar area of Neredmet, Hyderabad. The young boy, a Class 3 student, was playing near his home when a pack of dogs attacked him, causing severe injuries. Despite being rushed to Gandhi Hospital for treatment, Prasad succumbed to his injuries shortly after. According to a complaint filed by Prasad's father, Premdas Jadhav, the boy was bitten on his left thigh. The Neredmet police have launched an investigation and registered a case regarding the incident. Relatives of the boy expressed concerns over frequent attacks by stray dogs in the neighborhood, mentioning a similar incident that occurred months earlier involving a four-year-old boy who was attacked by stray dogs in the nearby area of Rajendranagar. The community is alarmed by these repeated incidents and is demanding action to address the issue of stray dog attacks.

items.title: Golfer Simon Mariani unexpectedly dies at 28 after lightning strike hits New Jersey golf course
items.story: Tragedy struck New Jersey's Ballyowen Golf Club when 28-year-old golfer Simon Mariani was fatally injured by a lightning strike during a sudden storm. The incident occurred on July 8, 2025. Mariani, a resident of Franklin Lakes and an associate at MTS Health Partners, passed away on July 14, 2025, after battling for his life for six days. He was remembered for his talent and character, and his funeral was scheduled for July 18 in Franklin Lakes. Mariani was well-regarded for his intelligence and dedication, having earned a degree in accounting and economics from the University of Notre Dame in 2019, and later an MBA in 2024. He was described in his obituary as driven, dedicated, and exceptionally talented, with a love for family, sports, and the outdoors. His untimely death has left his family, friends, and the community mourning his loss with sadness and love. Crystal Springs Resort, which operates the Ballyowen course, expressed their condolences, emphasizing guest safety as a top priority.

items.title: Government seeks views on including PDS food grains in CPI series
items.story:
NEW DELHI: Statistics ministry Saturday floated a discussion paper and invited views from experts, academicians, government bodies, states, financial institutions and other stakeholders on treatment of items distributed free of cost through PDS in the consumer price index compilation framework.

The ministry is currently undertaking a revision of the CPI with the objective of updating item weights, revising the consumption basket and incorporating methodological improvements to strengthen the index. At present, the CPI is compiled every month on the basis of price data collection from 1,181 rural markets and 1,114 urban centres across the country.

With the release of household consumption expenditure survey 2023-24, the ministry has also kicked off the exercise to revise the CPI base year from 2012 to 2024.

Including items distributed through the PDS in the retail inflation basket is a crucial issue as it could have a bearing on the actual headline inflation outcome.

In the existing CPI series, items that are distributed free of cost do not carry any expenditure share, since households incur zero out-of-pocket spending on them. This is consistent with international practice, according to the discussion paper which asked stakeholders to send in their comments by Oct 22.

The paper states CPI serves a dual purpose in India. It is not only the principal indicator for monetary policy formulation by RBI, but also widely used as a proxy for tracking changes in cost of living and for indexation of wages, pensions and formulation of social welfare schemes.

items.title: India to get normal rainfall in August; above normal in September, predicts IMD
items.story: India is expected to experience above-normal rainfall during the latter half of the monsoon season, specifically in August and September, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD). In an online press briefing, IMD director general Mrutyunjay Mohapatra stated that most regions, except the Northeast and adjoining eastern parts of the country, are likely to receive normal rainfall in August, while September is projected to have above-normal rainfall. India has already received above-average rainfall in the first half of the season (June-July), with some states like Himachal Pradesh experiencing flash floods. Overall, above-normal rainfall (106 percent of the long period average of 422.8 mm) is most likely over the country during the second half of the southwest monsoon season, Mohapatra said. He added that rainfall will be normal to above normal across most regions, except parts of Northeast, eastern India, central India, and southwestern peninsular India, where a shortfall is likely. Although rainfall activity may remain subdued over the next two weeks, it does not meet the criteria for a 'break monsoon phase', the IMD clarified. A break phase refers to a temporary monsoon pause when the rain-bearing trough shifts closer to the Himalayan foothills. Between June 1 and July 31, the country recorded 474.3 mm of rainfall against a normal of 445.8 mm, marking a 6% surplus. There were 624 very heavy rainfall events and 76 extremely heavy rainfall events, the lowest in five years, Mohapatra noted. He also highlighted that Northeast India has seen below-normal rainfall for the fifth consecutive year, in line with a 30-year declining trend in monsoon activity in the region. The strong July rains were attributed to favorable Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO) conditions and six low-pressure systems, of which four intensified into depressions. Among them, three formed over land and moved from Gangetic West Bengal/Northern Bay of Bengal to Rajasthan, triggering frequent heavy to very heavy rainfall and even extremely heavy rainfall on some days, said the IMD. The IMD also reported that ENSO-neutral conditions are currently prevailing and likely to continue through October, with a possibility of weak La Niña conditions post-monsoon. In May, the weather office had predicted monsoon rainfall at 106% of the long-period average of 87 cm for the June-September period. Rainfall between 96% and 104% is considered normal. The monsoon is crucial for India’s economy, particularly the agriculture sector, which sustains nearly 42% of the population and contributes over 18% to the GDP. It also plays a key role in replenishing water reservoirs essential for drinking water and power generation.

items.title: Just backing Pakistan without mention of India does not threaten sovereignty: Allahabad HC
items.story:
The Allahabad High Court has observed that merely expressing support for Pakistan without referencing any specific incident or mentioning India does not prima facie constitute an offense under Section 152 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with acts endangering the sovereignty or unity and integrity of India. The court made this observation while granting bail to Riyaz, who was accused of pledging support to Pakistan in an Instagram post. Justice Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal stated that the records show that the applicant did not mention anything that shows disrespect towards India. 

The court noted that merely posting a message to show support for any country might create anger or disharmony among Indian citizens, which could be punishable under Section 196 of the BNS, which deals with promoting enmity between different groups on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, etc. However, this does not attract Section 152, which requires there to be intent to promote secession, armed rebellion, or subversive activities that endanger India's sovereignty, unity, and integrity. 

Justice Deshwal emphasized the need for 'reasonable care' when invoking Section 152, highlighting that it is a new provision with stringent punishments, including life imprisonment, which had no equivalent in the Indian Penal Code (IPC). The court also stated that social media posts fall under the right to freedom of speech and expression and should not be narrowly interpreted unless they threaten the country's sovereignty and integrity or encourage separatism. 

During the hearing, the applicant's counsel argued that the social media post did not lower India's dignity and sovereignty, noting that the post did not mention India, nor did it include any disrespectful imagery towards the country. The state opposed the bail plea, arguing that such posts encourage separatism. However, the high court granted bail and directed the applicant not to post any material on social media that could create disharmony among people.

items.title: 'Trump coiled around Modi like a snake': Congress renews attack over US President's ceasefire claims; Pawan Khera says PM 'allergic to Rahul's advice'
items.story:
Congress leader Pawan Khera criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi, referencing former US President Donald Trump's claims of mediating a ceasefire between India and Pakistan following the Pahalgam attack. Khera's comments came after Rahul Gandhi challenged Modi to refute Trump's statements in Parliament. In response, Modi asserted that no foreign leader asked India to halt Operation Sindoor, directly contradicting Trump's assertions.

During a recent discussion, Khera remarked, "Trump is coiled around Modi like a snake. Rahul Gandhi gave him the perfect chance to deny Trump's claims by simply stating they were untrue, but Modi seemed reluctant to take Rahul's advice."

Trump's comments also touched on the ongoing trade deal negotiations between the US and India, mentioning high tariffs imposed by India. He stated, "India is a friend, but they impose high tariffs. The deal isn't finalized yet."

In Parliament, Modi firmly countered Trump's narrative, stating that no world leader requested a suspension of Operation Sindoor, responding to the opposition's demand for him to challenge Trump's remarks publicly.

items.title: Red Panda injured in dramatic fall during halftime at Indiana Fever vs Minnesota Lynx Commissioner's Cup
items.story: A dramatic incident occurred during the WNBA Commissioner's Cup final between the Indiana Fever and the Minnesota Lynx at Minnesota's Target Center. Renowned halftime performer Red Panda, famous for her unicycle and bowl-balancing act, suffered a fall shortly after the start of her performance. Medical staff attended to her on the court, and she was seen clutching her wrist. The arena fell silent as concerns about her condition grew. Red Panda, whose real name is Rong "Krystal" Niu, fell from her seven-foot unicycle, a signature element of her act, just moments after releasing the ladder she uses to mount it. She was eventually taken away by ambulance for further evaluation. The 50-year-old performer has been a staple in basketball arenas since 1993, known for her impressive feats during NBA, WNBA, and college basketball games, as well as her appearances on talent shows like Britain's Got Talent and America's Got Talent. She returned to performing in 2015 after a brief hiatus following her father's cancer battle. The sports community has shown an outpouring of support for her recovery, hoping for her swift and complete return to health.

items.title: IND vs ENG: 'Jasprit Bumrah is available but ...,' says Team India assistant coach Ryan ten Doeschate ahead of 2nd Test
items.story:
Following a defeat at Headingley, India is considering whether to field Jasprit Bumrah for the second Test, despite workload management plans limiting his appearances. Assistant coach Ryan ten Doeschate confirms Bumrah's availability, but the decision hinges on long-term strategy. Nitish Kumar Reddy might debut, offering balance if Bumrah rests, highlighting India's focus on sustained success. 

India trails 0-1 in the Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy following a disappointing loss at Headingley. The premier fast bowler Bumrah is available for selection ahead of the second Test, but whether he takes the field remains uncertain. Assistant coach Ryan ten Doeschate stated, "Jasprit Bumrah is available but we haven't made a call yet whether he will play this game or not." 

Meanwhile, Nitish Kumar Reddy could be in line for his debut. The young batting all-rounder has impressed in training and is "very close to getting a game," according to ten Doeschate. His inclusion could provide balance to the side, especially if Bumrah is rested.

The uncertainty around Bumrah isn’t a question of fitness but one of long-term planning. Head coach Gautam Gambhir had earlier confirmed that Bumrah would feature in only three of the five Tests in the series as part of a pre-decided workload management plan.

"The scoreline doesn’t change that," Gambhir had asserted after defeat in the first Test, underlining the importance of keeping Bumrah fresh for future fixtures. India’s bowling attack lacked bite in Leeds, and with the series heating up, there is growing pressure to field the strongest XI. Yet, team management seems firm on playing the long game, prioritizing Bumrah’s durability over short-term gains.

As the second Test looms, India faces a crucial decision — go all-in with Bumrah to level the series, or stick to the plan and back their depth. Either way, the management’s commitment to strategic rotation signals a shift in India’s approach: eyes not just on this series, but on sustaining success across formats.

items.title: Drug cartel led by Nigerian kingpin busted in Delhi: Rs 100 crore cocaine, MDMA seized; used women as carriers, ran WhatsApp call centre, app-style delivery network
items.story:
Delhi Police have dismantled a major drug trafficking operation in Delhi-NCR, seizing cocaine, MDMA, and OG ganja valued at over Rs 100 crore. Five foreign nationals, including the head of operations in India and distributors, were arrested. The syndicate was orchestrated by Nigerian kingpin Callistus and utilized encrypted WhatsApp channels, forged documents, and foreign nationals based in India for drug deliveries. According to Special Commissioner (crime) Devesh Shrivastava, the syndicate operated a call center model via WhatsApp, facilitating app-style deliveries using live tracking by foot soldiers. 

The police confiscated a sedan, Rs 2 lakh in cash, mobile phones, passports, 2,700 grams of Colombian cocaine, 1,000 grams of MDMA, and over 1 kg of OG ganja. The operation launched with a raid at a courier facility in Moti Nagar, west Delhi, where 895 grams of MDMA concealed in packaging was intercepted. This led to the apprehension of Cameroonian national Kameni Philipp, the India operations head. The cartel's structure, linked directly to Callistus in West Africa, was exposed. 

The investigation led to the arrest of three Nigerian nationals, Godwin John, Kelechi Chikwe, and Ibe Chinedu Austin, as well as Koulaie Philippe from Cote d'Ivoire. The syndicate smuggled pure cocaine into India using female Indian carriers, exploiting their lower risk at borders. Once in India, Philipp received the consignment, passing it to distributors like Godwin John, who adulterated the cocaine for street sales. The product was distributed to lower-level operatives for final delivery, with payments collected and funneled up the chain.

A major money laundering operation was also uncovered. Drug proceeds were laundered through an informal currency exchange network, with Indians in Nigeria paying in Naira to the syndicate, while their relatives in India received the equivalent in Rupees, bypassing formal banking channels.

items.title: BJP-Sena turf war escalates: MoS Misal, minister Shirsat clash over authority; Fadnavis steps in
items.story: Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis intervened in a growing dispute between Social Justice Minister Sanjay Shirsat of the Shiv Sena and Minister of State Madhuri Misal of the BJP, urging both leaders to resolve their differences internally. Fadnavis, addressing reporters in Nagpur, emphasized that ministers should communicate directly with each other to resolve issues. The conflict began when Shirsat objected to Misal convening a meeting with department officials without his prior approval, alleging she had no authority to do so. Misal, however, asserted she was within her rights and clarified that she had not issued directives during the meeting. Fadnavis explained that while ministers hold all the powers, any powers delegated to ministers of state are theirs to exercise. He added that ministers of state could hold meetings but any policy decisions needed ratification by the minister. The dispute escalated as Misal sought clarification on her powers from the chief minister’s office, while Shirsat insisted on all departmental meetings being convened with his permission. Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule mentioned that the chief minister would address the broader issue of power-sharing between cabinet ministers and their junior counterparts. Fadnavis’s call for coordination aims to prevent further strain within the coalition government.

items.title: From filters to fillers: Gen Z’s glitzy quest for ‘eternal youth’
items.story: In Hyderabad, young adults in their twenties are increasingly seeking cosmetic procedures such as fillers, boosters, and futuristic therapies with little concern for long-term consequences. The focus is not on aging gracefully but on preventing age from appearing altogether. Ajay Tomar reports that weeks before her wedding, a bride-to-be named Latha visited a clinic in Banjara Hills to enhance her appearance. She underwent several non-surgical aesthetic treatments, such as dermal fillers to correct lip asymmetry, enhance her nose bridge, and sharpen her jawline for a slimmer profile. She also had fillers injected into her cheekbones to add contour. Similarly, Seetha, in her early thirties, went to a clinic in Madhapur to fix what she felt was sagging skin. She opted for high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) and botox injections to achieve a youthful appearance. This trend is not limited to those experiencing midlife crises; many are in their twenties and early thirties.Young people are increasingly unhappy with their looks and are turning to quick anti-aging procedures. Cosmetic and dermatology clinics report a rise in young clients seeking minimally invasive and non-invasive treatments to delay signs of aging. About a decade ago, most clients were in their 40s, but now many in their mid-20s and early 30s are seeking these treatments. Senior plastic surgeon Dr. Priti Shukla notes that a lot of damage is already done by the time signs of aging appear on the skin.Besides smaller procedures, some are opting for advanced treatments like platelet-rich plasma (PRP) therapy, HIFU, hybrid laser treatments, and regenerative procedures such as exosome therapy using stem cells to improve collagen production, PDRN (polydeoxyribonucleotide) therapy, and nano-fat grafting. Data supports this trend, with the US-based market research firm Grand View Research estimating the Indian anti-aging market to reach $2.5 billion in 2024, projected to grow to $4 billion by 2033.The drive for such procedures is fueled by social media and peer pressure, where the perfect selfie and number of likes influence many young people's happiness quotient. The demand surge has also led to more affordable treatments, varying from Rs 5,000 to Rs 40,000 per session. Dr. Sumeera Farhath SK, a plastic surgeon, explains that increased social media presence and the culture of sharing photos and videos prompt individuals to observe their skin more closely. The popularity of South Korean television shows, which emphasize skincare, also influences Indian youth's interest in cosmetics and skincare. South Korea is a global leader in cosmetic treatments and plastic surgery. Senior psychologist Dr. Pragya Rashmi suggests that starting cosmetic enhancements at a young age may indicate low self-esteem and body image issues. Consultant psychiatrist and lifestyle expert Dr. Purnima Nagaraja highlights that many opt for cosmetic enhancements due to a distorted sense of body image, driven by societal expectations of a perfect body, flawless hair, and ideal shape.

items.title: Show us you can use: Amazon sets new requirement for employee promotions in these departments
items.story: Amazon employees at Ring, Blink security cameras, Key in-home delivery service, and Sidewalk wireless network must demonstrate artificial intelligence usage to secure promotions. This new mandate was announced by Ring founder Jamie Siminoff, who returned to lead the company in April. Siminoff stated that all promotion applications must explain how employees are using AI at work. The policy aims to reward "innovative thinking" and reinforce a culture of speed and efficiency. Employees must describe how they've used generative AI or other AI technologies to improve customer experience or increase operational efficiency, citing specific AI projects and measurable impact achieved. Management positions have additional requirements, needing to show how they used AI tools to accomplish "more with less" while reducing or maintaining headcount levels. This reflects Amazon CEO Andy Jassy's broader emphasis on productivity and cost-efficiency. Siminoff has implemented sweeping changes at Ring, including an "AI first" vision, and has pushed employees to use AI daily. This initiative aligns with other tech companies that are incorporating AI use into talent evaluation.

items.title: Skyroot Aerospace, Axiom Space team up to advance space exploration
items.story: Skyroot Aerospace, a company based in Hyderabad, India, and Axiom Space, a US firm, have signed a memorandum of understanding to collaborate on enhancing space exploration, particularly focusing on improving access to low Earth orbit (LEO). The collaboration was announced on the day Axiom-4 mission was launched, carrying Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla and three other astronauts to space. The partnership aims to utilize Skyroot's capabilities to send research payloads, establish orbital data center nodes, and conduct other future missions to the Axiom Station, which is currently under construction, and independently to LEO. Skyroot Aerospace, known for being the first private South Asian company to successfully launch a rocket into space using the Vikram-S sub-orbital launch vehicle in November 2022, is preparing to launch its first orbital rocket, the Vikram-1, later this year. The Axiom Space mission Ax-4 is India's second attempt at human spaceflight and its first mission on the International Space Station (ISS). The mission is seen as foundational for the construction and operation of the Axiom Station as the company seeks to develop a diverse global supply chain through partnerships like the one with Skyroot Aerospace. Pawan Kumar Chandana, co-founder and CEO of Skyroot Aerospace, emphasized the importance of enabling greater and equitable access to space for research institutes, startups, and national agencies. Tejpaul Bhatia, CEO of Axiom Space, expressed enthusiasm for the partnership, citing a shared vision to transform access to space and serve the growing global space ecosystem.

items.title: IND vs ENG: 'Earlier Kuldeep Yadav was kept out because of Ashwin' - Mohammad Kaif warns Team India ahead of 2nd Test
items.story: As India prepares for the second Test against England at Edgbaston, the focus has shifted sharply to team selection, particularly regarding the exclusion of Kuldeep Yadav. Former cricketer Mohammad Kaif has stirred the debate by calling out what he perceives as an ongoing oversight of the wrist-spinner. Kaif posted on X, expressing that "It will be unfair if Kuldeep Yadav doesn't get into the playing XI for the second Test. He has just played 13 Tests in 8 years. Earlier he was kept out because of Ashwin — now how do you justify his exclusion?" Kaif's remarks have added weight to an already tough decision for the team management. Following a disappointing loss in Leeds, India’s strategy of prioritizing batting depth over attacking bowling options is under scrutiny. With Jasprit Bumrah potentially sitting out due to workload management, India will be under pressure to find bowlers who can take 20 wickets, a challenge that proved too great in the series opener. The pitch at Edgbaston promises to offer help to spinners later in the match. While Ravindra Jadeja is a certainty, India must now decide whether to go with the more batting-friendly option in Washington Sundar or finally unleash Kuldeep, whose variations could trouble England’s aggressive lineup. Meanwhile, the team is also looking to tweak its all-rounder and pace combinations. Shardul Thakur might make way for Nitish Reddy, and Akash Deep could partner Mohammed Siraj in Bumrah’s absence. With England sharpening their "Bazball" approach, India must respond with courage — and picking Kuldeep Yadav could be that bold, match-turning move.

items.title: Deadliest Pharma Disaster in India: Sigachi Factory Blast Claims Lives
items.story: A devastating explosion at Sigachi Industries in Sangareddy has become the deadliest disaster in India's pharmaceutical sector history, claiming over 35 lives. The incident has exposed critical safety lapses, including poor maintenance, unqualified staff, and absent safety protocols, prompting renewed calls for stricter enforcement and relocation of hazardous units. The blast not only destroyed the factory but also caused damage to neighboring factories. Previously, the worst incident was the Escientia Bio Pharma Ltd factory explosion in Anakapalli, Andhra Pradesh, which killed 17 people in August 2024. Furthermore, there were other incidents such as the 2023 blast at Sahiti Pharma in Atchutapuram, Andhra Pradesh, which resulted in seven deaths, and a 2022 explosion at Laurus Labs' facility in Visakhapatnam, which killed four employees. Rescue efforts by fire services, SDRF, and NDRF have so far failed to locate any missing persons, with the possibility that unidentified bodies may belong to those missing. The operation, described as one of the most challenging, involves careful removal of debris, hindered by hazardous substances that caused continuous metallic flames. Criticism has arisen from relatives of the missing workers, who claim that the rescue efforts are insufficient due to inadequate equipment and personnel. Identifying the bodies has proven difficult, with 14 bodies identified and others pending DNA profiling. The incident has raised serious concerns about safety and regulation in the Indian pharmaceutical industry.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo signs massive $700 million deal with Al Nassr packed with perks no athlete has seen before
items.story: Cristiano Ronaldo, one of the most recognized footballers in the world, has signed a groundbreaking contract with the Saudi Arabian professional football club Al Nassr. The contract, valued at $700 million, is considered the largest in sports history. In addition to the substantial financial package, Ronaldo's deal includes numerous perks such as private jets, a 16-member personal staff, and a 15% ownership stake in the club. He also receives a $33.6 million signing bonus, $5.5 million for scoring the most goals in the Saudi Pro League, and around $82.4 million in sponsorship deals with Saudi brands. Notably, Saudi Arabia does not charge income tax, allowing Ronaldo to retain more of his earnings compared to Europe. Victor Matheson, a sports economist, noted that Ronaldo is likely earning as much as the entire league's revenue. Other athletes like Lionel Messi and David Beckham have also received lucrative extras in their contracts, such as Messi's deals with Apple TV and Adidas, and Beckham's rights to buy an MLS team, which he later did, becoming the owner of Inter Miami. Ronaldo's contract sets a new standard in sports salaries, highlighting the growing financial influence of Saudi sports investments.

items.title: 'Chor ko darr lagta hai... We are innocent. We are not scared'
items.story: Following their acquittal in the 11/7 Mumbai train bombings case by the Bombay High Court, the accused express optimism about a favorable outcome in the Supreme Court. Despite past hardships, including family losses during their 19-year incarceration, they maintain their innocence and trust in the judiciary. They are determined to fight the case legally, confident that the truth will prevail and they will ultimately be vindicated. Most of the accused in the 11/7 Mumbai train bombings acquitted by the Bombay high court said that they were hopeful that they would be acquitted by Supreme Court as well. A relative of Naved Hussain, who was given the death sentence by a trial court and was acquitted by the high court, said it was a process of law. "We would have been disappointed if the apex court had asked the men to return to jail. That is not the case. We will fight this case legally in Supreme Court and are sure to win it there too," said the relative. Dr Tanvir Ansari, who was termed a conspirator in the case and was acquitted, said, "Chor ko darr lagta hai (A thief feels scared). We are innocent. We are not scared. The high court judgment has covered all the angles. We will see it legally." Ansari had lost his mother while in jail. Shareeful Rehman, elder brother of acquitted accused Zameer Shaikh, said that there was uncertainty till SC issued an order Thursday. "Now we are relaxed. We are hopeful that we will win our case in Supreme Court," said Rehman. Shaikh had lost both his parents during his time in prison. During the last 19 years that the 12 accused were in jail, either the mother or father or both of a majority of them passed away. The wife of Majid Shafi Shaikh died due to medical complications while he was incarcerated. Sohail Shaikh said, "This stay is not the victory of lies of the ATS. This is a procedure. The ATS should not think it has won. The lies have been going on for the last 19 years." Another acquitted accused said the trial court ignored the torture they had suffered and the fake confessions prepared by the police. He said the high court looked into all aspects, examined all angles, and acquitted them. Sajid Ansari, another acquitted accused, said he had faith in Allah and the judiciary. "The lawyers and Jamiat-ul-Ulema are fighting our case. We are sure of winning it at SC," Sajid said. While in prison, he completed seven certificate courses including those on human rights, Arabic language, tourism studies, AIDS and family education, teaching of English, and BA, MA in political science; he has also completed two years of LLB. His mother and two sisters passed away while he was in jail. Another acquitted accused, Muzammil Shaikh, who worked as a database administrator in Bengaluru, said that he lost both parents during his time in jail.

items.title: Bihar polls: Prashant Kishor accuses PM Modi of ignoring key issues; says 'spoke about four things, and left'
