The minister said that 51 commanders (P1) and 61 first officers (P2) called in sick on a single day after the deadly crash, news agency PTI reported.

The June 12 crash involved a Boeing 787-8 aircraft bound for London Gatwick. It plummeted into a building shortly after takeoff from Ahmedabad, killing 241 passengers, 19 people on the ground, and leaving just one survivor. The catastrophe is one of India’s deadliest civil aviation accidents in recent history.

In light of the tragedy, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has reiterated its 2023 circular advising airlines to implement customised mental health training for crew and to ensure access to Peer Support Programmes (PSP) - confidential, non-punitive systems designed to help flight crew cope with stress, anxiety, and trauma.

In a separate written reply, the minister clarified that no specific compensation policy currently exists for civilian victims on the ground in plane crashes.

Meanwhile, India on Wednesday virtually trashed a British media report, which claimed that two grieving families in the United Kingdom received wrong bodies of the victims of the Air India plane crash in Ahmedabad. The ministry of external affairs said all mortal remains were handled with utmost professionalism and with due regard for the dignity of the deceased.

"We have seen the report and have been working closely with the UK side from the moment these concerns and issues were brought to our attention," MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.

"In the wake of the tragic crash, the concerned authorities had carried out identification of victims as per established protocols and technical requirements," he added.

Jaiswal was responding to media queries regarding a report in the "Daily Mail" on the Air India crash. "All mortal remains were handled with utmost professionalism and with due regard for the dignity of the deceased. We are continuing to work with the UK authorities on addressing any concerns related to this issue," he said.

items.title: SC questions ED role, upholds HC order clearing Siddaramaiah's wife
items.story: The Supreme Court of India questioned the role of the Enforcement Directorate (ED) in politically sensitive cases while upholding the Karnataka High Court's decision to dismiss the case against Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah's wife, B M Parvathi, under the anti-money laundering law. The court cautioned against using the ED as a tool in political battles, emphasizing that political issues should be resolved electorally. The bench, consisting of Chief Justice B R Gavai and Justice K V Chandran, remarked, "Let political battles be fought before the electorate. Why are you being used?" This comment was made during the hearing of the ED's appeal against the HC order that quashed proceedings against Parvathi concerning alleged irregularities in the allotment of compensatory sites in Mysuru. The Chief Justice warned the additional solicitor general who attempted to justify the ED's actions, indicating that continuing the argument might lead to harsh comments from the bench. The Supreme Court dismissed the ED's petition, agreeing with the HC's judgment, which had previously set aside ED's summons to Parvathi and urban development minister B S Suresh. The HC's decision followed petitions challenging the ED's actions, which were stayed by the court earlier this year. Siddaramaiah also faced allegations related to illegal allotments of sites to his wife by the Mysuru Urban Development Authority, with several individuals, including the Chief Minister's family, being named in a FIR registered by the Lokayukta Police following a special court directive.

items.title: India bans specific jute, textile items from Bangladesh: Imports permitted only through Nhava Sheva seaport - new trade restrictions explained
items.story: India has banned the import of specific jute products and woven fabrics from Bangladesh via land routes, restricting entry solely through the Nhava Sheva seaport, according to a Directorate General of Foreign Trade notification. On Friday, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade issued a notification stating that these imports would only be permitted through the Nhava Sheva seaport. Previously, on May 17, India had restricted port access for various Bangladeshi imports, including readymade garments and processed food items. The restricted items comprise jute products, single flax yarn, single yarn of jute, multiple folded, woven fabrics or flex, and unbleached woven fabrics of jute. This decision comes in response to growing tensions with Bangladesh's interim administration led by Muhammad Yunus. Earlier, India had implemented import restrictions on various products from Bangladesh, including a ban on readymade garments through land routes. The move allows garments to be imported only through Nhava Sheva and Kolkata ports, impacting a significant portion of Bangladesh's $700 million garment exports to India. The Directorate General of Foreign Trade's notification exempts fish, edible oil, LPG, and crushed stones from the restrictions. However, imports of several products through land customs stations and integrated check posts in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram, and West Bengal's Changrabandha and Fulbari will be discontinued. The action comes as retaliation to Bangladesh's recent restrictions on Indian yarn and rice imports. India had previously disallowed the transit of Bangladesh garments meant for third-market exports, as these goods were taking up freight space at the expense of Indian products. The timing of these restrictions coincides with Yunus' recent proposal for a comprehensive economic plan involving Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, and India's northeastern states.

items.title: Death toll rises to 45 in Sigachi Industries explosion in Hyderabad
items.story: Hyderabad: The death toll in the explosion at the chemical factory of Sigachi Industries climbed to 45 on Monday morning as one more victim, who was undergoing treatment at a private hospital, died of cardiac arrest. The deceased was identified as 45-year-old Tarak from West Bengal, who suffered over 75% burn injuries in the June 30 explosion that ripped through the dryer unit of the firm located in Pashamylaram of Sangareddy district. Arrangements were made by district authorities to send the deceased's body to his native place. Currently, four more patients are undergoing treatment at the same hospital, with one of them, Rajesh Kumar Chowdary (42) from Bihar, being on a non-invasive ventilator (HIV). The condition of the other three is stable, according to doctors. Meanwhile, another two victims, Videshi Kahar (48) and Ganga Mukhiya (38), both of whom suffered from 40% burns, were declared stable and were discharged from another private hospital in Patancheru on Monday. Eight people are still untraced from the incident.

items.title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's adorable son Ares steals the spotlight during NBA finals family portrait session
items.story: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, a prominent player for the Oklahoma City Thunder, had a remarkable 2025 NBA season, not only excelling on the court but also balancing his role as a dedicated father. During the NBA Finals family portrait session, his son, Ares Alexander, captured the attention of fans and the internet. Shai is married to Hailey Summers, a former college soccer player, and they welcomed their son Ares in April 2024. During the portrait session, Ares charmed everyone by stealing the spotlight, a moment shared widely online. A video from the NBA's official Instagram showed Ares joyfully participating in the portrait session with the championship trophies. In May 2025, Shai celebrated a victory in the Western Conference finals against the Minnesota Timberwolves by sharing a special moment on the court with his wife and son. Videos showed Ares trying to dribble a basketball, bringing smiles to spectators. The Oklahoma City Thunder won the game 114-88, with Shai leading the team and earning the MVP title in the finals.

items.title: IND vs ENG Test: Ex-India cricketer questions Gautam Gambhir's tactics – 'Take a chill pill'
items.story: Sanjay Manjrekar has criticized Gautam Gambhir's coaching during the Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy, citing "poor tactics" and "questionable selections." Manjrekar disputes Gambhir's claim that Karun Nair wasn't dropped, emphasizing India's past losses under Gambhir's leadership. He attributes the team's fighting spirit to the players, not tactical decisions. On Sunday, after India pulled off a heist at Old Trafford, Gautam Gambhir said that Karun Nair was not dropped and that the team was picked based on the right combination. Gambhir's blunt statement didn’t sit well with Manjrekar. "And to suggest that Karun Nair ‘wasn’t dropped’… come on. You guys see it as a drop; for them, it’s about ‘picking the right team.’ If someone is dropped, he is dropped," Manjrekar said on JioHotstar. “I feel India has done well despite some of his (Gambhir’s) tactical decisions. Let’s not forget: India lost 3-0 at home to New Zealand and lost comfortably to Australia away. The fight we’ve seen in this team? That’s down to the players. Because tactically, Gambhir hasn’t always made things easier — especially with some of his selections," he added. Manjrekar also urged Gambhir to relax a bit, saying he always appears to be in a combative mood. "It’s not about ‘you guys think’ and ‘we think’ – we’re all part of the same industry and the same country. I’d just like to see him take a chill pill, relax a bit, and be open to tough questions. Whether that will happen, I’m not sure," said Manjrekar. The fourth Test ended in a stalemate after centuries from skipper Shubman Gill, Ravindra Jadeja, and Washington Sundar saw India dominate the final day’s play at Old Trafford. The fifth and final Test will begin on July 31 at The Oval.

items.title: Wimbledon: Novak Djokovic’s daughter steals spotlight with adorable dance after win | Watch
items.story:
Novak Djokovic celebrated his 100th Wimbledon singles win on Centre Court, but his daughter, Tara, stole the show. During an on-court interview, Djokovic explained a dance he's been doing is to the song "Pump It Up." He then encouraged Tara to demonstrate, and she happily obliged, pumping her fists to the delight of the crowd. 

After his straight-sets victory over compatriot Miomir Kecmanovic on Centre Court, Djokovic was asked about his now-familiar "Pump It Up" celebration. With a wide smile, the Serbian legend looked up into the crowd and said, "There's a song with my kids - look, my daughter's doing it right now. You want to show it darling?" The cameras then panned to Tara in the players’ box, joyfully demonstrating the dance. Her moves - pumping her fists downward, then to the sides, and finally overhead - instantly won over the Wimbledon crowd, which erupted in warm applause.

"She's the master," Djokovic chuckled. "It's a little tradition we have right now. Hopefully we can keep going so we can keep pumping more in Wimbledon."

The heartwarming moment added a personal touch to Djokovic's milestone day, proving once again that while Grand Slam records are remarkable, it's the family moments that often leave the biggest mark.

items.title: Gita shlokas to be recited daily in Uttarakhand govt schools
items.story: Uttarakhand schools will now recite Shrimad Bhagavad Gita shlokas during prayer meetings. The government aims to integrate traditional knowledge with modern education, emphasizing the importance of understanding the meanings and scientific relevance of the shlokas. Teachers will explain the principles of the Gita to enhance students' human values and character. The initiative is supported by the inclusion of new textbooks that incorporate teachings from the Gita and Ramayana. The directive was issued by Dr. Mukul Kumar Sati, director of secondary education, and aligns with the national education policy 2020, which encourages the integration of traditional Indian knowledge systems into modern education. The teachings, rooted in psychology, logic, and moral philosophy, are intended to promote character development, self-control, and leadership skills among students. The initiative has been welcomed by various educational leaders and is expected to foster unity and progress within the state.

items.title: Man loses money due to account number error, court orders banks to pay up
items.story: In Hyderabad, a routine health insurance payment turned into a two-year ordeal for 69-year-old Vanga Krishna Reddy. This involved two banks, an insurance firm, and eventually a consumer court. A single-digit error occurred when transferring Rs 52,659 online for policy renewal in June 2023, causing the funds to be sent to the wrong account and remain there. Krishna Reddy, a resident of Peerzadiguda, made the transaction using his bank's mobile app just before the deadline. However, he mistyped one digit of the beneficiary account number, leading the transaction to show as "successful," but the funds never reached the insurer. Realizing the mistake after not receiving confirmation of renewal, he made a second payment with the correct details to keep the policy active, but the first transaction was lost. Krishna Reddy promptly informed his bank, which acknowledged the mistake and initiated a chargeback with the receiving bank. However, the process stalled when the other bank stated that the "customer cannot be contacted for obtaining debit confirmation." With no resolution, Krishna Reddy took the matter to the Ranga Reddy District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in May 2024. During the hearings, his bank claimed it followed procedure and was not at fault as it never received the money. The other bank failed to appear and was declared ex-parte. The commission found both banks guilty of service deficiency. It noted that banks are responsible for verifying mismatches between account numbers and beneficiary names, a step neither bank took. The court criticized the banks' apathy despite being alerted, which caused financial loss and mental distress to the customer. It ordered the two banks to jointly refund the Rs 52,659 with 10% annual interest, and also pay Rs 10,000 each towards compensation and legal expenses.

items.title: Coldrif tragedy: Doctor held, SIT set up as Madhya Pradesh's 'syrup toll' rises to 14
items.story: BHOPAL: Three more children died in Madhya Pradesh's Chhindwara on Sunday after allegedly having cough syrup, taking the toll to 14 on a day a government doctor was arrested, an SIT was formed and the body of a two-year-old girl was exhumed for autopsy - the first among the reported fatalities so far. In Chhindwara, doctor Praveen Soni, who prescribed Coldrif to many of the young victims, was charged with negligence causing death. Two other deaths, of kids aged two and four, were reported from neighbouring Betul but the collector did not link them to cough syrup. Body of 2-year-old girl exhumed with parental consent: Cops. Dr Praveen Soni was charged with prescribing many victims Coldrif, the cough syrup that MP government banned on Saturday after a test report confirmed diethylene glycol, in samples of the formulation. The FIR against Dr Soni also mentions Sresan Pharmaceuticals, the Tamil Nadu-based manufacturer of Coldrif. All deaths were due to renal failure and most of the children were aged four and below. 'The accused doctor has been arrested. The SIT will also visit TN. On Sunday, body of a two-year-old girl, who died Saturday, was exhumed with parental consent, and an autopsy was conducted. The report is awaited,' Chhindwara SP Ajay Pandey told TOI. Dr Soni, remanded in police custody, was suspended hours after the FIR, which accused him of conducting private practice and prescribing medicines without proper diagnosis. An inquiry instituted against him concluded that his negligence 'caused irreparable harm' and 'tarnished the department's image'. The FIR charged the doctor and the cough syrup maker with negligence causing death, and adulterating of drugs. They were also booked under Section 27(a) of Drugs and Cosmetics Act, which mentions that anyone manufacturing, selling, or distributing an adulterated or substandard drug that causes death or grievous harm is liable for imprisonment of up to 10 years. Chhindwara ADM Dheerendra Singh said financial aid was sanctioned for families of the 14 children: 'In Nagpur, eight children are still admitted.' In Betul, officials said both victims suffered kidney failure after treatment in Parasia. However, the Betul collector did not confirm any links of the deaths with Coldrif.

items.title: 'Will continue to ask': Bhagwant Mann rebuffs MEA’s condemnation; says he has right to question PM's foreign tours
items.story: Punjab's Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann has responded to the Ministry of External Affairs' (MEA) condemnation of his criticism regarding Prime Minister Narendra Modi's frequent foreign visits. Mann questioned the purpose and benefits of these trips, especially pointing out a correlation between Modi's travels and the expansion of Adani's business interests. He expressed concerns over whether these visits genuinely benefit the country, highlighting the need for the Prime Minister to engage with India's 140 crore citizens and address domestic issues, such as the water disputes between Punjab and Haryana. The MEA had labeled Mann's remarks as irresponsible and regrettable, suggesting they could harm India's international relations, particularly with nations in the Global South. Mann's comments came after PM Modi's recent tours to countries like Ghana, Trinidad and Tobago, Argentina, Brazil, and Namibia. Mann mocked the value of these trips, questioning the significance of receiving accolades from countries with small populations and ridiculing the choice of destinations. The MEA distanced itself from Mann's statements, emphasizing their potential to undermine India's diplomatic ties.

items.title: Gujarat bridge collapse: Death toll rises to 19; rescue operations continue
items.story:
The Mahisagar River bridge collapse in Gujarat's Vadodara district has claimed 19 lives, with rescue operations ongoing for two missing individuals. A section of the 40-year-old bridge collapsed, sending vehicles into the river. Preliminary reports suggest pedestal and articulation failure as the cause, leading to the suspension of four engineers and a statewide bridge survey.

In response to the tragedy, Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel suspended four engineers from the state's Roads and Buildings Department. A preliminary report indicated pedestal and articulation failure as the likely cause of the collapse. A high-level inquiry committee will submit a comprehensive report within 30 days. Additionally, a statewide survey identified 7,000 bridges, some of which require urgent repairs or replacement.

The rescue operations involve the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), and local volunteers, facing challenges due to muddy terrain and chemical leaks from vehicles involved in the crash. Since 2021, Gujarat has witnessed at least six major bridge collapses, raising concerns about infrastructure safety across the state.

items.title: Kolkata law college gang rape: 'Keep room ready,' Monojit Mishra told guard before assault; cops collect his salary slip, appointment letter
items.story: Monojit Mishra, the prime suspect in a gang rape at a law college in Kolkata, allegedly instructed the security guard, Pinaki Banerjee, to prepare a room before the crime took place. Banerjee was aware that parties frequently occurred in the guards' room and was threatened to remain silent. Prior to the incident, Monojit reportedly told Banerjee to keep the room ready with sufficient water and a clean bed sheet. Despite Banerjee's attempt to inform Monojit that the college had closed for the day, Monojit allegedly threatened him to stay quiet. After the three accused entered the room, Zaib Ahmed and Pramit Mukherjee instructed Banerjee to lock the main gate and hand over the keys to them, effectively directing him to leave. Banerjee complied and left for tea. He later noticed Zaib fetching an inhaler, which Zaib claimed was needed by someone, and advised Banerjee not to worry about it. The 24-year-old victim mentioned in her complaint that she was given an inhaler due to breathlessness from a panic attack and was then raped. Banerjee has been presented before Alipore court and remanded in police custody. Police have reconstructed the crime scene with the accused and are investigating the social media activities of Monojit and the others. They have collected Monojit's salary slip, appointment letter, and attendance register from the college to verify his employment status. The investigation is being handled by the women's grievance cell and a special investigation team.

items.title: Can't decipher FIR, 1984 murder unsolved
items.story: The murder of an Army man during the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in Kanpur will remain unsolved due to an illegible First Information Report (FIR). Despite efforts by the Central Forensic Science Laboratory (CFSL) to reconstruct the document, the names of the accused and details of the incident remain undecipherable. The Supreme Court has directed the Special Investigation Team (SIT) and Uttar Pradesh police to keep the case open for further investigation based on new information. An army man's murder by an anti-Sikh riots mob at Kanpur on November 1, 1984, remains unsolved as the time-torn and damaged FIR remains illegible. Even the Central Forensic Science Laboratory could neither decipher the names of the accused nor the narration of the incident except that it was lodged under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code. Sketchy details of the FIR, provided by Uttar Pradesh government's standing counsel Ruchira Goel to a bench led by Justices Surya Kant in January this year, revealed that on November 1, 1984, a day after the assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, around 150-200 people barged into the house of retired Army personnel Diwan Singh at Yashoda Nagar in Naubasta, Kanpur, murdered him, and looted his house. The bench had ordered the state to take the assistance of CFSL in reconstructing the FIR to attempt to bring to book the culprits who unleashed a massacre virtually backed by the then governing political party. However, the counsel informed a bench of Justices Kant and Joymalya Bagchi that the FIR remains illegible despite the best efforts of CFSL. Unwilling to give up the pursuit of delivering justice, the bench asked the Special Investigation Team it had constituted to re-investigate anti-Sikh riot cases and UP police to keep the case open and pursue it further whenever they get hold of additional information relating to Diwan Singh's cold-blooded murder. For the PIL petitioner Manjit Singh GK, advocate Jagjit Singh Chhabra told the bench, though charge sheets were filed by SIT in nine anti-Sikh riots cases in Kanpur, High Court has stayed trial in three cases on appeals filed by the accused seeking quashing of the final probe reports. The Supreme Court bench said, "While we do not want to impact the rights of the accused, including their right to seek quashing of chargesheet, we would request High Court to take up these appeals out of turn for expeditious adjudication."

items.title: Season’s first cyclone, ‘Shakhti’, forms over Arabian Sea; IMD warns of high sea activity
items.story: PUNE: The season's first cyclonic storm over the Arabian Sea intensified into ‘Cyclone Shakhti’ on Friday, stated the India Meteorological Department (IMD). The system, currently centred about 250km west-southwest of Dwarka, is expected to strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by Saturday. While forecasters said it is unlikely to make a significant impact on Indian landmass, sea conditions are expected to be rough over the weekend. As of 11.30am on Friday, Cyclone Shakhti lay over the northeast Arabian Sea near latitude 21.7°N and longitude 66.8°E, around 270km southwest of Naliya, 300km west of Porbandar and 360km south of Karachi in Pakistan. The system was moving northwestwards at a speed of 8kmph and will later track west-southwestwards towards the central Arabian Sea, said IMD. It is likely to reach central parts of north and adjoining central Arabian Sea by Oct 5. 'Though the system will intensify into a severe cyclone, it will weaken considerably before nearing Gujarat's coastline. Rainfall is expected in parts of Gujarat, but no major impact is anticipated in India,' said a weather blogger from Vagaries of Weather. Independent weather forecaster Abhijit Modak also said, 'The storm's remnants may bring some rain to Saurashtra and Kutch.' An IMD official confirmed that the storm's trajectory is away from the Indian landmass. 'The movement is west-northwestwards initially and then west-southwestwards. The system won't directly impact land but will affect sea conditions. Fishermen are advised not to venture into the sea,' the official said. According to IMD, sea conditions were very rough to high over the northwest Arabian Sea, adjoining northeast and central Arabian Sea till the afternoon of Oct 3 and will turn high to very high between Oct 4-6. Rough to very rough sea conditions are expected along and off the Gujarat-north Maharashtra and Pakistan coasts till Oct 5. From Oct 3-6, fishermen have been advised to not venture into northwest Arabian Sea, adjoining northeast Arabian Sea, central Arabian Sea, and along/off Gujarat-north Maharashtra coasts. Meanwhile, light to moderate rain and thunderstorms are likely at most places in Madhya Maharashtra and Marathwada on Oct 3-4, influenced by a depression over interior Odisha, added IMD.

items.title: Make yoga part of your daily life, not just an annual activity, say practitioners in Hyderabad
items.story: On Saturday morning, KBR Park, one of Hyderabad's greenest and most iconic spaces, was filled with energy as nearly 100 people unrolled their yoga mats to celebrate the International Day of Yoga. People of all ages began arriving at the park in the morning wearing tracksuits and white tees bearing the slogan 'Yoga for Harmony and Peace'. The event featured a display of various 'asanas' and meditation exercises. The session began with 'tadasana' and progressed through a series of yoga poses, stretches, and breathing practices, culminating in the 'suryanamaskar'. Regular practitioners told STOI how yoga has helped them navigate different life challenges. Sadik, a 15-year-old, said yoga helped improve his grades. 'I perform yoga twice a week. It has helped me focus more on my studies,' he said, effortlessly switching yoga poses. 'Yoga didn’t just help me with my studies, it has also improved my mental health. It’s taught me how to remain calm and avoid stress,' the youngster explained. Along with Sadik, several other young people shared their experiences of how starting yoga at a young age had a profound impact on their lives. For Saikirti, 24, yoga was a cure for her health problems. 'I was suffering from thyroid and diabetes. I was unable to find a cure for it for the longest time,' she said. Embracing yoga offered the elusive solution she was looking for, she said. 'I have been practising yoga for the last six months. It has been one of the best decisions of my life. My health is much better now, and I am in a happier space,' Saikirti said. 'I had spondylitis (inflammation of the bones that make up the spine). Yoga helped cure it. It has also improved my lung capacity,' said Yashasri, a GHMC employee working with the Swachh Bharat mission. For 46-year-old P. Seetha Ram, yoga is the key to a long and healthy life. 'I’m turning 50 in a few years and I’m still feeling young and fit, like a youngster. I’m sure if I keep practising yoga, I won’t have to suffer body and joint pains when I grow older,' he said confidently. As the sun set on another International Day of Yoga, practitioners had only one request — make yoga a routine, not something to be reserved only for an annual celebration.

items.title: Social media ban: After violent protests, Nepal restores Facebook, X; minister cites emergency cabinet decision
items.story: Nepal's government has reversed its ban on 26 social media platforms following widespread protests in Kathmandu. Thousands of young Nepalis demonstrated against the decision, leading to violent clashes with police. Tragically, the unrest resulted in 19 fatalities and over 300 injuries as police used force to disperse the crowds. The Nepal government lifted the ban on social media after thousands of young Nepalis took to the streets of Kathmandu to protest. Nepal’s communication and information minister Prithvi Subba Gurung on Sunday said the government has rolled back its decision to ban social media platforms after an emergency Cabinet meeting. He announced that agencies have been directed to restore access to the platforms, days after authorities ordered 26 sites, including Facebook and X, to be blocked for not registering with the government. The reversal came after large-scale protests in Kathmandu, led by ‘Gen Z’ demonstrators who had camped outside Parliament. Gurung appealed to the group to call off their agitation. The protests turned violent on Monday when some participants breached the Parliament complex, forcing police to use water cannons, tear gas, and live rounds to disperse them. According to reports, clashes between protesters and police left 19 people dead and more than 300 others injured. The demonstrations, largely driven by the youth, erupted after the controversial decision was announced, with police resorting to firing at multiple locations to disperse crowds. The India-Nepal border has been put on alert amid protests in Nepal. The Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB), which guards the border, has stepped up vigilance and is closely monitoring developments to prevent any spillover of unrest into Indian territory. Officials stressed that the alert is ‘preventive in nature’ and that the situation remains under control. Nepal’s home minister Ramesh Lekhak resigned after violent protests. Lekhak, a Nepali Congress leader in the coalition government, stepped down on ‘moral grounds’ amid nationwide outrage. The protests, led largely by youths, shook Kathmandu and several other cities before turning deadly. The blackout, which began Friday, followed a government order blocking 26 social media platforms for failing to register locally. The list included Facebook, Instagram, X (formerly Twitter), YouTube, WhatsApp, LinkedIn, and Reddit. At a Cabinet meeting chaired by Communications Minister Prithvi Subba Gurung, companies were given seven days to meet compliance rules: register with the ministry, appoint a grievance officer, name a compliance officer, and set up a point of contact in Nepal. While some apps such as TikTok, Viber, Wetalk, and Nimbuzz have registered — and Telegram and Global Diary are in the process — major global platforms have yet to comply. Officials said access will be restored once requirements are met. The decision came after a Supreme Court ruling in September 2024 directing stricter oversight of unlicensed platforms, OTT apps, and browsers. A joint bench of Justices Tek Prasad Dhungana and Shanti Singh Thapa had upheld petitions seeking regulation of ads and content. Nepal’s blackout mirrors a global trend, with governments from the US and EU to India, Brazil, China, and Australia tightening controls on Big Tech amid concerns over misinformation, privacy, online safety, and national security.

items.title: IND vs ENG: Team India arrives in Manchester via train, takes last moment U-turn and walks 300m in rain
items.story: TimesofIndia.com in Manchester: The Indian cricket team arrived in Manchester via train this afternoon and was greeted by a steady drizzle. The team, however, took a last-minute U-turn and didn't take the planned route of exiting the platform where the train had arrived. They instead snuck out from a back door, and the players were made to walk 300m, mostly in the rain, to board the team bus. Captain Shubman Gill was spotted with the team as others rushed into the bus because of the rain. India stayed back in London after the heartbreak at Lord's and even had a training session in Beckenham. Every player except KL Rahul was in attendance, and while the likes of Rishabh Pant, Akash Deep, and Mohammed Siraj took it easy, the rest operated at full intensity. There was a cause for concern as Arshdeep Singh, who is yet to play a game, injured his bowling hand. The side will now begin preparations at the Old Trafford Ground in Manchester with sessions tomorrow, the day after, and on the eve of the match. The first session will be behind closed doors without any access to the media, just like it happened for two sessions in Birmingham, and doors will be opened for the morning session on July 21 and the afternoon hit on July 22. The Indian team will find the city very pleasant compared to London as it is much cooler and there has been consistent drizzle for the last few days. Even the match days have forecasts of rain, but it hasn't been threatening so far. An odd spell of light showers here and there shouldn't really be a cause for major concern. The weather, however, can play funny tricks in England, and Manchester is unlikely to be any different in the coming week.

items.title: Supreme Court junks plea against Telangana’s 42% Backward Classes quota in local body polls
items.story: Hyderabad: The Supreme Court on Monday dismissed a petition challenging the Telangana government's decision to enhance reservations for Backward Classes (BCs) to 42% in the upcoming local body elections. A division bench comprising Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sundeep Mehta declined to entertain the plea, noting that two similar petitions are already pending before the Telangana high court. However, the bench granted liberty to the petitioner, Vanga Gopal Reddy, to approach the high court to pursue the matter. 'As prayed by the petitioner, liberty is granted to approach the high court,' the court said while dismissing the petition. The Telangana high court has already heard petitions filed by B Madhav Reddy and Goreti Venkatesh on similar grounds and has scheduled the next hearing for Oct 8. Vanga Gopal Reddy, a resident of Rajanna Sircilla district, had approached the Supreme Court challenging GO No. 9, issued by the state government on Sept 26, which increased BC reservations in local body elections to 42%, in addition to 15% for SCs and 10% for STs. The petitioner sought directions to the state government to conduct elections in accordance with section 285A of the Telangana Panchayat Raj Act, 2018, which prohibits exceeding the 50% total reservation cap in local body polls. Appearing for the petitioner, advocate Somiran Sharma argued that the government issued the GO after court working hours and at the start of court vacation, in violation of Supreme Court guidelines on reservation limits. He also pointed out that the high court, during a house motion hearing on Sept 27, had refused to stay or modify the GO, following which the election notification was issued on Sept 29. 'Since the election notification has been issued applying the latest reservation pattern, it will be difficult for the petitioners to continue their challenge,' Sharma submitted. The Supreme Court, however, observed that since the high court had not granted a stay, the petitioner could not bypass the high court and approach the apex court directly, and accordingly dismissed the petition.

items.title: Glimpses from Kuno! Video shows Cheetahs Agni and Vayu after hunting; cubs resting
items.story: Union minister Bhupender Yadav shared two videos highlighting the progress of cheetah conservation efforts at Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh. In one video, two adult male cheetahs, Agni and Vayu, are seen roaming the grasslands after a successful hunt. These cheetahs, initially relocated from South Africa in February 2023, were released into the open forest across the Kuno River in December 2024, aligning with International Cheetah Day. Prior to their release, they spent over a year in protective enclosures. Another video shows the male cubs of cheetah Aasha resting in the wild after a hunt. Born in December 2023, these cubs are now just over a year old. Their father, Pawan (also known as Oban), was one of the first cheetahs introduced to Kuno but died in August 2023. The release of Aasha’s cubs into the open forest is seen as a positive step towards sustaining the cheetah population in India. Madhya Pradesh chief minister Mohan Yadav praised the move, noting its benefits to wildlife and regional tourism.

items.title: Language row rages: Remove Hindi banners from Ooty railway station, A Raja writes to Ashwini Vaishnaw; cites Tamil sentiments
items.story: DMK's A Raja has urged Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw to remove Hindi banners from the Nilgiris railway station. Raja argues that the increasing use of Hindi disregards Tamil Nadu's linguistic identity and violates the state's two-language policy. In his letter, Raja expressed concerns about the growing prominence of Hindi at the railway station, which has led to widespread protests. He pointed out that the Udhagamandalam railway station, which is over 100 years old, is undergoing renovation under the Amrit Bharat scheme. Although only 90% of the work is complete, banners have already been put up, which he claims hurt the sentiments of the Tamil people. Raja emphasized Tamil Nadu's proud history of linguistic identity and cultural autonomy, noting that the state has always supported a two-language policy. The developments at Udhagamandalam railway station are seen as a linguistic imposition, promoting Hindi in public spaces, which seems disconnected from the local population's linguistic needs and is seen as a political assertion. Raja reiterated that a quote attributed to Malaviya was actually said by Tamil poet Mahakavi Bharathi and urged the removal of the banners to respect the linguistic sentiments of Tamil Nadu's people.

items.title: Presidential reference case: SC issues notice to Centre, states; timeline for governor assent to bills under review
items.story:
The Supreme Court of India has addressed a Presidential reference concerning the timelines for governors and the President to act on Bills passed by state legislatures. A Constitution Bench led by Chief Justice of India BR Gavai has issued notices to the Central government and all states, seeking clarity on the Court's authority to set such deadlines. The Bench, which includes Justices Surya Kant, Vikram Nath, PS Narasimha, and Atul S Chandurkar, has asked Attorney General R Venkataramani to assist in the matter, with Solicitor General Tushar Mehta representing the Centre. The case has been scheduled for further hearing on Tuesday, July 29. 

This reference was made by President Droupadi Murmu under Article 143(1) of the Constitution, which allows the President to seek the Supreme Court's opinion on legal questions or matters of public importance. The reference follows an April ruling where the Supreme Court established timelines for the President and governors to act on Bills. This ruling was made in response to a case filed by the State of Tamil Nadu, where the Court stated that the absence of a time limit under Article 200 does not allow governors to delay action indefinitely. 

The April 8 verdict marked the first time the Court prescribed that the President should decide on the Bills reserved for her consideration within three months from receiving such reference. The Court ruled that inaction by a governor under Article 200 is subject to judicial review and emphasized that the President's decision under Article 201 must be made within a reasonable period. The ruling challenged the interpretation of Articles 200 and 201, arguing that neither article grants the Court the power to set these timelines, nor is the concept of "deemed assent" mentioned in the Constitution. Following this, President Murmu posed fourteen questions to the Supreme Court regarding the powers of governors and the President in dealing with state legislature Bills.

items.title: "I just kept going": Dwyane Wade's wife Gabrielle Union reveals she miscarried while filming and had to keep going like nothing happened
items.story:
Dwyane Wade and Gabrielle Union are enjoying family time with their daughter, Kaavia, following a challenging year that included Wade's kidney surgery. Union has recently spoken about her struggles with miscarriages, including a particularly difficult experience while filming 'Being Mary Jane.' The couple, who married in 2014, faced fertility issues and ultimately welcomed their daughter Kaavia via surrogacy. 

Gabrielle Union opened up about her traumatic experience of having a miscarriage while filming, saying, "I just kept going. When your heart is literally ripped out, each pregnancy just feels like a dream come true." Despite the hardships, the couple is now in a happy phase of their lives.

items.title: GSI celebrates one year of NLFC with pledge to expand live landslide warnings
items.story: The Geological Survey of India (GSI) celebrated the first anniversary of its National Landslide Forecasting Centre (NLFC) at the Dharitri Building in Salt Lake Sector V, Kolkata. The event highlighted a year of scientific advancements and critical early warning interventions in India's most landslide-prone areas. Starting July 20, residents and tourists in Kalimpong, Darjeeling, and the Nilgiris will receive live landslide forecast bulletins, aiming to enhance community preparedness and reduce casualties during the monsoon season. The event was inaugurated by GSI Director General Asit Saha, with the presence of Priyanka Singla from the West Bengal State Disaster Management Authority and other key stakeholders. The NLFC, launched under the Ministry of Mines, focuses on high-risk zones, integrating advanced modeling tools, real-time rainfall data, and slope instability monitoring to issue timely alerts. Over the past year, the NLFC has operationalized the Landslide Early Warning System (LEWS), providing daily forecast bulletins in 21 districts across eight states. A senior GSI official stated the Centre's goal to extend LEWS coverage nationwide by 2030. To mark the milestone, GSI hosted a national-level workshop with experts from NDMA, IMD, ISRO's National Remote Sensing Centre, state governments, IITs, and academic institutions to discuss technology, success stories, and the future of landslide forecasting. The NLFC's growing role emphasizes GSI's commitment to a safer, more resilient India through scientific excellence and collaboration.

items.title: Telangana municipal officials booked for Rs 7.2 lakh fraud: Fake bills raised under 'Pattana Pragathi' scheme; ACB names Huzurnagar commissioner, 2 engineers
items.story:
The Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has registered a case against Huzurnagar municipal commissioner Kankati Srinivas Reddy and two other officials for allegedly misappropriating Rs 7.2 lakh of government funds during their earlier tenure in Tandur municipality under the 'Pattana Pragathi' scheme. The ACB action followed a vigilance inquiry after a complaint by Ward 13 councillor of Tandur municipality, Varala Srinivas Reddy, accusing the commissioner and two engineers of creating bills for fictitious development work using benami contractors by falsifying records. 

The ACB FIR, issued on May 5, stated that Srinivas Reddy, Mohd Younus (deputy executive engineer), and Gopala Mahesh (assistant engineer) colluded to siphon off government funds in the name of fake development work. The FIR noted that in one instance, the complainant personally undertook silt removal in Chilakavagu, a drain flowing through his ward, using his own resources. However, officials sanctioned Rs 3 lakh in the name of another individual, R Santosh Kumar, for the same work. In another case, officials exaggerated the usage of an excavator during the second phase of the scheme. While the machine was deployed for 20 hours, the records falsely showed 144 hours of work, and bills worth Rs 5 lakh were raised.

The ACB's internal investigation by inspector Akula Srinivas revealed that the trio submitted fake bills using three measurement books for Rs 3 lakh, Rs 2.46 lakh and Rs 1.73 lakh - totaling Rs 7.20 lakh. These works were neither executed nor verified on the ground. The inquiry concluded that all three officials abused their official positions and committed offenses under Section 13(1)(a) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (as amended in 2018), and IPC Sections 409 and 420.

items.title: Top 5 entertainment news: Salman Khan sells Bandra West apartment for Rs 5.35 Crore, Jackson Wang REACTS to dating rumours with Disha Patani
items.story: Today in Tinseltown, several exciting events took place. Salman Khan has sold his Bandra West apartment in Mumbai’s Shiv Asthan Heights for ₹5.35 crore. Despite the sale, he continues to reside at Galaxy Apartments, which is located just 2.2 km away. In a separate development, K-pop star Jackson Wang has addressed rumors about dating Bollywood actress Disha Patani, clarifying on The Kapil Sharma Show that they are just friends. He also mentioned on the Chapter Two podcast that he has been single for two years and is not currently interested in dating. Meanwhile, Bollywood actor Vicky Kaushal shared a heartfelt birthday post for his wife, Katrina Kaif, on Instagram. The post included candid and affectionate moments, such as playful peeks and serene picnics, accompanied by a loving caption that went viral. In family news, Sidharth Malhotra and Kiara Advani announced the birth of their daughter, Raina, expressing their joy and gratitude. Their announcement has received an outpouring of love and congratulations from Bollywood celebrities. Lastly, comedians Samay Raina and Vipul Goyal were reprimanded by India's Supreme Court for making jokes about disabled individuals, with the court emphasizing the need for humor to respect human dignity and the rights of vulnerable communities.

items.title: Extorted over months, manipulated through threats: Blackmailed into paying 2.5cr hush money, Mumbai CA kills himself; FIR names 2 Instagram friends
items.story: A 32-year-old chartered accountant in Mumbai died by suicide after allegedly being blackmailed for a sum of ₹2.5 crore by two individuals he had befriended on Instagram. Vakola police have registered a case of abetment to suicide and extortion against these two suspects, who have not yet been arrested. The chartered accountant had previously filed a complaint against them, claiming they had threatened to release intimate videos. According to police, the accountant's mother found three suicide notes where he expressed that he was compelled to withdraw money from family savings and siphon off funds from his company's account to meet the demands of the blackmailers. The police are now examining the company's accounts for such withdrawals. The mother reported that her son became depressed after the suspects visited their home on June 7, where they allegedly threatened to expose his relationship with them and post intimate videos online. In her complaint, the mother mentioned that her son confided in her about the extortion. Of the three suicide notes, one was directed to his mother, another to his company, and the third held the two suspects accountable for his death.

items.title: Just 50 air-launched weapons pulverised Pak, says IAF vice-chief
items.story: In a recent seminar on aerospace power, Indian Air Force Vice Chief Air Marshal Narmdeshwar Tiwari highlighted the success of Operation Sindoor, where under 50 air-launched weapons were deployed to target Pakistani airbases and radar sites. This operation, according to Tiwari, compelled Pakistan to negotiate and seek peace. He emphasized the strategic value of air power, indicating that a minimal number of weapons can force an adversary to the negotiation table. The operation involved the use of Sukhoi-30MKI, Rafale, and Mirage-2000 fighters to launch BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles, as well as Crystal Maze-2, Rampage, and Scalp missiles, achieving precise strikes on Pakistani targets, some near nuclear facilities. Chief of Defence Staff General Anil Chauhan emphasized the need for constant high operational readiness and the importance of learning both warfare tactics ('shastra') and knowledge ('shaastra'). He noted the ongoing relevance of Operation Sindoor and the necessity for the Indian military to adapt to rapid technological advancements and geopolitical changes. The seminar also stressed the importance of prioritizing the development of aerospace power in India, citing its strategic importance in maintaining escalation dominance over Pakistan and setting a new red line against nuclear blackmail.

items.title: No body, no relief: Missing Telangana's Sigachi workers' kin left in agonising limbo; call for strict & transparent regulations
items.story: Nearly two weeks after the devastating explosion at Sigachi Industries, the families of eight missing workers continue to live in anguish, lacking answers, bodies, and closure. Despite repeated DNA tests and sleepless nights outside hospitals, there is still no confirmation on the fate of their loved ones. The absence of official death certificates means that not a single rupee of the promised compensation from the state government has reached these families. The state government and the company promised Rs 1 crore as relief, with Rs 1 lakh to be released immediately for day-to-day expenses, but the families have received nothing. P Pravinya, Sangareddy collector, stated that the families could leave as it is unlikely that the remains of the eight missing workers will be found. However, they can stay at the rehabilitation center as long as they want. The collector explained that a final report on all forensic findings must be submitted to the government before discussing compensation. Many families, like that of Umesh Chandra Sharma, are caught in an endless wait, unsure of their loved ones' fate. Bajrangi Lal Nishad, searching for his two elder brothers, expressed similar despair, as did Anitha Kumari, awaiting word on her husband, Shivaji Kumar. The families are grappling with the uncertainty and the lack of closure, as they wait indefinitely for answers and compensation.

items.title: Saiyaara box office day 7: The Ahaan Panday-Aneet Padda starrer surpasses Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahani with Rs 170 crore collection
items.story: Mohit Suri's film 'Saiyaara,' starring Ahaan Panday and Aneet Padda, has achieved remarkable success at the box office, grossing over ₹170 crore in its first week. The film's success is attributed to positive reviews and significant buzz on social media, which helped it surpass the lifetime collection of 'Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahani.' The director, Mohit Suri, expressed his gratitude towards Sandeep Reddy Vanga for his early support of the film. Despite being a weekday, the film continues to draw crowds, with earnings of ₹16.61 crore on the seventh day. With no major releases slated for the upcoming Friday, 'Saiyaara' is expected to maintain its momentum into the second weekend. The film's total collection has now reached ₹170.36 crore, officially surpassing the ₹153.55 crore lifetime earnings of 'Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahani.' The story of 'Saiyaara' revolves around Krish Kapoor (played by Ahaan Panday), an aspiring musician, and Vaani Batra (played by Aneet Padda), a reserved writer. Their romantic journey takes an unexpected turn following a shocking revelation. The film is produced by Yash Raj Films. On Thursday, Mohit Suri thanked Sandeep Reddy Vanga on social media for being the first to express confidence in the film.

items.title: Devotion & drums: Month-long Bonalu festival starts at Golconda Fort with Bonam offering to Goddess Jagadambika
items.story: Telangana's vibrant Bonalu festival commenced with traditional fervor, honoring Goddess Mahakali. The rituals began with priests invoking blessings, followed by a procession to the Jagadamba temple. Women carried Bonams, offerings of cooked rice and jaggery, while Potharajus danced to drum beats. Minister Konda Surekha offered 'pattu vastrams' on behalf of the state government. The Bonalu festival is a spirited celebration of Telangana’s rich cultural and spiritual heritage. It is celebrated during the Ashada masam to honor the Goddess Mahakali for protecting people from disease and evil. The rituals began with priests invoking divine blessings, followed by a lively procession from Langar Houz to the hilltop Jagadamba temple. Hundreds of women, clad in vibrant sarees and traditional jewelry, carried intricately decorated earthen pots on their heads. These Bonams—offerings of cooked rice, jaggery, curd, and neem leaves—symbolize devotion and a prayer for protection. They were accompanied by Potharajus, whip-wielding guardians believed to represent the goddess’s brother, dancing energetically to the beats of drums. Endowments minister Konda Surekha offered ‘pattu vastrams’ to the deity on behalf of the state government. The festivities were attended by Greater Hyderabad mayor Gadwal Vijayalakshmi, assembly speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar, and transport minister Ponnam Prabhakar, among others.

items.title: Jaish ultra killed in Basantgarh operation was a top commander: J&K DGP
items.story: A top commander of the Jaish-e-Mohammad, identified as Haider, was killed in an encounter with security forces in the Basantgarh area of Udhampur district, as confirmed by the Director General of Police (DGP) of Jammu and Kashmir, Nalin Prabhat. Haider had been active in the Dudu-Basantgarh forests for four years, marking one of the longest periods of activity for a terrorist in the region. The DGP mentioned ongoing anti-terror operations in the Union Territory during an event in Akhnoor, where he spoke to reporters. The event was held at the Akhnoor police station, which was recognized by the Union home ministry as the best police station in Jammu and Kashmir for 2024. Several policemen were awarded for their exemplary service during this ceremony.

items.title: 'Boasted friendship with Trump proving to be hollow': Jairam Ramesh targets PM Modi; lists '4 facts'
items.story:
Congress leader Jairam Ramesh strongly criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi's foreign policy, highlighting recent U.S. actions involving Pakistan as evidence of its shortcomings. Ramesh pointed out President Trump's claims of intervening in the India-Pakistan conflict, the praise from the U.S. Central Command for Pakistan's counter-terrorism efforts, and meetings between U.S. officials and Pakistani leaders.

In a post, Ramesh listed four recent developments that, according to him, demonstrate the failure of the Modi government's foreign affairs management. He accused the Prime Minister's supporters of misleading the public with exaggerated claims of diplomatic success.

Ramesh referred to President Trump's repeated claims about intervening in the India-Pakistan conflict, and noted the following points:

1. Since May 10, 2025, President Trump has claimed 25 times he personally intervened to stop Operation Sindoor, warning India and Pakistan that without halting the war, there would be no trade agreement with the USA.
2. On June 10, 2025, General Michael Kurilla, head of the U.S. Central Command, praised Pakistan as a phenomenal partner of the U.S. in countering terrorism.
3. On June 18, 2025, President Trump held an unprecedented luncheon meeting with Pakistani Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir at the White House. Munir had previously made provocative remarks that set the stage for the brutal Pahalgam terror attacks on April 22, 2025.
4. On July 25, 2025, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar, thanking Pakistan for its partnership in countering terrorism and maintaining regional stability.

Ramesh concluded by recalling Modi's 2020 statement on China, suggesting it had already cost the country dearly. He stated that Modi's much-vaunted friendship with President Trump is now proving to be hollow.

items.title: Asia Cup 2025 schedule: Complete fixtures, India vs Pakistan date out
items.story: The 2025 edition of the Men’s Asia Cup is officially scheduled to take place in the United Arab Emirates from September 9 to 28, as confirmed by the chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board on social media. The announcement promised a 'spectacular display of cricket'. Cricket fans can expect the detailed schedule, including specific venues and fixtures, to be released soon. India and Pakistan are likely to be drawn into the same group, setting up a highly anticipated match between the arch-rivals. This encounter would be their first since the political tensions following a terror attack in Pahalgam. Although Pakistan is the official host, the tournament will be held in the UAE, following the Asian Cricket Council's policy of holding events in neutral venues when India or Pakistan are designated hosts. Dubai and Abu Dhabi are expected to host the matches. The Asia Cup will feature eight teams and will serve as preparation for the ICC T20 World Cup in February 2026, which will be co-hosted by India and Sri Lanka. India, the defending champions, won the title in 2023 under Rohit Sharma's captaincy. The complete match schedule, including the India vs Pakistan fixture, will be announced soon.

items.title: 'Khula' a right, but only courts can issue it: Telangana high court
items.story: In a significant ruling, the Telangana High Court has clarified that 'khula' - a form of divorce initiated by Muslim women under Islamic law - is a legitimate right, but must be legally processed only through courts, and not by religious bodies. This ensures legal clarity and enforceability of the divorce, the HC said. A division bench comprising justices Moushumi Bhattacharya and B. R. Madhusudhan Rao on Tuesday upheld a family court's February 2024 ruling in a case where a homemaker had obtained 'khula' from her husband, a businessman. The HC ruled that while 'khula' was indeed a recognised form of divorce under Muslim personal law, religious bodies such as a mufti or sharia council could not issue binding divorce certificates. Only courts, or a qazi officially appointed under the law, had the legal power to declare the end of a marriage, it said. The HC ruling comes close on the heels of a Supreme Court judgment in April this year, which reaffirmed that while a Muslim woman had the right to seek 'khula', it was ultimately the courts, specifically family courts, that had the authority to grant or validate the divorce. The apex court also clarified that while a wife could initiate the process of 'khula', the husband could challenge it in court. In the present case, the husband had challenged the 'khulanama' (divorce certificate) obtained by his wife, arguing that it was granted by a religious body, Sada-e-Haq Sharai Council, which he claimed had no legal authority. The family court, however, upheld the divorce, noting proper legal procedures had been followed. The husband filed an appeal against the verdict, but the HC dismissed it.

items.title: Hyderabad teen plots mother's murder for love; boyfriend, brother turn killers
items.story: In Hyderabad, a 16-year-old girl, her boyfriend, and his brother have confessed to the murder of the girl's mother. The incident took place in Shapurnagar, where the girl plotted her mother's murder due to her disapproval of the relationship with her boyfriend, Shiva. Despite initially being supportive, the mother changed her stance, leading to conflict. Shiva and his brother strangled the mother, while the girl ensured the act was completed as the victim showed signs of life after the initial attempt. The murder took place on June 23, and the police confirmed the cause of death as strangulation. The girl, along with Shiva and his brother, were taken into custody, with the minors sent to juvenile homes and Shiva to Chanchalguda prison. The girl had previously instigated Shiva to commit the murder after her mother opposed the relationship and had even lodged a kidnap complaint against Shiva. On the day of the murder, the girl stood guard while the brothers carried out the act, and later ensured the murder was completed when the victim showed signs of life. The police have registered a murder case based on the younger sister's complaint.

items.title: Green tinge, slope and the Lord's: India batters set for their 'first' England challenge; third IND vs ENG Test from July 10
items.story: Ahead of India’s Test match at Lord’s, the pitch is expected to be more conducive to bowlers, especially in the early sessions, with more life than previous matches. The batting coach, Sitanshu Kotak, mentioned the green tinge and the potential for low first-innings scores. The iconic slope at Lord’s presents a unique challenge, requiring batsmen to adjust their techniques to handle the ball’s movement. Before India’s first training session, the support staff, led by head coach Gautam Gambhir, inspected the pitch. There was a fresh green tinge on the pitch, and coaches like Morne Morkel and Sitanshu Kotak conducted firmness checks. Some grass was shaved off to make the surface brighter, and the pitch received generous watering to keep it fresh. The pitch is expected to have more life than the ones at Headingley and Edgbaston. Jasprit Bumrah, while speaking with the ground staff, compared the surface to those in Nagpur and Kanpur. The pitch is likely to be livelier on the opening day, especially in the first two sessions. Sitanshu Kotak noted that there is more green on the wicket than in the last two matches, and the scores in the first and second innings at Lord’s are typically low. Many players will be facing their first match at Lord's, and the eight-foot slope requires minor adjustments. The slope makes the ball move away from right-handers more than usual from the Pavilion End and exaggerates movement towards right-handers from the Nursery End. This presents challenges for both batsmen and bowlers. A few minor adjustments can help batsmen handle the conditions. Kotak emphasized that dealing with the slope is more about mindset, as some players see it as a natural variation. India’s batsmen have been performing well in the Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy, and their ability to handle the slope will be crucial in determining the series outcome.

items.title: Kolkata rape case fallout: Rift in TMC widens as Kalyan Banerjee drags Mahua Moitra's personal life; takes 'honeymoon' jibe
items.story:
Trinamool Congress MPs Kalyan Banerjee and Mahua Moitra are embroiled in another public dispute, this time over Banerjee's controversial remarks regarding the South Calcutta Law College rape case. Barely three months after their previous public spat, Banerjee responded to Moitra's criticism by attacking her personal life, referencing her marriage, and questioning her ethics. 

Banerjee, while responding to Moitra’s criticism, targeted her personal life, referring to her marriage with former Biju Janata Dal (BJD) MP Pinaki Misra. "Mahua has come back to India after her honeymoon and started fighting with me! She accuses me of being anti-woman. What is she? She has broken up a 40-year marriage and married a guy who is 65 years old. Did she not hurt the lady?" he said. He further said, "An MP who was expelled from parliament for breach of ethics is preaching me! She is the most anti-woman."

Banerjee’s remarks came after Moitra backed the TMC's decision to publicly distance itself from his and party MLA Madan Mitra's statements about the Kolkata rape case. On Saturday, the TMC posted on X, "The remarks made by MP Kalyan Banerjee and MLA Madan Mitra concerning the heinous crime at South Calcutta Law College were made in their personal capacities. The party unequivocally disassociates itself from their statements and strongly condemns the same." Quoting the party’s post, Moitra wrote: "Misogyny in India cuts across party lines. What differentiates @AITCofficial is that we condemn these disgusting comments no matter who makes them."

Banerjee, in a statement on Friday, had said, "What can be done if a friend rapes his friend? Will the police be there in schools? This was done by students to another student. Who will protect her?" Mitra, meanwhile, blamed the survivor. "If someone calls you when the college is closed, then don't go. If she had taken a friend or informed someone, this wouldn't have happened," he said.

The alleged gang-rape took place on June 25. According to the 24-year-old survivor, three men -- Manojit Mishra, Pramit Mukherjee, and Zaib Ahmed -- took her to a guard’s room inside the law college, raped her, filmed the assault, and threatened to leak the video. She said she was confined for over three hours and was hit with a hockey stick when she resisted. All three accused were arrested within 24 hours. Mishra, a former office-bearer of the Trinamool Chhatra Parishad, was working on a temporary contract at the college and is a practising lawyer. The security guard, Pinaki Banerjee, has also been arrested. The accused are in police custody until July 1. A Special Investigation Team (SIT) has been set up.

The National Commission for Women (NCW) has taken suo motu cognisance and demanded a time-bound investigation. The BJP has also criticised the Mamata Banerjee-led government, with senior party leaders demanding her resignation and accusing the administration of failing to ensure women’s safety.

items.title: 'Angered every Indian': PM Modi slams attack on CJI Gavai; applauds top Justice's calm
items.story: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday spoke to Chief Justice of India BR Gavai after he was allegedly attacked during proceedings in the Supreme Court. In a social media post on X, PM Modi called the incident a 'reprehensible act' and said that the attack has angered every Indian. 'Spoke to Chief Justice of India, Justice BR Gavai Ji. The attack on him earlier today in the Supreme Court premises has angered every Indian. There is no place for such reprehensible acts in our society. It is utterly condemnable,' PM Modi said. 'I appreciated the calm displayed by Justice Gavai in the face of such a situation. It highlights his commitment to values of justice and strengthening the spirit of our Constitution,' he added. Earlier, an advocate named Rakesh Kishore attempted to hurl a shoe at Chief Justice of India B R Gavai during proceedings in the Supreme Court. The incident took place around 11.35 am, when the 71-year-old lawyer, identified as a resident of Mayur Vihar in Delhi, removed his sports shoes and tried to throw them towards the Bench presided over by the CJI. The CJI, however, remained composed during the disruption, telling the courtroom, 'Don’t get distracted by all this. We are not distracted. These things do not affect me.' Kishore was swiftly restrained by security personnel as he shouted, 'Sanatan ka apman nahi sahenge' ('We will not tolerate insults to Sanatan Dharma'). Later in the day, the Bar Council of India on Monday suspended advocate Rakesh Kishore from practising in any court with immediate effect, after he allegedly attempted to hurl a shoe at Chief Justice of India B R Gavai during proceedings in the Supreme Court. CJI Gavai had, during the hearing of the Lord Vishnu idol matter, remarked that the petitioner seeking directions to restore the idol should go and seek the remedy by praying to Lord Vishnu, as the Court declined to entertain the same. While refusing to hear the case, the top court opined that it's a dispute over a temple, which is a protected monument under the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), suggesting that the ASI is a better authority to intervene in this regard. As his remarks sparked reactions on social media, CJI Gavai clarified that he respects all religions. The comments came during the post-lunch session of the CJI-led bench at the Supreme Court. The Solicitor General of India (SGI), Tushar Mehta, who was also present in the court, stated that he has known the CJI for the last ten years and is aware that the CJI visits all religious places. Mehta added that these days, things are blown out of proportion on social media.

items.title: 'Got very big success': Terrorist killed in Udhampur was top JeM commander, J&K police reveals; vows to continue crackdown
items.story: Jammu and Kashmir's Director General of Police (DGP) Nalin Prabhat announced that a terrorist killed in a recent encounter in the Dudu-Basantgarh forest, Udhampur, was a top commander of the Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) from Pakistan. This commander had been active in the area for four years. The DGP emphasized the ongoing anti-terror operations and credited public support as crucial to their success, according to PTI reports. During a press briefing at the Akhnoor police station, the DGP stated, "The anti-terror operations are ongoing, and we have achieved significant success in Dudu-Basantgarh, where a senior and top JeM commander, active for the last four years, was eliminated. The operations will continue until all terrorists are eradicated." On June 26, a Pakistani terrorist known as Haider, or Maulvi, was killed during the operation, but three of his associates escaped due to inclement weather and the difficult terrain of the dense Basantgarh forest. The DGP did not disclose the exact number of active terrorists in Jammu's forested areas, citing security reasons. Accompanied by IG CRPF Gopal Sharma, IG Police Bhim Sen Tuti, and DIG Shiv Kumar, the DGP visited the Akhnoor police station to present the Ministry of Home Affairs' 'Award of Excellence' for outstanding performance in J-K's 2024 police station rankings. During the award ceremony, the DGP praised the station's personnel for their community engagement and highlighted a successful operation earlier in the year as evidence of effective public cooperation. He asserted that public support is vital for police success, easing challenging tasks. The DGP commended Jammu police for their efforts in combating drug trafficking, bovine smuggling, and organized crime. He recognized the leadership of former SHO Tariq Ahmed, SDPO Mohan Sharma, and SP Brijesh Sharma in 2024, and encouraged current SHO Sanjeev Chib and SDPO Varinder Gupta to maintain high standards.

items.title: Kiren Rijiju attends Dalai Lama's 90th birthday; pledges to follow his guidance
items.story:
Union Minister Kiren Rijiju participated in the 90th birthday celebrations of the 14th Dalai Lama in Dharamshala, Himachal Pradesh. The event involved prayers and tributes to the Tibetan spiritual leader. Tibetan Buddhist monks in exile conducted special prayers at Dorjidak Monastery near Shimla to mark the occasion. Rijiju addressed the gathering, highlighting the Dalai Lama's role as a bridge between ancient wisdom and the modern world, and expressed a sense of blessing from his presence in India. The Dalai Lama reflected on his life in exile, expressing his desire to continue benefiting others.

The celebrations occurred amid ongoing debates over the Dalai Lama's succession, a contentious issue between India and China. The Chinese foreign ministry recently stated that the selection of the next Dalai Lama must follow a Beijing-approved process, urging India to handle Tibet-related matters carefully to avoid straining bilateral relations. Kiren Rijiju reaffirmed India's stance, stating that India and millions of devotees worldwide would abide by the decisions and guidelines of the Dalai Lama's institution, rejecting external interference, specifically from China. The Dalai Lama has also asserted that his successor will be chosen by the India-based Gaden Phodrang Trust, the non-profit organization he founded, rejecting any outside interference, a message seen as directed at China.

items.title: 'Iran will never rebuild its nuclear program': Donald Trump says 'really unhappy with Israel'; adds 'not happy with Iran either'
items.story: US President Donald Trump has criticized both Israel and Iran for allegedly violating the recent ceasefire agreement. He specifically disapproved of Israel's actions following the truce, citing reported airstrikes after a missile launch from Iran. Despite acknowledging the violations, Trump expressed uncertainty about whether the ceasefire is entirely broken. During a press briefing, Trump accused both nations of breaching the agreement and cautioned Israel against further escalation. He reiterated his firm stance against Iran's nuclear ambitions, stating, "Iran will never rebuild its nuclear program." Trump expressed his displeasure at Israel's immediate retaliation, saying, "I am not happy that Israel is going out now. There was one rocket that I guess was fired overboard, and it missed its target. Now Israel is going out. These guys gotta calm down. Ridiculous. I didn't like the fact that Israel unloaded right after we made the deal... That's not what we want..." In a stern message on Truth Social, Trump warned, "Israel. Do not drop those bombs. If you do it is a major violation. Bring your pilots home, now! Donald J Trump, President of the United States." His message followed reports of Israeli airstrikes in response to an Iranian missile. Reacting to these developments, Trump stated, "They've been fighting so long and so hard that they don't know what they're doing," referring to Israel's military actions under the ceasefire. Speaking to reporters, Trump expressed clear dissatisfaction with both sides, saying, "I didn't like that Israel 'unloaded' immediately after agreeing to a ceasefire," and added, "I'm not happy with Iran either." He criticized both nations for failing to uphold the ceasefire terms, even as he downplayed the breach. When asked directly if the ceasefire had been officially broken, Trump responded, "I don't think so." In another post on Truth Social, Trump said, "ISRAEL is not going to attack Iran. All planes will turn around and head home, while doing a friendly 'Plane Wave' to Iran. Nobody will be hurt, the Ceasefire is in effect! Thank you for your attention to this matter!" During a conversation with reporters, Trump stated, "They (Iran) violated, but Israel violated it too. As soon as we made the deal, Israel came out and dropped a load of bombs... We basically have two countries that have been fighting so long and so hard that they don't know what they're doing."
items.relevanceReason: This is primarily a US–Israel–Iran ceasefire issue, not directly linked to Dr. Shashidhar’s constituency, Hindutva agenda, or local political landscape. While it touches on national security themes, it lacks immediate relevance for his Indian voter base or political positioning. Commenting might not yield significant traction or address his core objectives.

items.title: MS Dhoni files trademark for 'CAPTAIN COOL'; he joins ICC Hall of Fame - details inside
items.story:
MS Dhoni, the legendary former captain of the Indian cricket team, has filed a trademark application for his famous nickname 'CAPTAIN COOL.' The trademark application, which has been accepted and advertised, aims to cover services related to sports training, facilities, coaching, and related services. The application was filed on June 5 and published in the official trademark journal on June 16. Simultaneously, Dhoni is set to be inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame in 2025, highlighting his outstanding leadership, tactical brilliance, and valuable contributions to cricket.

Dhoni, admired for his calm demeanor under pressure and strategic skills, is recognized as one of cricket's greatest leaders and wicketkeepers. He is the only captain to have won all three ICC white-ball trophies: the inaugural T20 World Cup in 2007, the 2011 ODI World Cup, and the 2013 Champions Trophy. Under his leadership, India also achieved the number one ranking in Test cricket.

While Dhoni has not commented on the trademark development, another company, Prabha Skill Sports (OPC) Pvt Ltd, had previously applied for the same trademark, which is currently under 'rectification filed' status.

items.title: Mysuru shocker: Family of 4 attacked with machetes in full public view; accused on the run
items.story: In Mysuru, a shocking incident occurred where a family of four was brutally attacked with machetes while they were traveling in an auto-rickshaw on Ramanuja Road. The attack happened in full public view when a black car intercepted the auto, and a group of men emerged to assault the occupants. The incident took place on 14th cross Ramanuja Road in Agrahara around 9:30 pm. The brutal assault was captured on CCTV and mobile phone cameras, and the footage has gone viral on social media. Bystanders were seen panicking as the assailants fled the scene. All four victims, including Rajanna, who sustained serious injuries, were rushed to a nearby hospital, and according to the police, they are out of danger. DCP (Crime) KS Sundar Raj stated that a case of attempted murder has been registered against four individuals, and an investigation is underway by Krishnaraja police. An officer explained that the attack occurred when Rajanna, an accused in a POCSO case, was leaving Vidyaranyapuram police station after providing his statement. His wife, mother-in-law, and niece were with him in the auto at the time of the attack. Rajanna is facing charges of abusing a minor girl, and he had recently met the girl again after she turned 18, which angered the girl's family and led to the attack.

items.title: Centre revises price list: CGHS rates for tests, procedures increased; sharply in some cases
items.story: NEW DELHI: For the first time in over a decade, the Centre has revised the price list for nearly 2,000 tests and procedures for CGHS beneficiaries with the increase in some cases adding up to seven times the current level. The move is expected to help over 40 lakh CGHS beneficiaries who often faced difficulties in getting treatment at some of the top hospitals due to the low rates. While in most cases the increase in rates are nominal, there are also examples of significant increases. For example, the rate of complicated extraction of a tooth under local anaesthesia has been revised from Rs 115 to Rs 800 for NABH-accredited health facilities. Similarly, the rate of MRI mammography (test to find out breast cancer), stood at Rs 2,550 for non-NABH accredited hospitals, which has now been raised 67% to Rs 4,250. In the case of NABH-accredited and super-speciality hospitals it has been increased by around 60% to Rs 5,000 for NABH-accredited and super-specialty hospitals as per the revised rate list. The rate of exploratory laparotomy — an abdominal surgery — has been revised to Rs 27,500 from Rs 25,000 for NABH accredited hospitals. The new CGHS rates will be effective Oct 13, according to a govt order. It said CGHS has adopted the structure of differential rates based on accreditation status, hospital type, city classification and ward entitlement. Under this, the non-NABH and non-NABL healthcare facilities will get 15% lower rates than NABH/NABL accredited healthcare organisations (HCOs). (NABL – National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration of Laboratories). Also, rates for super-speciality hospitals shall be 15% higher than those applicable to NABH-accredited hospitals for the corresponding super-specialities within the same city category, govt order stated.
