The order added the rates for healthcare facilities located in Tier II cities and Tier III cities rates shall be 10% and 20% respectively lower than those located in Tier I cities.

items.title: Telangana's GI count hits 27 with 9 applications filed in past 2 months
items.story: Telangana's efforts to preserve its agricultural and artisanal heritage have accelerated in 2025, with nine new geographical indication (GI) applications submitted in the past two months. These include five applications for agricultural products, two for handicrafts, and one each for textiles and manufactured goods. Historically, it took over two decades for Telangana to obtain GI tags for just 18 products in categories like handicrafts, textiles, food, and agriculture. However, this year alone, eight applications were filed in July and one for Balanagar Custard Apple in June. This brings Telangana's total GI count to 27. With four more products nearing the filing stage, Telangana is on course to surpass 30 GIs in the coming months, according to Subhajit Saha, who has filed three of these nine applications on behalf of Resolute4IP. The four agricultural GI applications include Kollapur Benishan Mango, Nalgonda Nimma (acid lime), Jagtial Sesame, and Nalgonda Dosakai. Jagtial Sesame is known for its high oil content and nutty flavor, while Nalgonda Nimma is noted for its high juice content and intense tangy flavor. Nalgonda Dosakai (cucumber) is recognized for its mildly tangy taste, and Kollapur Benishan Mango is famous for its sweet taste, fiberless flesh, and vibrant yellow skin, making it highly sought after in export markets. The two handicraft applications are for Nalgonda Banjara Tribal Needle Crafts, involving patchwork and applique work by the Lambada tribe, and Warangal Rangasaipet Brassware, known for intricate embossing techniques using brass and bronze dating back to the Kakatiya era. The textile GI application is for Mahadevpur Tussar Silk Products, including the renowned 'Konda Patti' Tussar silk sarees made in Jayashankar Bhupalapally district using local silkworms.

items.title: Tamil Nadu tragedy: 9 workers killed; steel arch collapses at build site
items.story: NEW DELHI: Nine workers died and several others were injured when a steel arch collapsed at the Ennore Thermal Power construction site in Tamil Nadu on Tuesday. Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced ex gratia of Rs. 2 lakh from PMNRF for the next of kin of each deceased. The injured would be given Rs. 50,000. According to Dr J Radhakrishnan, chairman of the Tamil Nadu Generation and Distribution Corporation (TANGEDCO), the workers were from Assam and nearby areas. “There was an unfortunate incident at the Ennore Thermal Power construction site where a steel arch fell, resulting in nine deaths. One person is injured. BHEL officials are present at the spot,” he told reporters. Preliminary reports indicate that some of the injured suffered serious injuries and have been taken to Stanley Government Hospital in North Chennai. Police officials said the exact cause of the accident is still under investigation. “More than 10 others were seriously hurt in the collapse. Rescue operations are ongoing, and authorities have launched a detailed probe into the incident,” the Avadi Police Commissionerate said. More details awaited.

items.title: IND vs ENG: 'They were speaking loudly in Hindi' - Sachin Tendulkar reveals Shubman Gill-Rishabh Pant's genius mind game vs England
items.story:
Indian cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar has praised Rishabh Pant's unique and fearless shot-making, especially highlighting the left-hander's distinctive falling paddle sweep during his blistering 134 off 178 balls in the first Test at Headingley. Tendulkar called the stroke not an accident, but a product of sharp cricketing intelligence. "Rishabh's falling paddle sweep is not accidental. It is intentional and extremely clever. Going down with the shot allows him to get under the ball and scoop it over leg slip with control," Tendulkar wrote, praising Pant's calculated execution against spinner Shoaib Bashir.

Tendulkar also observed the subtle mind games being played between the wickets during the partnership between skipper Shubman Gill and Pant. "Also noticed something interesting during Bashir's spell. Shubman and Rishabh were speaking loudly in Hindi between deliveries. It wasn't just casual talk. They were playing mind games with the bowler, trying to disrupt his rhythm. These minor details may not appear on the scoreboard, but they can have a significant impact on the game," he added.

After Yashasvi Jaiswal’s aggressive 101 off 159 balls gave India a solid start, the Gill-Pant duo took charge and stitched together a commanding 209-run partnership. The stand put England’s inexperienced bowling attack under immense pressure, particularly during the second session of Day 1.

While Pant switched gears with flair, Gill held a steady tempo, setting the tone of the innings with his composed 147 off 227 balls. Gill fell short of a well-deserved 150, miscuing a flick off Shoaib Bashir to deep square leg. Pant, on the other hand, reached his century with a trademark one-handed six, but was later trapped LBW by Josh Tongue after shouldering arms to a ball that jagged back in. India’s innings folded for 471 after the departure of the two set batters.

items.title: 'Bihar Bandh': Rahul Gandhi, Tejashwi Yadav lead Mahagathbandhan protest over EC's voter roll move; key points
items.story:
Rahul Gandhi and Tejashwi Yadav led a "chakka jam" in Bihar, protesting the Election Commission's electoral roll revision ahead of assembly elections. The Grand Alliance march faced opposition from the BJP, who accused them of hooliganism and defended the EC's standard procedure.

On Wednesday, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi joined RJD's Tejashwi Yadav for "chakka jam" in Bihar over the Election Commission's special intensive revision of electoral roll just months ahead of the upcoming assembly elections. Rahul and Tejashwi, along with CPI's D Raja and CPM's Deepankar Bhattacharya, led the Grand Alliance march to the chief electoral officer's office. Rahul and other leaders were atop a vehicle during the protest march which started at Income Tax Golambar in Patna.

Tejashwi issued a call for "kranti" (revolution) against BJP and Nitish Kumar's "Godi Aayog," stating that they won't allow the "Dadagiri" of BJP and Nitish Kumar's 'Godi Aayog'. Bihar is the mother of democracy, and they want to finish democracy here, but the people of Bihar won't let this happen.

Rahul claimed that a similar attempt is being made in Bihar, as was done in Maharashtra. He alleged that during the Lok Sabha elections, new voters were added in constituencies where BJP won. When they asked for the voter list from the ECI, they did not receive it. Rahul warned that the Maharashtra elections were rigged, and they are trying to do the same in Bihar.

Meanwhile, the BJP accused the INDIA bloc of hooliganism under the guise of "Bihar Bandh," stating that they have no real issues or valid criticism against the NDA government. BJP leader Shahnawaz Hussain said that the Election Commission is their soft target.

BJP leader Ravishankar Prasad supported the poll body's exercise, emphasizing that only "citizens of India" are entitled to vote in the elections. He questioned whether the opposition wants "infiltrators" in the voter list, pointing out that Rohingyas get their names registered. Prasad insisted that the opposition is trying to create pressure.

The Election Commission, on a social media post, shared Article 326 of the Constitution, affirming that elections to the House of the People and Legislative Assemblies are based on adult suffrage. RJD and Grand Alliance supporters disrupted road and railway traffic across Bihar. The poll body stated that the ongoing exercise is a standard procedure to update the voter list before every election, as mandated by law.

items.title: Terror in Mali: 3 Indians, including 2 from Telugu states, abducted by al-Qaeda-linked militants; diamond cement factory staff taken hostage
items.story:
In a suspected terror attack in Mali, three Indian nationals, including two from the Telugu states, were abducted on July 1st from a cement factory in the city of Kayes. The abducted individuals are believed to have been taken by militants linked to the al-Qaeda-affiliated Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM). The kidnapped individuals include a senior employee from Maharashtra, Amareswar, a service engineer from Telangana, and Ramana, a foreman from Andhra Pradesh. These identities were confirmed by intelligence sources from Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.

The Diamond Cement factory, where the abduction occurred, is owned by the Hyderabad-based Prasaditya Group. The Indian embassy in Bamako, Mali's capital, is actively working with local authorities and the government of Mali to secure their release. They are also in regular contact with the families of the abducted men and the management of the factory. Following the incident, senior executives from Prasaditya Group traveled to Mali to coordinate with local law enforcement.

The Ministry of External Affairs of India has issued a statement condemning the act of violence and urging the Malian authorities to ensure the safe and swift release of the abductees. Although no group has officially claimed responsibility yet, security agencies suspect JNIM's involvement.

items.title: Donald Trump's $5 million Gold Card in demand! Indian professionals from these sectors show big interest; what happens to EB-5 visa?
items.story:
Donald Trump's proposed $5 million Gold Card visa program is generating significant buzz among Indian professionals, particularly those in the tech, finance, and healthcare sectors. Despite the lack of official launch and legislative support, the initiative has attracted considerable interest.

The proposed $5 million Gold Card visa scheme has received an exceptional response, attracting over 70,000 registrations shortly after the official website launched last month. The initiative specifically targets ultra-wealthy individuals and investors, rather than early-career or mid-level professionals.

The program has garnered particular attention from Indian professionals working in the US across technology, financial services, and medical sectors, primarily in the age bracket of 28-45 years. Whilst exploring existing immigration pathways like EB-5, these professionals are eagerly anticipating details about the Gold Card program specifics.

Indian nationals are making enquiries regarding Trump's Gold Card, according to Prachi Shah, who established and leads her namesake legal practice. "Most of the interest so far is coming from professionals in the tech, finance, and healthcare sectors," Shah said.

"Nearly 50% of interest is probably coming from the Middle East and a few wealthy countries, many of which are home to sizeable Indian diaspora populations who may also factor into the program's uptake," Sukanya Raman, country head, Davies & Associates, LLC, an immigration law firm told the financial daily.

Whilst initial interest from Indian High Net-worth Individuals appears substantial, it remains to be seen how many preliminary enquiries will result in actual applications, noted Keshav Singhania, who heads the private client division at Singhania & Co, a legal firm.

It is important to note that the Gold Card program presently lacks legislative support. Experts suggest that the program's publicity is primarily driven by marketing efforts rather than genuine demand.

The current online registration portal appears to collect only basic details without requiring substantial documentation, according to experts. "Without such filters, it is difficult to ascertain whether these registrants are genuinely interested and eligible, or simply curious," Shah said.

"We are urging caution to our clients until the legislation framework is in place and full details are made available," said Singhania.

The Trump Gold Card website presently displays a notification registration system for those interested in receiving updates about the program's launch.

Alexander Jovy, a lawyer, points out that the United States lacks both a legal structure and an official policy or executive order to initiate a Gold Card immigration program. "While the idea is gaining traction, it remains a proposal, not a legally recognized immigration pathway," he said.

Speculation suggests that the Gold Card might replace the current EB-5 visa program, spurring an increase in EB-5 applications due to its lower investment requirements. According to experts, the Gold Card and EB-5 programs can operate simultaneously as distinct schemes.

Whilst people await the official introduction of the Gold Card, numerous individuals are considering well-established alternatives such as EB-5, H-1B, or National Interest Waiver programs.

Rajneesh Pathak, who established Global North Residency and Citizenship, told ET that his firm, which specializes in immigration and investment advisory services, is receiving enquiries from clients regarding how the Gold Card might affect the EB-5 program's future. "We are advising our clients that at this stage EB-5 is live and kicking ...also Gold Card can be a success only if it comes with no tax on global income," Pathak said.

items.title: Watch: Supporters of BJP, NCP (SP) clash inside Maharashtra assembly premises; viral video shows heated face-off
items.story: A video capturing a confrontation between supporters of BJP MLA Gopichand Padalkar and NCP (Sharad Pawar) MLA Jitendra Awhad inside Maharashtra's Vidhan Bhavan has gone viral, raising significant security concerns. Filmed near the main staircase and lobby, the video shows both parties exchanging blows before onlookers intervened. This altercation occurred a day after Padalkar and Awhad were filmed in a heated argument outside the legislature premises. In that earlier footage, the two MLAs were seen exchanging sharp words, reportedly after Awhad alleged that Padalkar slammed a car door at him. Responding to the incident, Awhad questioned the safety inside Vidhan Bhavan, stating, "If MLAs are not safe even here, what's the point of being a public representative?" Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis condemned the scuffle, describing it as a serious breach of Vidhan Bhavan's dignity and called for stringent action. Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Uddhav Thackeray also commented on the viral video, alleging that "goondaism has reached Vidhan Bhavan." Security officials confirmed the detention of two individuals seen in the video. Assembly Speaker Rahul Narvekar has ordered a detailed investigation into the incident, promising strict action based on the footage. The video has sparked outrage across party lines, with calls for tighter control over entry passes and visitor movement within the legislature complex.

items.title: Scary scene! Shubman Gill takes nasty blow to the head, Rishabh Pant's reaction goes viral – WATCH
items.story: During the second Test against England, Indian captain Shubman Gill was struck on the head while fielding, causing immediate concern. The incident happened during Ravindra Jadeja's over when Harry Brook played a powerful drive that hit Gill on the head. Shubman Gill, visibly in pain, called for the physiotherapist after showing his injury to teammate Rishabh Pant. Fortunately, after receiving on-field treatment, Gill was able to continue playing. This incident occurred shortly after Gill achieved an emotional milestone, having received congratulatory messages from his parents for his record-breaking double century in the match. Gill became the first Indian captain to score a double century in England and set a record as the first Indian batter to hit a double ton in Tests outside Asia since Virat Kohli's 200 in 2016. His score of 269 surpassed Kohli's previous record for the highest score by an Indian Test captain and also beat Sachin Tendulkar's record for the highest score by an Indian in Tests outside Asia. The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) shared a video capturing Gill's emotional reaction to his parents' messages, emphasizing his deep connection with his father, who inspired him to play cricket. Gill’s innings helped India achieve their highest Test total in England in 18 years, scoring 587 runs.

items.title: Model Ruchi Gujjar slaps ‘So Long Valley’ producer Karan Singh at movie premiere, files FIR over Rs 23L film deal fraud
items.story: Mumbai Police have registered an FIR against Karan Singh, the producer of 'So Long Valley,' for allegedly defrauding model Ruchi Gujjar of Rs 23 lakh. Gujjar claims Singh promised her a stake in a television movie project, including profit share and on-screen credit, but the project never materialized, and the money was not returned. During the movie's premiere on Friday night, viral videos captured Gujjar slapping Singh on stage. The FIR was filed at Oshiwara police station under various cheating-related sections. The model's lawyer stated that a second FIR would be lodged at Amboli police station against Singh for allegedly assaulting Gujjar. 'So Long Valley' is a Hindi-language crime thriller featuring Tridha Choudhury and Vikram Kochhar.

items.title: Telangana factory tragedy: Toll rises to 42 at Sigachi; 8 still missing
items.story:
The death toll in the Sigachi Industries factory explosion in Sangareddy, Telangana, has risen to 42 after Jitendra Kumar, a 30-year-old worker from Uttar Pradesh, succumbed to his injuries. The explosion, which occurred on June 30, has also led to the identification of another victim, Chikkan Singh from Madhya Pradesh, through DNA analysis. Eight individuals are still missing following this tragic incident. Out of the 33 people initially injured, 14 have been discharged, while 18 continue to receive medical treatment in various local hospitals. The company reported that 61 of the 143 people present during the explosion were unharmed. 

The explosion severely damaged the dryer unit of the factory, and recovery efforts have uncovered 44 body parts, including legs and fingers. These remains are being sent for DNA analysis to the Telangana Forensic Science Laboratory. The search and recovery operations are being conducted by SDRF, NDRF, and HYDRAA teams. The forensic team is facing difficulties due to many body parts being severely burned and reduced to ashes, complicating the identification process. 

Efforts to clear the debris continue, and arrangements are being made to transport the identified bodies to their respective hometowns.

items.title: K Chandrashekhar Rao admitted for standard tests, no serious health concerns: K T Rama Rao
items.story: BRS working president KT Rama Rao clarified that former Chief Minister K Chandrashekhar Rao was admitted to a private hospital in Hyderabad on Thursday evening for routine medical check-ups. KTR assured the public that it was a precautionary measure, addressing concerns about KCR's health. He emphasized that the hospitalization was a preventive measure to monitor KCR's diabetes and low sodium levels, dismissing public speculation of any serious health issues. KTR stressed that there is no cause for concern regarding his father's health.

items.title: Gold as 'new barometer': RBI Guv says gold prices reflect global uncertainty as crude did earlier; warns of global equity market correction
items.story:
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra on Friday said gold prices may now be acting as a fresh barometer of global uncertainty, similar to how crude oil once reflected geopolitical risks, even as he cautioned of a potential correction in global equity markets.

Speaking at the Kautilya Economic Conclave 2025, Malhotra noted that despite widespread fiscal stress, oil prices have remained range-bound in the face of geopolitical tensions, which in earlier decades would have triggered sharp spikes, PTI reported.

"Despite geopolitical tensions that would have sent oil prices soaring in an earlier decade, they (oil prices) have been very range bound. This could be due to a decline in oil intensity in GDP, not just in India, but across the world. Perhaps gold prices now are showing the kind of movement that oil used to that is acting as a barometer of global uncertainty," the RBI Governor said, PTI quoted.

Malhotra further observed that the current global trade policy environment could hurt growth in some economies. He also warned that stock markets, led by technology stocks in recent rallies, might be getting complacent.

"Correction might be in the offing," he remarked, adding that fiscal stress is evident in almost every major economy.

Earlier this week, the RBI had left the key interest rate unchanged at 5.5 per cent with a neutral monetary policy stance, noting that while the global economy has been more resilient than expected, the outlook remains clouded.

Meanwhile, spot gold edged higher on Friday to $3,867 per ounce and is poised for a seventh consecutive weekly gain. On Thursday, the metal had retreated from a record high of $3,896.9 per ounce to close at $3,856.6 per ounce.

items.title: 'Too hard on brain': Flight phobia grips travellers after Ahmedabad Air India crash; bookings drop & cancellations spike
items.story:
Following the Air India plane crash in Ahmedabad, a wave of panic has surged among flyers in India, leading to increased anxiety and fear. This incident has caused a spike in therapy requests, flight cancellations, and a preference for specific aircraft types. The crash footage has triggered insomnia, panic attacks, and obsessive flight tracking, impacting the travel industry with booking declines and cancellations. 
 
 'I'm bloody terrified currently,' this is how people are reacting when it comes to taking flights after the Air India plane crash in Ahmedabad on June 12. The flying anxiety has skyrocketed among flyers after the deadly incident that claimed 242 lives, with many taking experts' help to overcome the 'flying fear.' A wave of panic has gripped flyers and led to a sharp surge in fear-of-flying therapy requests, ticket cancellations, and unusually specific questions about aircraft types. 
 
 Dinesh K, a retired Indian Air Force wing commander and founder of Cockpit Vista, told Reuters that demand for his $500 therapy course has exploded since the Air India flight crash incident. "Fear of flying is typically to do with things happening on an aeroplane - the sounds, motion, vibrations ...exposure therapy is the only solution," Dinesh told Reuters. His centre used to receive about 10 enquiries a month. Since the crash, it's logged over 100. 
 
 Chilling videos of the Dreamliner bursting into flames shortly after take-off have gone viral across social media. It's not just fuelling fear, it's inducing insomnia, panic attacks, obsessive checking of flight trackers, and even refusal to let loved ones fly, say mental health professionals, according to Reuters. Some people are unable to focus on daily life while a loved one is flying, said psychologist Pankti Gohel, describing cases of "debilitating anxiety". 
 
 According to Google Trends, searches for "flying fear" in India peaked the day after the crash and remain high. 
 
 The impact is being felt across the travel industry. Tour operators report a dramatic drop in bookings and a spike in cancellations, especially on Air India routes. 
 
 "Flight bookings are down by 15–20%. Cancellations are up by 30–40%," Ravi Gosain, president of the Indian association of tour operators, told Reuters. Even more telling: Travellers are now filtering bookings by aircraft type, actively avoiding Dreamliners and Boeing planes. "People don't want to hear about Dreamliners," he added. 
 
 For many flyers in India, the crash and its terrifying visuals were a psychological tipping point. While flying remains statistically one of the safest modes of transport, with only 1.87 accidents per million departures in 2023, emotions, not stats, are now driving decisions.

items.title: EC must stop SIR, says opposition; calls it ‘exercise of exclusion’
items.story: Opposition parties in India are raising concerns about the Election Commission's special intensive revision of Bihar's electoral rolls, alleging it could disenfranchise marginalized communities. They question the potential exclusion of 66 lakh people and criticize the rejection of certain documents. The Election Commission defends the process, urging parties to submit claims and objections during the designated period. Ahead of a Supreme Court hearing on the special intensive revision (SIR) of Bihar's electoral rolls, the opposition INDIA bloc on Sunday alleged it is an "exercise of exclusion", questioning data released by the Election Commission after SIR's first phase that 66 lakh people might be excluded on grounds such as "deceased, permanently shifted or untraceable." Congress functionary Abhishek Singhvi said the EC should not show "institutional arrogance" with INDIA bloc parties from Bihar urging the poll panel to stop SIR as it will result in "large-scale disenfranchisement of poor and marginalized sections". "Recent pressers of EC and refusal to accept Aadhaar, EPIC, and ration card as valid documents clearly point towards the fact that the entire SIR process is a citizenship verification process," he alleged. EC responded by asking why opposition parties are trying to create "an impression that the draft list is the final list, which it is not, as per SIR order." It said it is not able to understand the big fuss now, when a full one month period from Aug 1-Sept 1 is available to point out wrongful inclusion or wrongful exclusion of any name. "Why don't the parties ask their not 1.6 lakh booth level agents to submit claims and objections from Aug 1-Sept 1?" it asked. Gearing up to step up the protests both inside and outside Parliament, Congress, RJD, CPM and CPI (ML)-Liberation leaders at a presser expressed fear that many more people will be excluded from rolls during the verification process ahead due to lack of documents like birth, caste and domicile certificates. RJD MP Manoj Jha said the whole SIR process is based on presumptions. "Clearly, opacity has become the hallmark of EC functioning," Jha said. "There is no time or option for the right to appeal for people who will be excluded in the whole process. There are also numerous reports of people found alive who are included in the dead list," he alleged. On the number of deceased, CPI (ML)-Liberation Dipankar Bhattacharya said, "Does this mean that in just six months, around 22 lakh people have passed away? So, does this mean the EC's January 2025 summary revision was a flop?"

items.title: HYD@25 TOI summit to kick off in Hyderabad today; CM Revanth Reddy to deliver keynote
items.story: Hyderabad: The Times of India is bringing together top visionaries, policymakers, and industry leaders for HYD@25: Hyderabad Ready to Leap, an exclusive summit to chart the city's roadmap to 2050. The event will be held on Monday at Trident, Hitec City, from 4.30pm onwards, and entry is by invitation only. Chief minister A Revanth Reddy will deliver the keynote speech, with IT and industries minister D Sridhar Babu also addressing the gathering. Among the notable speakers are Jayesh Ranjan, special chief secretary for tourism, culture and sports; AV Ranganath, HYDRAA commissioner; Charu Sinha, ADGP-CID & women safety; and Dr D Nageshwar Reddy of AIG Hospitals. Leaders from innovation and enterprise, including Naga Bharath Daka (Skyroot Aerospace), Rohit Chennamaneni (Darwinbox), Sai D Prasad (Bharat Biotech), and actor-producer Nani, will add diverse perspectives. The conclave, powered by Renova Hospitals, with Shapoorji Pallonji and Bower School of Entrepreneurship as associate sponsors, will debate Hyderabad's evolution into a world-class metropolis with discussions spanning technology, healthcare, law, urban planning, and culture.

items.title: Coming home to heal: Rise of returning doctors from US & UK reshaping Hyderabad's healthcare
items.story: In a quiet but profound trend, a growing number of Indian doctors, who once pursued careers in the United States and the United Kingdom, are now making their way back home, bringing with them decades of global experience and a renewed commitment to serve their country. Hyderabad, with its booming healthcare infrastructure and growing demand for specialized care, has emerged as a hub for these returnees. Many of them are not only joining leading hospitals but are also setting up their own healthcare institutions. At the heart of this movement is a deep sense of purpose—personal, professional, and patriotic. Some doctors are drawn back by the desire to care for aging parents, while others return driven by a vision to contribute to India’s rapidly evolving medical landscape. The city is now home to the Returning Doctors Association, an informal network of over 150 physicians who have resettled here after stints abroad. Dr. Kavitha Gone, a senior nephrologist who returned from the UK after 16 years, is one of the key voices in this community. She mentions that the association acts as a support system, where returning doctors share experiences, guidance, and advice due to differing medical protocols across countries. Dr. Kavitha spent six years working in a corporate hospital upon her return before launching her own practice, emphasizing the transition as challenging but rewarding. Several returnees have founded hospitals of their own, such as Dr. Venkatesh Movva, a pioneer in regenerative medicine and founder of RegenOrthoSport. After nearly a decade in the US, he returned to impact healthcare in India, citing the over-reliance on surgery for minor injuries in India as a key concern. Dr. Karthik Mikkilineni, a vascular surgeon, returned post-Covid to bridge gaps in clinical protocols, noting rushed surgeries and tests without sufficient evaluation. Interestingly, recent years have seen a stronger trend of repatriation from the US. Dr. Venkata Swamy, founder of Roma Hospital and a trauma orthopedic specialist, returned from the UK twice, with missions rooted in community care, setting up hospitals in both his village and the city.

items.title: 'Extended maintenance task': Air India Delhi to Washington flight halts mid-way; passengers disembarked
items.story: An Air India flight, AI103, traveling from Delhi to Washington, DC, was forced to make an unscheduled stop in Vienna, Austria, on July 2 due to a maintenance issue that was detected during a planned refueling stop. The issue required immediate attention, and as a result, the continuation of the flight to Washington was canceled, and all passengers were disembarked in Vienna. An Air India spokesperson explained to the news agency ANI that the routine aircraft checks uncovered the maintenance task, necessitating rectification before the aircraft could continue. This incident also led to the cancellation of the return leg, flight AI104, from Washington, DC to Delhi via Vienna. Affected passengers were rebooked on alternative flights or given full refunds.

items.title: Uttarakhand CM Dhami celebrates women entrepreneurs driving local economy, says women, youth, and culture will drive Uttarakhand's next 25 years
items.story: Reflecting on 25 years since Uttarakhand's formation in 2000, Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami emphasized the pivotal role women played in reshaping the state's economy. In an exclusive interview with the Times of India, Uttarakhand’s CM, Pushkar Singh Dhami highlighted women becoming the backbone of Uttarakhand’s grassroots entrepreneurship. "I have visited all 13 districts and met with women involved in various enterprises. We organised 'Nari Shakti Vandan' festivals and I saw first-hand the talent and strength they possess," he said. Dhami noted women’s contribution in the production of millet-based products, temple prasad, traditional embroidery, locally-made toys, and sustainable goods that are both preserving cultural identity and generating income. He added that these efforts are creating self-reliant communities and enabling women to lead economically independent lives. Reaffirming Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s confidence in the state’s future, Dhami recalled his speech from his 2021 Kedarnath visit. "When the Prime Minister visited Kedarnath in November 2021, the words came spontaneously from his mouth: 'The third decade of the 21st century will be the decade of Uttarakhand.'” Dhami backed the state’s growth trajectory with data as Uttarakhand ranked first in NITI Aayog's 2024 Sustainable Development Goals Index. The unemployment rate in the state has seen a 4.5% drop, and the state's financial management was ranked second among smaller Indian states. "These figures are not just statistics, but proof of how Uttarakhand is moving forward with a clear vision," Dhami said. Chief Minister also boasted about the state's transformation into a favorable film shooting destination for aspiring filmmakers. "Hundreds of films are now being shot annually. We have streamlined permissions and improved locations to attract filmmakers." He emphasized that better infrastructure is central to this growth. "When connectivity improves, everything improves. Filmmakers are coming. Travel between Dehradun and Haridwar will soon be just two hours," he added, highlighting the state’s push on highway and transport infrastructure. Looking ahead, Dhami said his government is committed to ensuring that this momentum reaches even the remotest parts of the state. "Our women, our youth, our culture, and our mountains will together shape a developed and empowered Uttarakhand for the next 25 years."

items.title: IND vs ENG: When will Team India begin preparations in Manchester for fourth Test?
items.story:
Following a narrow defeat at Lord's, Shubman Gill and the Indian team have arrived in Manchester for a crucial fourth Test against England, starting July 23. With England leading the series 2-1, India faces a must-win situation. Preparations include optional and full training sessions, with media interactions scheduled to address the pressure and strategies for a comeback. 

After a heartbreaking defeat at Lord’s, where India narrowly lost by 22 runs in a tense final session, captain Shubman Gill and his team have arrived in Manchester with eyes firmly set on the fourth Test at Old Trafford. With England leading the five-match series 2-1, the upcoming clash starting 23 July has become a must-win for India to stay alive in the contest and push the series into a decider at The Oval.

As per the current schedule, India will begin their preparations with an optional training session on 20 July at 1:30 PM. This session is open only for visual media coverage, with no player or support staff scheduled to speak to the press. 

On 21 July, the team will undergo a full training session from 9:30 AM to 12:30 PM. A media interaction is expected around 12:45 PM, where a player or a member of the coaching staff will address the media and provide insights into the team’s mindset ahead of the crucial match.

India will return for another optional training session on 22 July at 1:30 PM, and this time, a media interaction is scheduled at approximately 1 PM, ahead of the practice. The Lord’s Test result was a bitter pill to swallow for India, who had fought hard in the fourth innings only to fall short in the final hour. With just two matches left, the pressure is mounting on the visitors to level the series. A strong showing in Manchester will be key as India look to bounce back, correct key mistakes, and keep their hopes of a memorable series win alive.

items.title: Pilot falls ill before takeoff, IndiGo Delhi-Pune flight delayed by 4.5 hours: 'Appropriate medical assistance was provided'
items.story: A Delhi-to-Pune IndiGo flight was delayed by four-and-a-half hours after the pilot scheduled to operate the aircraft fell ill just before takeoff. Flight 6E 2262, which was set to depart from Delhi at 6:00 am, had to return to the bay as the pilot felt unwell. IndiGo confirmed that the crew member received immediate medical attention and an alternative crew was arranged, leading to the delay. The flight eventually took off at 10:27 am. Additionally, the delay was further impacted by temporary airspace restrictions at Pune Airport. On the same day, another incident occurred where an Air India commander collapsed in the cockpit in Bengaluru before a flight to Delhi.

items.title: Telangana: Kids as young as 2 addicted to spiked toddy
items.story: In Telangana, the adulteration of toddy, a traditional alcoholic beverage, has led to a disturbing trend involving children as young as two years old. The issue came to light after a recent incident where seven adults died and many others were hospitalized due to consuming spiked toddy. Doctors have reported an increase in cases of children showing withdrawal symptoms such as seizures, fever, and sleeplessness. This is attributed to parents and grandparents in rural areas giving toddy to children to help them sleep, unaware that it is often laced with sedatives like alprazolam (Xanax), diazepam (Valium), and chlordiazepoxide (Librium). The problem has worsened since the pandemic, with four to five cases reported each month. Children as young as seven or eight are facing addiction issues, causing significant harm to their developing bodies, according to Dr. Srinivas SRRY, head of the psychiatry department at Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Hospital in Warangal.

items.title: "Her BBL smelled like a trash bag": Stefon Diggs responds to bizarre "smelly BBL" claim hours after shutting down Cardi B breakup rumors
items.story: Stefon Diggs has denied the claims that he described Cardi B as "smelly" due to her BBL. The rumors emerged after Cardi B removed pictures from her Instagram, which led fans to speculate about a breakup. Despite the rumors and cryptic social media posts, the couple appears to be strong, with Diggs posting a video of them working out together. A few days ago, a quote went viral suggesting Diggs commented on Cardi B being "smelly because of her BBL," which has since been debunked by Diggs himself, who responded "Cap" under the post on Instagram. Cardi B also made some controversial posts on X, which some fans believe were in response to the breakup rumors or potentially directed at Nicki Minaj. Recently, Cardi B publicly apologized to her music label for being difficult about releasing a song, which she initially did not want to drop but later acknowledged its success.

items.title: ‘I came with toys, left with heartbreak’: Mystery surrounds Russian woman found in Gokarna cave; Israeli father denied reunion
items.story: Dror Goldstein, an Israeli musician, traveled to India in hopes of reuniting with his daughters, Prema, 6, and Ama, 4, who were found living in a cave near Gokarna with their mother, Nina Kutina, a Russian national. Upon arrival, Dror faced legal challenges that prevented him from seeing his children, who are now in a Foreigners Detention Centre. It was a minor landslide on July 11 at Ramatirtha Hills of Gokarna that led local police to discover the family living in the cave. Nina has been residing in India since 2017, initially on a business visa, and chose a life away from conventional living in the forests of Gokarna. Dror and Nina met in Goa in 2017 and lived together for a few years before separating, but Dror still visited his children regularly. After authorities intervened, Nina and her daughters were moved to a Foreigners Detention Centre in Dibburu, Tumakuru. Dror traveled there with gifts for his daughters but was denied visitation without official permission from the Foreigners Regional Registration Office. Dror is now in Bengaluru to start the legal process for visitation rights. He hopes to see his children soon but respects Nina's choices and would not take the children to Israel without her consent. Dror remains in Bengaluru, awaiting permission to see his daughters while considering the complexities of their life situation.

items.title: ITC announces Rs 20,000cr investment push: Focus on FMCG margin boost; Puri sees demand rebound ahead
items.story: ITC Ltd. has announced plans to invest Rs 20,000 crore across its various business sectors over the next five to six years. This investment follows the inauguration of eight new manufacturing facilities. The company, which has already invested Rs 4,500 crore in capital expenditures over the last two years, is also considering potential acquisitions to drive growth. The announcement was made by Chairman Sanjiv Puri during the company's 114th annual general meeting, which was held virtually. ITC is focusing on boosting the margins in its FMCG sector, aiming to improve them by 80-100 basis points annually. Puri mentioned that the company is looking at potential acquisitions to align with its strategic goals and enhance its growth trajectory. ITC has made notable acquisitions in recent years, including the frozen food company Prasuma and organic packaged staples brand 24 Mantra Organic. The company is also expanding into areas such as horticulture and integrating AI across its value chain to improve operations and market reach. ITC's initiatives are part of its strategy to capitalize on emerging trends like health and wellness and to sustain its growth momentum.

items.title: Grief, boardroom and the game of succession: Inside family feud tearing through Sona Comstar after Sunjay Kapur’s death
items.story: In a high-stakes corporate drama riddled with grief, suspicion, and boardroom intrigue, Sona Comstar held its Annual General Meeting (AGM) on July 25 - brushing aside an emotional plea from Rani Kapur, mother of Sunjay Kapur, to delay the proceedings. What unfolded wasn’t just a shareholder meeting, but a glimpse into a brewing succession war cloaked in mourning. The clash, steeped in a "saas-bahu" powerplay, erupted barely weeks after the sudden death of Sunjay Kapur, the company’s former chairman, in London under what Rani Kapur described as "highly suspicious and unexplained circumstances." Rani Kapur, widow of Sona Group founder Surinder Kapur and a self-proclaimed major shareholder, asked the board to postpone the AGM by two weeks. Her reason? The family was still reeling from Sunjay’s death and critical decisions about control and legacy were being rushed through behind her back. In her letter to the board and shareholders, Rani called the AGM "insensitive," accusing unnamed individuals of exploiting the family's tragedy to "wrest control" of the company and install their preferred nominees. Among her most strident objections: the proposed appointment of Sunjay’s wife, Priya Sachdev Kapur, as a non-executive director, a move she said she never authorized, alleging coercion, misrepresentation, and exclusion from the decision-making process. "I was emotionally shattered, and I was coerced into signing documents I was never shown," she wrote, alleging she was kept in the dark about key company decisions. Sona Comstar didn’t blink. In a sharply worded response, the company said the AGM was conducted in "full legal and regulatory compliance." It dismissed Rani Kapur’s objections, stating that she hadn’t been a shareholder "since at least 2019." According to the company’s filings, it was Sunjay Kapur, not Rani, who was declared the sole beneficial owner of the RK Family Trust, which holds stake via the promoter firm Aureus Investments Pvt Ltd (AIPL). Rani Kapur’s claim of being the majority shareholder by virtue of her late husband’s will was flatly rejected. "For clarity, the company confirms that no documents have been signed or obtained from Rani Kapur following Sunjay Kapur’s death," Sona Comstar said, dismissing allegations of coercion. At the heart of the feud is the rise of Priya Sachdev Kapur, the glamorous third wife of Sunjay and a former model-businesswoman, who has now been formally inducted into the board. Despite being recently widowed, Priya has swiftly moved to claim her space in the boardroom — a decision that was greenlit by shareholders and the company’s Nomination and Remuneration Committee. The company insisted she had submitted all necessary statutory documents and was not disqualified under any law. Meanwhile, the board also appointed Jeffrey Mark Overly as the new chairman, just days after Sunjay's death, a move that further fueled speculation of a hasty transition orchestrated with surgical precision. The 53-year-old industrialist and polo patron died suddenly on June 12 in Windsor, England, after collapsing mid-match at the prestigious Guards Polo Club. He reportedly swallowed a bee during the polo match that triggered a fatal heart attack. Sona Comstar, the Gurugram-based auto components giant he chaired, confirmed the death in a formal statement, while the polo club noted he "became unwell" during play at its elite Smith’s Lawn grounds — a venue long associated with Britain’s royal family. Kapur, who owned and captained the Aureus polo team, had travelled to England for a summer season of matches. The son of industrialist Surinder Kapur, Sunjay took charge of Sona Comstar in 2015, steering it toward global expansion, particularly in EV systems and components. Under his leadership, the company grew to operate across India, China, Mexico, and the US, employing over 4,600 people. On the day of his death, he had posted a tribute on social media mourning victims of the Air India crash in Ahmedabad, a poignant final message from a man whose own passing would soon rock his company and family. Sunjay’s personal life had long made headlines. In 2003, he married actress Karisma Kapoor. They had two children, Samaira and Kiaan, before a highly publicised divorce in 2016. He had earlier been briefly married to fashion designer Nandita Mahtani. In 2017, Sunjay married Priya Sachdev, a former model and entrepreneur. She survives him along with their young son, Azarias, and his two older children. Sunjay Kapur left behind a grieving but deeply divided family — and a company now at the center of a bitter inheritance battle. "Certain people are now misrepresenting themselves as family nominees and the largest shareholders without my consent,” Rani alleged in her letter, which was also marked to Sebi, escalating the fight beyond boardroom walls. Rani Kapur’s legal counsel has hinted that further action could be on the horizon if her pleas continue to be ignored. In her words: "If you choose to move forward without conferring with me, I will assume this is a conscious betrayal of the family legacy.” What was meant to be a procedural corporate event has now turned into a public spectacle — one part grief, one part power struggle, and all parts Shakespearean. And as the dust settles from the AGM, one thing is clear: this family feud is far from over.

items.title: Vanessa Bryant extends her warm gesture on Ciara’s cheerful post for husband Russell Wilson featuring the kids
items.story: Vanessa Bryant expressed her support for Russell Wilson's family by commenting on an Instagram post by Ciara, Wilson's wife. The post showed Ciara and their children cheering for Wilson during his training camp. This gesture underscores the close relationship between Vanessa and Ciara, who have supported each other through significant life events, including the passing of Kobe Bryant. Their families maintain a strong friendship, often celebrating milestones and spending vacations together. Vanessa's warm reaction, marked by heart emojis, stood out among the comments on Ciara's post. The friendship between Vanessa Bryant and Ciara has been evident through their mutual support during challenging times. After Kobe Bryant's death, Ciara and Russell Wilson supported Vanessa and her family. Vanessa also honored Kobe's legacy by releasing a collection of apparel and accessories, with Ciara being one of the first to wear the Mamba sweatshirt. The two families have shared many joyful moments, including vacations and special occasions, with Vanessa even referring to Ciara and Russell as her children's uncle and aunt.

items.title: Patrick Mahomes' mom Randi shares a tearful truth as her youngest steps into a new world
items.story: Randi Mahomes is experiencing a mix of emotions as her youngest daughter, Mia, prepares for high school. Randi is focused on equipping Mia with resilience and the wisdom to navigate challenges while prioritizing her emotional well-being. Randi's message resonates with parents as she balances pride with the understanding that her role is evolving into one of mentorship. As the mother of NFL superstar Patrick Mahomes, Randi Mahomes is no stranger to life in the spotlight—but right now, it’s her youngest daughter Mia who’s at the center of her heart. With Mia preparing to begin high school, Randi is entering a deeply personal new phase of motherhood—one that’s as thrilling as it is emotional. It’s a familiar moment for many parents: the bittersweet pride of watching your child grow up. And for Randi, it’s stirring a wave of reflection, vulnerability, and love. Randi isn’t just a supportive mom in the bleachers anymore—she’s focused on helping Mia build the inner strength to navigate real-world situations. As Mia steps into high school, the stakes go beyond athletics and academics; it’s about becoming emotionally resilient. “I want her to be strong and resilient,” Randi shared in a recent social media post, showing just how deeply she’s thinking about her daughter’s emotional foundation. There’s a clear desire to arm Mia with the courage to face challenges while staying soft at heart. Randi’s message reflects more than encouragement—it’s protection in the form of wisdom. She wants Mia to thrive but also recognize when something isn't right. “But I also want her to know she doesn't have to stick around in situations that are unhealthy either,” she wrote, a line that resonated with many parents online. It’s the kind of nuanced advice that grows with you—especially during the difficult teen years. Randi’s emotional transparency reminds readers that parenting doesn’t stop at rules and routines—it evolves into life mentorship. There’s something quietly powerful about Randi’s honesty—she’s not pretending this transition is easy. Watching Mia walk into high school feels like both an arrival and a departure: a step toward independence, but also a small goodbye to the little girl she once was. For Randi, that shift is emotional. It forces her to acknowledge that Mia’s choices, friendships, and battles will increasingly be her own. Even as she lifts her daughter up, Randi is learning to let go—an act that’s brave in itself. It’s the quiet struggle of motherhood that’s rarely shown: watching from the sidelines and trusting your child to carry the values you’ve tried to instill. Her vulnerability strikes a chord with anyone who has ever had to give their child space to grow. And in sharing this moment publicly, she’s invited others to sit in that space of mixed emotions with her. Mia’s entrance into high school is more than a family milestone—it marks a shift in how Randi sees herself as a mother. The hands-on, always-there parenting of the early years is now transforming into emotional coaching from a step back. She’s teaching her daughter how to be independent, but also when to walk away from people or places that dim her light. That balance between strength and self-protection is at the heart of Randi’s message. In a world that often pressures girls to “tough it out,” Randi’s words act as a much-needed permission slip to prioritize emotional safety. By acknowledging both her pride and her fear, she’s showing that it’s okay for parents to feel uncertain, too. Her post wasn’t just a note to Mia—it was a moment of connection with every parent going through a similar phase. Because growing up is hard—but watching someone you love grow up can be even harder.

items.title: CAG report flags T’s rising deficits, financial strain in 1st quarter
items.story: Hyderabad: Telangana's financial position in the first quarter of the fiscal year appears strained, according to the latest report from the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG). The state is grappling with high deficits and lower-than-expected revenue collections. As of June, the state recorded a revenue deficit of ₹10,582 crore—meaning it spent that much more than it earned. This is a sharp contrast to the budget's projection of a ₹2,738 crore surplus. The fiscal deficit, which measures how much the government needs to borrow to meet all its expenses, stood at ₹20,266 crore. That's already 37.5% of the annual target of ₹54,009 crore—just within the first three months. The primary deficit—which is the fiscal deficit minus interest payments on past loans—reached ₹13,493 crore, which is nearly 39% of the ₹34,640 crore planned for the year. Income: Far behind projections. The state's total receipts in the first quarter—including ₹20,266 crore raised through borrowings—stood at ₹57,499 crore. This is just 21% of the ₹2.84 lakh crore projected for the full year. Around 24% of this income came from the Centre in the form of Telangana's share of central taxes and grants. Interest payments alone amounted to ₹6,772 crore—about 35% of the annual allocation of ₹19,369 crore—raising concerns about the state's ability to manage future debt. Salaries, pensions, and subsidies dominate spending. On the expenditure side, a significant portion of the budget has already been used up. On salaries and wages, ₹11,608 crore was spent, which is nearly 35% of the annual ₹44,478 crore target. On pensions, ₹4,572 crore (34.9% of the ₹13,109 crore estimate) was used and subsidies, mainly for free electricity, cost ₹5,932 crore—over 36% of the ₹16,345 crore set aside for the year. What do these deficits mean? A revenue deficit means the state's income isn't enough to cover its regular expenses like salaries and subsidies. A fiscal deficit shows the overall gap between total income and total expenditure, including capital and interest costs. A primary deficit isolates current borrowing needs, leaving out the burden of interest on older debts. Key revenue figures: Tax revenue: ₹35,721 crore (20.4% of the ₹1.75 lakh crore target) GST collections: ₹12,622 crore (out of ₹59,074 crore projected) Stamp and registration fees: ₹3,712 crore (19.5% of ₹19,087 crore) State excise duty: ₹4,595 crore (16.6% of ₹27,623 crore) Sales tax: ₹8,466 crore (22.6% of the ₹37,463 crore estimate).

items.title: Age no barrier: 3 senior citizens, including 2 lawyers, apply for MBBS in Tamil Nadu after clearing NEET 2025
items.story: In Tamil Nadu, several older individuals, including lawyers and other professionals, have applied for MBBS admissions after clearing NEET 2025. While the National Medical Commission (NMC) has no age restrictions, officials are grappling with document discrepancies and debating whether a special quota for government school students should extend to older graduates. Three senior citizens, aged 68, 67, and 60, including two lawyers, cleared the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) 2025 and applied for MBBS admissions in Tamil Nadu. State selection committee officials noted that at least 25 people, including professionals such as dentists, nurses, homeopaths, siddha practitioners, lab technicians, and lawyers, above the age of 35, are competing for the undergraduate medical and dental courses. The National Medical Commission, the apex body regulating medical education in India, has stated there is no bar on age or the number of attempts to appear for the qualifying examination. Merit in NEET is the sole criterion for admissions to medical or dental colleges across India. "This year, we see many graduates and professionals aspiring for a medical or dental seat. It's the highest number of middle-age and older applicants we have seen since 2017," said a senior official. They may not have adequate scores to compete against younger candidates, but some have secured marks that could secure them a seat under the 69% reservation category and allow them to study medicine at a subsidized cost at a government college or free of cost at a private college. All three senior citizens applied for admission under a special quota, where 7.5% of seats are reserved for students from government schools. Under this scheme, students pursue medicine in government or private colleges free of cost. The government pays the fees and takes care of the boarding charges. While the government has not set a ceiling on age or attempts, officials are seeing technical hitches as not all documents match the requirements. "Most of them have documents that may be equal but don't match requirements mentioned in the prospectus," an official said. "Some people have given pre-university course scores instead of a Class XII mark sheet. In some cases, a Class XII subject is mentioned as natural sciences; instead of biology, botany or zoology. We don't know if we must allow them to appear for counseling, reject their applications, or give them time to get equivalence certificates," he added. Furthermore, the core debate among officials is whether this special quota should extend to all graduates, regardless of age. While officials are discussing this with health secretary P Senthilkumar and consulting legal departments, educationalists and counselors are raising alarms. "This quota was introduced only because there was no level playing field in NEET. Unlike other students, government school students cannot afford coaching in private tutorials," said Dr. Karthikeyan R, who runs Aatrupadai Foundation, an NGO that offers free NEET coaching. "Asking them to compete with professionals, who have access to private training institutes, is unfair," he said. Student counselors such as Manickavel Arumugam argue that the state cannot give fee subsidies either. "Will a senior citizen be able to complete the strenuous course? Will they be able to work 24-hour shifts during house surgery?" he said. "If people quit the course in between, they must be asked to pay a fine of 10 lakh and the entire non-subsidized course fee," he added.

items.title: Evening news wrap: SC refuses to stay Bihar voter revision, Congress hits out at Shashi Tharoor over Emergency remark; and more
items.story:
On Thursday, significant developments unfolded across various sectors including the judiciary, politics, and international relations. The Supreme Court of India decided not to halt the voter revision process in Bihar, instructing the Election Commission to consider using Aadhaar, Voter ID, and Ration Cards for the special intensive revision of the electoral rolls in the state. This decision comes amid concerns about the timing of this exercise in an election year.

In political news, Congress found itself in a bit of a stir as MP Manickam Tagore subtly criticized fellow party MP Shashi Tharoor for his comments about the Emergency declared during Indira Gandhi's leadership. Tagore's remarks suggested that Tharoor's views were aligning with those of the BJP, sparking debate within the party.

On the international front, tensions between India and the US escalated as India threatened to impose retaliatory tariffs on steel and aluminum imports from the US. This move was in response to American safeguard measures and occurred amidst ongoing trade discussions between the two nations.

Additionally, Arunachal Pradesh's Chief Minister Pema Khandu declared that the next Dalai Lama would be born in a free world, asserting that China should have no role in this spiritual succession.

In sports, the third Test match at Lord's between India and England began with India gaining an early advantage. Nitish Kumar Reddy made a significant impact on his debut by dismissing England's Ben Duckett, adding excitement to the series which is currently tied.

items.title: RSS workers tortured in jails during Emergency, at least 100 died: Sunil Ambekar
items.story: Sunil Ambekar, a senior RSS functionary, stated that thousands of RSS volunteers were jailed and tortured during the Emergency imposed by Indira Gandhi in 1975, resulting in approximately 100 deaths. He described the Emergency as a "black spot" on India's democracy, highlighting the arrests, beatings, and torture inflicted upon RSS workers. Ambekar explained that at least 100 RSS workers died during this period, with some dying in jail due to extreme torture. The Emergency, which lasted for 21 months, was characterized by a massive crackdown on political opponents, forced mass sterilizations, press censorship, and suspension of constitutional rights. The RSS played a significant role in the movement against the Emergency, with many of its members being arrested and tortured in an attempt to force them to support the government. Despite the harsh conditions, the mass movement eventually led to the restoration of democracy. The RSS's involvement included a Satyagraha in which 80,000 to one lakh people participated, contributing to the end of the Emergency and the announcement of elections. Ambekar also addressed misleading claims that the then RSS chief wrote to Indira Gandhi from jail, clarifying that the letters were meant to save people from further suffering. The government now observes June 25 as 'Samvidhaan Hatya Diwas' to honor those who faced "inhuman pains" during that period.
items.relevanceReason: This story directly connects with the leader’s RSS background by highlighting Congress-led repression during the Emergency, a historical grievance for Sangh Parivar. It resonates ideologically with the leader’s Hindutva stance and offers a potent opportunity to criticize Congress’s past authoritarian actions. Publicly acknowledging it can strengthen the Sangh’s narrative and underscore the leader’s longstanding commitment to safeguarding democracy and Hindu rights.

items.title: 'Badly damaged’: In a first, Iran admits impact on nuclear sites in US strikes; keeps details under wrap
items.story: Iran has acknowledged that recent US strikes caused significant damage to its nuclear installations. This admission follows President Trump's claims that the strikes "obliterated" Iran's nuclear program. Trump asserted that Iran's nuclear ambitions have been significantly delayed, drawing a controversial parallel to the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Iran on Wednesday for the first time admitted that recent US strikes "badly damaged" its nuclear installations. Speaking to Al Jazeera, Iran’s foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said the June 22 strikes by American B-2 bombers using bunker-buster munitions had caused significant destruction. “Our nuclear installations have been badly damaged, that’s for sure,” Baghaei said, while declining to provide further details. The admission comes after US President Donald Trump repeatedly claimed the strikes had “obliterated” Iran’s nuclear programme. Trump’s special envoy to the Middle East, Steve Witkoff, also told Fox News that the US and Israel had achieved their objective of "total destruction of the enrichment capacity" in Iran. He added that Iran’s earlier precondition for talks — an end to Israel’s military campaign — had now been addressed. Meanwhile, speaking ahead of the NATO summit in the Netherlands, Trump declared that Iran’s nuclear ambitions had been “set back decades,” just a day after announcing a truce between Iran and Israel. “They’re not going to be building bombs for a long time,” Trump said, insisting that US strikes had caused the “total obliteration” of Iran’s nuclear sites. Drawing a parallel with World War II, Trump said, “That ended the war. I don’t want to use an example of Hiroshima. I don’t want to use an example of Nagasaki. But that was essentially the same thing. That ended that war.” The reference was to the US atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki in 1945, which led to Japan’s surrender and the end of the Pacific theatre in World War II. Commenting on the possibility of Iran resuming uranium enrichment beyond permitted levels, Trump added, “I think they’ve had it. They just went through hell... the last thing they want to do is enrich.” On June 22, the US carried out Operation Midnight Hammer, dropping 30,000-pound bunker-buster bombs on three key underground nuclear sites. The attack was designed to deal a critical blow to Iran's uranium enrichment programme, in line with Trump's stance that Iran cannot be allowed to possess nuclear weapons. According to Pentagon figures, more than 125 aircraft participated in the mission, including stealth bombers, support planes, fighters and surveillance craft. A total of 75 precision weapons were used, including 14 bunker busters and over two dozen cruise missiles.

items.title: 'With a good heart...': Prithvi Shaw shares cryptic post as he parts ways with Mumbai cricket
items.story: India batter Prithvi Shaw's recent cryptic Instagram post has fueled speculation following his departure from the Mumbai domestic cricket team. After being dropped from Mumbai's Ranji Trophy squad and failing to secure a spot in the Vijay Hazare Trophy team, Shaw will now represent Maharashtra in the upcoming domestic season. The 25-year-old posted a quote that appeared to reflect his current mindset amidst a turbulent phase in his cricketing career. "Do everything with a good heart and expect nothing in return," the story read. Once hailed as one of Indian cricket's most promising young talents, Shaw has found himself on the sidelines of late. He was dropped from Mumbai’s Ranji Trophy squad after just two rounds in the 2024–25 season and subsequently failed to make the cut for the state’s Vijay Hazare Trophy team. With limited options in Mumbai, Shaw has now decided to restart his domestic journey with a new team. He will represent Maharashtra in the upcoming domestic season, hoping to revive his form and stake a claim for higher honors. Shaw’s cricketing career has seen extreme highs and lows. He made a century on Test debut for India at the age of 18, but injuries, form issues, and disciplinary concerns have plagued his progress since. To compound his challenges, Shaw went unsold in the 2025 IPL auction - a clear indicator of his dip in form and fading visibility. He was last seen in competitive action during the 2025 edition of the Mumbai T20 League. With a new team and fresh motivation, Shaw will be keen to script a comeback.

items.title: Landmark Land Law Reforms: CM Dhami marks 4 years of Uttarakhand government's progressive agenda
items.story:
On the occasion of completing four years as the Chief Minister of Uttarakhand, Pushkar Singh Dhami discussed the significant achievements of his government, notably the amendment of the state’s land law. This amendment restricts the sale of agricultural and horticultural land in 11 of the 13 districts in Uttarakhand, with Haridwar and Udham Singh Nagar being exempt from these stringent regulations. Dhami emphasized that these amendments reflect public sentiment and have led to the introduction of various laws, including an anti-cheating law that has become a model nationwide.

Dhami highlighted the government’s efforts to combat corruption, stating that actions have been taken against corrupt individuals regardless of their position. He mentioned the anti-cheating law, anti-riot law, anti-conversion law to prevent religious conversion, and an encroachment removal campaign, which has cleared over 6,500 acres of land. The state legislative assembly passed the Uttarakhand (Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Destruction and Land Reforms Act, 1950) (Amendment) Bill, 2025, in February, aligning land reforms with public sentiment.

The government is committed to protecting state resources and lands from misuse by land mafias. Permission for land purchase for agricultural and industrial purposes, previously granted at the collector level, is now restricted in 11 districts and decided at the state government level only in Haridwar and Udham Singh Nagar. A significant change is that land purchases for tourism, industry, and educational facilities will have a ceiling of 12.5 acres in 11 districts, with the possibility of purchasing more in the remaining two districts.

Dhami stated that the new law includes significant changes and incorporated views from stakeholders in Gairsain. Land purchases outside municipal limits are covered by this amendment, and an affidavit is now mandatory for purchasing 250 square meters of land for residential projects. If found false, the land will revert to the state government.

items.title: Why Elon Musk hates researchers and loves engineers — after he corrected xAI employee Aditya Gupta's hiring post
items.story: Elon Musk is advocating for a unified engineering workforce at xAI and SpaceX, eliminating the title "researcher." He believes this outdated term creates unnecessary hierarchies and hinders collaboration. Musk emphasizes that focusing on practical engineering and accountability will accelerate innovation and deliver tangible results in the fast-paced AI industry, fostering a meritocratic environment. Elon Musk recently made waves by publicly correcting a hiring post from an xAI employee, Aditya Gupta, who initially sought to recruit both "researchers" and "engineers" for the artificial intelligence startup. Musk emphatically declared that the term "researcher" is outdated, pretentious, and fosters a problematic two-tier system within the engineering workforce. He insisted that at xAI—and also at SpaceX—everyone should simply be called "engineers." This shift reflects Musk’s vision for a unified, accountable, and highly practical technical team, breaking away from traditional academic distinctions he views as unnecessary and even harmful to innovation and team cohesion. Elon Musk has been vocal about his dislike for the title "researcher," which he frequently describes as a "relic of academia." In Musk’s view, the label “researcher” creates an artificial hierarchy within technical teams, suggesting that researchers are somehow distinct, or even less accountable, compared to engineers. He argues that this division weakens ownership, blurs responsibility, and fosters a separation that slows practical progress. Elon Musk reasons that in fast-paced technology companies like xAI and SpaceX, what matters most is the ability to build, iterate, and solve real-world problems—responsibilities encompassed by the role of an "engineer." By rejecting the researcher title, Musk aims to eliminate what he perceives as academic pretentiousness that can sometimes encourage theoretical work disconnected from product outcomes. He emphasizes that this distinction is not only outdated but counterproductive, introducing inefficiencies and hindering collaboration. As Musk noted, his insistence on the universal "engineer" title promotes a culture where every team member is equally accountable for delivering tangible, impactful results, fostering a meritocratic and results-driven environment. At xAI, Musk champions a workforce composed of builders and implementers rather than theorists. The company’s mission to rapidly advance AI technologies, relying on cutting-edge methods like reinforcement learning and massive computing infrastructure, requires a practical, hands-on approach. Musk specifically points out that although SpaceX conducts groundbreaking technological research, it never labels any employees as “researchers.” This reflects his belief that true innovation depends on rigorous engineering discipline, rapid prototyping, and direct problem-solving. This approach denotes a preference for those who can translate ideas into working systems efficiently, rather than spending extended time in exploratory research without definite product outcomes. In Musk’s philosophy, eliminating the “researcher” distinction accelerates the engineering feedback loop, promoting speed and accountability critical for breakthrough innovation. Musk’s correction of the xAI hiring post is more than a cosmetic change—it embodies his no-nonsense, high-accountability management style. By publicly enforcing uniform job titles, Musk sends a clear message that academic or theoretical fragmentation has no place in his companies. Experts interpret this move as symbolic of a broader Silicon Valley trend favoring flatter, integrated teams with streamlined roles to enhance agility and rapid product delivery. However, this shift has its critics. Some industry analysts warn that entirely removing the "researcher" role risks sidelining deep exploratory inquiry and ethical considerations essential in AI development—areas traditionally safeguarded by academic research freedoms. The balance between practical engineering and theoretical investigation remains a subject of debate. Elon Musk’s terminological shift is already influencing company cultures beyond xAI. SpaceX has long embraced this engineering-only framework, and other prominent AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic are experimenting with novel job title structures to blur conventional boundaries between research and engineering roles. Musk’s approach underscores his desire to build startups that push technological frontiers aggressively while maintaining crystal-clear lines of accountability and measurable output. Whether this “engineer-only” model will foster faster innovation or create challenges in navigating the complex landscape of AI research remains to be seen. For now, Elon Musk has unequivocally communicated his stance: at xAI, there are no researchers—only engineers—united in building the future of artificial intelligence.

items.title: ‘Historic flight’: President Murmu takes Rafale sortie in Ambala - watch
items.story: NEW DELHI: President Droupadi Murmu took a sortie in a Rafale fighter jet at the Indian Air Force Station in Ambala, Haryana, on Thursday. Air Chief Marshal A P Singh was among those present for the occasion. Rafale jets, manufactured by French aerospace company Dassault Aviation and formally inducted into the Indian Air Force in September 2020 at Ambala, played a key role in Operation Sindoor. This was President Murmu's second flight in a combat aircraft, following her 2023 sortie in a Sukhoi-30 MKI at Tezpur Air Force Station in Assam. Operation Sindoor was launched on May 7 in response to the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack, the operation targeted terror infrastructure in Pakistan-controlled territories and led to four days of intense clashes, concluding with an agreement to halt military actions on May 10, at the request of the Pakistani DGMO. The Rashtrapati Bhavan had confirmed the development on Tuesday, describing it as part of the President’s engagement with India’s defence forces. "The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu, will visit Ambala, Haryana tomorrow where she will take a sortie in Rafale," a statement issued on Tuesday by the Rashtrapati Bhavan said. Former Presidents A P J Abdul Kalam and Pratibha Patil had previously flown sorties in Sukhoi-30 MKI aircraft at Lohegaon Air Force Station in 2006 and 2009, respectively. This is a developing story. Details to follow...

items.title: IAF strip, used in 3 wars, secretly sold off using fake papers
items.story: In a brazen act of deceit, a mother-son duo in Ferozepur, Punjab, allegedly sold off a World War II-era airstrip in 1997, colluding with revenue officials. The Punjab and Haryana High Court intervened, leading to an FIR against Usha Ansal and Naveen Chand after a Vigilance Bureau probe confirmed the land belonged to the Indian Air Force. The airstrip, used during the 1962, 1965, and 1971 wars, was allegedly sold off using fake papers. The land, located in Fattuwala village near the Pakistan border, was finally restored to the Ministry of Defence in May 2025 after court intervention. The investigation revealed that the accused deceitfully claimed ownership and sold the land after forging revenue records. An FIR was filed under various sections of the IPC, including cheating and criminal conspiracy. The case has drawn attention due to the potential threat to national security, and the investigation is ongoing.

items.title: Rajasthan: 6 dead, 5 critical after fire breaks out at Jaipur’s SMS Hospital trauma ICU
items.story:
NEW DELHI: Six patients died and five remain critical after a fire triggered by a short circuit broke out at the trauma ICU of Jaipur’s Sawai Man Singh (SMS) Hospital late on Sunday night.

SMS Hospital Trauma Centre Incharge Anurag Dhakad told ANI that the fire started in the trauma ICU on the second floor and spread quickly, releasing toxic gases. “Our trauma centre has two ICUs on the second floor: a trauma ICU and a semi-ICU. We had 24 patients there; 11 in the trauma ICU and 13 in the semi-ICU. A short circuit occurred in the trauma ICU, and the fire spread rapidly, releasing toxic gases,” he said.

Dhakad added that most of the patients in the ICU were comatose. “Our trauma centre team, our nursing officers, and ward boys, immediately rescued them on trolleys and brought as many patients as we could out of the ICU and shifted them to another location. Six of those patients were very critical; we tried very hard to revive them with CPR, but they couldn't be saved,” he said.

According to Dhakad, two of the deceased were women and four were men. Five patients are still critical. “There were 24 that we evacuated: 11 in the trauma ICU and 13 in the adjacent ICU,” he said.

Authorities are investigating the cause of the short circuit and assessing damage to the facility. Rescue operations were completed shortly after the blaze was brought under control.

More details awaited.

items.title: AAIB DG leading crash probe gets X security cover
items.story: The government has provided X category security cover to the Director General of the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau, GVG Yugandhar, who is leading the investigation into the crash of AI-171. Following a threat perception report, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has instructed the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) to provide him with security. Meanwhile, India has granted observer status to an expert from the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) for the crash probe. The United Nations' aviation branch, ICAO, had formally requested to send an observer to the inquiry. As a signatory to ICAO's Chicago Convention (1944), India investigates aircraft accidents in accordance with ICAO's and its own rules.

items.title: Dentists can perform facial aesthetics, hair transplants: Telangana Dental Council counters medical body’s advisory; backs oral surgeons' training and DCI norms
items.story: The Telangana Dental Council (TDC) has stated that registered oral and maxillofacial surgeons (OMFS) are qualified to perform facial aesthetic procedures and hair transplantation. This announcement opposes a circular from the Telangana Medical Council (TGMC), which advised against such procedures by dentists, citing insufficient training. The TDC asserts that these surgeons are trained under the standards set by the Dental Council of India and are capable of performing facial aesthetic procedures and hair transplantation. The TGMC's advisory was based on a clarification from the National Medical Commission, which suggested that dentists might not be adequately trained for these procedures. However, the TDC highlights that oral and maxillofacial surgeons are specialists in diagnosing and treating conditions related to the mouth, jaws, face, and neck, including performing minor oral surgeries, treating soft tissue injuries, fractures, gunshot wounds, and aesthetic deformities of the jaws and face, as well as conducting aesthetic facial surgery.
