items.title: Bengaluru stampede: Karnataka high court orders full disclosure of status report
items.story: The Karnataka High Court has ordered the full disclosure of a status report related to the stampede at M Chinnaswamy Stadium, which occurred on June 4 and resulted in 11 fatalities. The court rejected the state government's request to keep the report confidential, as it does not involve issues of national security or public interest that would warrant such secrecy. The report, dated June 12, is to be included in court records and shared with the Karnataka State Cricket Association, Royal Challengers Bengaluru, and DNA Entertainment Pvt Ltd. The court dismissed the previous sealed cover approach, noting that the arguments presented by the advocate-general, Shashikiran Shetty, were insufficient. The court emphasized that sealed cover proceedings are generally reserved for cases involving national security, public interest, or privacy rights. The bench, led by Acting Chief Justice V Kameshwar Rao and Justice CM Joshi, noted that the disclosure of the report would not influence ongoing magisterial inquiries or judicial commissions, as these are conducted by independent and experienced individuals. The proceedings aim to uncover the causes of the tragedy and suggest preventive measures for the future. The court also stated that the proceedings do not fall under Section 192(5) of the BNSS, which means investigative confidentiality is unnecessary. The facts presented in the report are not expected to change post-inquiry.

items.title: 'Sitaare Zameen Par' box office collection day 8 (LIVE): The Aamir Khan starrer touches Rs 90 crore after completing a week; sees a slight drop as 'Maa' releases
items.story: Aamir Khan's film 'Sitaare Zameen Par' has grossed over Rs 90 crore in its first week of release. This success is attributed to positive word-of-mouth, as the film was not expected to perform like typical blockbusters. Initially, the film saw strong earnings, but experienced a slight decline mid-week, possibly due to competition from new releases like Kajol's 'Maa' and the South Indian film 'Kannapa'. The daily earnings for the film were Rs 10.7 crore on opening day, Rs 20.2 crore and Rs 27.25 crore on the first Saturday and Sunday respectively. It earned Rs 8.5 crore on both Monday and Tuesday, Rs 7.25 crore on Wednesday, and Rs 6.75 crore on Thursday. The film's total earnings for the first week reached Rs 89.15 crore. On the following Friday, it earned Rs 96 lakhs by the afternoon, bringing the total to Rs 90.11 crore. The film's performance is expected to be affected by the new releases.

items.title: Drunk man kills wife in Bihar; villagers blame liquor sale in area for crime spike
items.story: In the village of Shyam in Madhepura, Bihar, a tragic incident unfolded when an intoxicated man, Vilash Rishideo, allegedly killed his wife, Sushila Devi, by biting her neck multiple times during a quarrel about his drinking habits. The altercation took a deadly turn late Tuesday night, leading to Sushila's death. Vilash fled the scene after the crime, but was apprehended by villagers and subsequently arrested by the police on Wednesday morning after they were alerted by the community. The couple's children, three daughters and a son, were found crying by neighbors who discovered the body. Sushila's remains were sent for an autopsy, and charges were filed against Vilash based on the testimony of the victim's family. This incident has caused widespread shock in the village, with the local community attributing the rise in such crimes to the illegal sale of liquor in the area, calling for stricter enforcement of the liquor ban by the authorities.

items.title: 'So very American': Indian-origin Vaibhav Taneja listed as treasurer of Elon Musk's America Party
items.story: Indian-origin Vaibhav Taneja was named the treasurer of the America Party in the paperwork that was filed to create Elon Musk's America Party on Sunday. Elon Musk announced the creation of the America Party after his fallout with President Donald Trump and the GOP over the 'Big, Beautiful Bill', aiming to break the two-party system of US politics. According to the FEC form, which has gone viral on social media, the America Party is headquartered at 1 Rocker Road, Hawthorne, and lists Elon Musk as the single candidate. Vaibhav Taneja is mentioned as the custodian of records and the treasurer, with a Texas address listed for Taneja. Vaibhav Taneja is the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of Tesla, having assumed the role in August 2023 after the departure of Zach Kirkhorn. An Indian-origin executive, Taneja has played a key role in Tesla’s accounting and financial operations for several years. He joined Tesla in 2017 through its acquisition of SolarCity, where he was already serving in a senior finance role. Before Tesla, Taneja worked at PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) in both India and the United States for nearly 17 years. Known for his low public profile and steady management style, Taneja has helped oversee Tesla’s financial strategies during a time of rapid global expansion and increased scrutiny over the company’s margins and performance. He holds a commerce degree from Delhi University and is a certified chartered accountant, making him one of the few Indian-origin CFOs at a major American tech company. The revelations about Taneja's role in filing for the new party have drawn backlash on social media, with users dubbing the America Party as the H-1B party, given Elon Musk's support for the H-1B program that allows US companies to hire foreign workers. Taneja recently made headlines for earning more than Satya Nadella and Sundar Pichai in 2024, with a total pay package of $139 million as Tesla's CFO, compared to Sundar Pichai's $10.73 million and Satya Nadella's $79.1 million.

items.title: Bihar bizman's killer identified; police probe jail & gangster links
items.story:
Police investigating the murder of businessman Gopal Khemka in Patna have identified the shooter and are tracing his escape. Authorities are exploring connections to a Beur jail inmate and a possible link to a land dispute. The 2018 murder of Khemka's son is also under investigation, leading to jail raids, detentions, and the suspension of jail officials.

Police probing the murder of prominent businessman Gopal Khemka here have identified the shooter and tracked his escape route, inspector general of police (IGP) Jitendra Rana said on Sunday. He said all possible angles were being investigated, including possible links to an inmate at Beur jail. "The involvement of a notorious gangster in the killing is being suspected. A land-related dispute has also come to light. Besides, we are also probing connection with the murder of Gunjan Khemka (Gopal's son) who was shot outside his factory in Hajipur in 2018," the IGP said. Police have detained several suspects in the district. Authorities also conducted a raid on the jail on Saturday. "The raid was carried out due to suspected links in the Khemka murder case. Some mobile handsets, SIMs, and other items were seized from the jail. Some inmates were also interrogated," Singh told TOI. This prompted authorities to suspend three jail warders and issue show-cause notices to deputy superintendent Ajay Kumar, assistant superintendent Niraj Kumar Rajak, and section-in-charge Girish Yadav.

items.title: IND vs ENG 4th Test: After Sachin Tendulkar, Sunil Gavaskar and Rahul Dravid, KL Rahul 11 runs away from...
items.story: Indian cricketer KL Rahul is on the verge of joining an elite list of Indian cricketers who have scored 1,000 or more Test runs in England. He is just 11 runs short of this milestone as he prepares for the fourth Test match against England, which is set to begin on July 23 in Manchester. Currently, England leads the series 2-1. KL Rahul has accumulated 989 runs in 12 Tests and 24 innings in England, with an average of 41.20. His record includes four centuries and two fifties, with a highest score of 149. Only three Indian batters have previously reached this achievement in England: Sachin Tendulkar with 1,575 runs in 17 Tests at an average of 54.31, Rahul Dravid with 1,376 runs in 13 Tests at 68.80, and Sunil Gavaskar with 1,152 runs in 16 Tests at 41.14. In the ongoing series, Rahul has been in impressive form, scoring 375 runs in three Tests at an average of 62.50, including two centuries and a fifty, with a top score of 137, making him the fourth-highest run-getter in the series. India's Test squad for the series includes Shubman Gill as captain and Rishabh Pant as vice-captain, along with other players like Yashasvi Jaiswal, Sai Sudharsan, and Jasprit Bumrah. In contrast, the England squad will be led by Ben Stokes and includes players like Jofra Archer and Joe Root. Despite scoring his second century at Lord's during the third Test, Rahul ended up on the losing side. He aims to continue his impressive form in England and contribute to a potential series-leveling victory for India in Manchester.

items.title: Supreme Court to hear plea for 'Udaipur Files' release 'in a day or two'
items.story: The Supreme Court has assured the producers of the film 'Udaipur Files: Kanhaiya Lal Tailor Murder' that it will swiftly hear their appeal against the Delhi High Court's decision to halt the film's release. The film, depicting the Kanhaiyalal beheading incident, was approved by the censor board with certain edits. Senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia appealed for an urgent hearing before a bench of Justices Surya Kant and Joymalya Bagchi. The high court's decision to stop the release was based on a petition by Maulana Arshad Madani, who argued that the film disparaged an entire community. However, the filmmakers contend that the movie is based on the true event of Kanhaiyalal's beheading by two Muslim men in June 2022, due to a social media post about Prophet Mohammad. They argue that all necessary cuts suggested by the CBFC were made. The high court allowed Madani to appeal against the film's release to the Union government, stating the film's release should remain paused until the government decides on any interim relief requested through a revision petition under the Cinematograph Act. The producers, represented by advocate Pulkit Agarwal, cited Supreme Court judgments asserting that a film cleared by the censor board should not be prevented from screening unless it violates the 'reasonable restrictions' on the right to free speech under Article 19(2) of the Constitution.

items.title: Who was Virginia Giuffre? The voice that took on Epstein - and why her ghost haunts Trump administration
items.story:
Virginia Giuffre, once an anonymous teenage victim of Jeffrey Epstein's sprawling sex-trafficking operation, became one of the most prominent and courageous voices to expose the web of elite abuse he orchestrated. She died by suicide in April this year at her farm in Western Australia at the age of 41. Now, the US justice department and FBI have released a long-awaited memorandum that squarely debunks the most persistent conspiracy theories surrounding Epstein’s 2019 prison death and his alleged blackmail operations. According to the memo, there is no evidence that Epstein was murdered, ran a "client list," or blackmailed powerful individuals. Investigators reaffirmed that Epstein died by suicide and said extensive reviews of his digital and physical records—while confirming abuse of over a thousand victims—revealed no incriminating material involving third parties. Yet for many, especially in political circles tied to US President Donald Trump, that memo feels more like a closing statement on a chapter that never quite opened.

Who was Virginia Giuffre? Virginia Giuffre, born Virginia Louise Roberts in 1983, was one of the most prominent survivors and whistleblowers in the Jeffrey Epstein sex-trafficking scandal. Her life story, marked by abuse and resilience, became central to exposing the vast network of exploitation orchestrated by Epstein and his close associate Ghislaine Maxwell. Recruited in 2000 at age 16 while working at Mar-a-Lago - Donald Trump's resort in Florida - Giuffre was approached by Maxwell under the pretense of becoming Epstein’s traveling masseuse. What followed, she later revealed, was years of sexual abuse, during which she was trafficked to wealthy and powerful men, including Britain’s Prince Andrew. Giuffre first sued Epstein in 2009 under the pseudonym "Jane Doe 102" and later became the first of his victims to publicly share her story in 2015. Her detailed accounts helped fuel criminal investigations and lawsuits that would eventually lead to Maxwell's 2021 conviction for sex trafficking and a 20-year prison sentence. Giuffre herself sued Prince Andrew in 2021 for sexual assault, resulting in a high-profile settlement the following year. She also successfully sued Maxwell for defamation in 2015. Giuffre's testimony and activism played a pivotal role in bringing Epstein's crimes—and the complicity of those around him—into the public spotlight.

Why her ghost haunts Trump administration? Giuffre’s connection to the Trump world was unambiguous: she was first recruited into Epstein’s network while working at Mar-a-Lago, Trump’s Florida resort, when she was just a teenager. Her death by suicide raised several eyebrows as she had clarified in a post in 2019 that she wasn't "suicidal." "I am making it publicly known that in no way, shape or form am I suicidal. I have made this known to my therapist and GP- If something happens to me- in the sake of my family do not let this go away and help me to protect them. Too many evil people want to see me quieted," she had said. And although Trump has never been accused of wrongdoing in connection to Epstein, he was named in a cache of documents unsealed earlier this year. The release triggered a brief feud between Trump and Elon Musk, who accused the president of being “in the Epstein files” - a claim Musk later deleted. For Trump’s base, the Epstein saga has often been weaponized as a partisan tool, used to implicate Democrats and celebrities while ignoring ties closer to home. Ironically, some of the most vocal conspiracy theorists about Epstein’s death - like Trump’s own FBI director Kash Patel and deputy director Dan Bongino - have been forced into silence by the DOJ’s findings.

items.title: Destroying evidence: Rahul Gandhi targets EC again; questions 45-day CCTV footage wipeout; poll body reacts
items.story:
Rahul Gandhi has intensified his criticism of the Election Commission, alleging a lack of transparency and the destruction of vital election data. The EC defended its decision to erase CCTV footage 45 days post-election, citing voter privacy and potential misuse. Officials stated that releasing webcasting footage could compromise voter security and contravene legal provisions, despite claims of promoting democratic integrity.

NEW DELHI: Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, on Saturday renewed his attack on the Election Commission, questioning its transparency and alleging a deliberate attempt to destroy crucial poll-related data. The poll body reacted saying that making webcasting footage of polling stations public violated privacy and security concerns of voters.

"Voter list? Will not provide machine-readable format. CCTV footage? It was hidden by changing the law. Photo-video of the election? Now, not in 1 year, we will destroy it in 45 days only. The one from whom the answer was needed - is destroying the evidence. It is clear - the match is fixed. And a fixed election is poison for democracy," read a post by Rahul Gandhi on X. EC officials argued that while such demands appeared to champion voter interest and democratic integrity, they were actually intended to achieve the "opposite objective".

What is presented as a reasonable and logical request directly contradicts voter privacy, legal provisions under the Representation of the People Acts of 1950 and 1951, and Supreme Court directives, PTI reported citing EC officials. Officials warned that sharing the footage could allow easy identification of voters and non-voters, exposing them to potential pressure, discrimination, or intimidation by anti-social elements. Citing a possible scenario, officials further said that if a political party received fewer votes at a specific booth, it could use CCTV footage to identify who voted and who didn’t—potentially leading to targeted harassment or intimidation of those individuals.

They clarified that the Election Commission retained CCTV footage, used solely as an internal administrative tool, for 45 days in line with the legal window for filing an election petition. Since no election can be challenged beyond this period, they argued that keeping the footage any longer could lead to its misuse by non-contestants to spread misinformation or malicious narratives. They added that if an election petition is filed within 45 days, the footage is preserved and made available to the competent court upon request.

The government, last year, amended election rules, based on the EC's recommendation, to restrict public access to certain electronic records—such as CCTV and webcast footage—to prevent misuse. In a May 30 letter, the EC informed state officials that multiple recording methods, including photography, videography, CCTV, and webcasting, are used to document the election process.

items.title: Explained: What are new porn rules in UK and that have led to 500%-plus jump in VPN
items.story: The UK's new stringent age verification laws for online pornography aim to protect minors, leading to a significant increase in VPN usage as users try to bypass these restrictions. These regulations require adult content websites to implement stringent age checks, raising privacy concerns and facing industry opposition. The regulations, which became effective on July 25th, aim to prevent under-18s from accessing pornography and other harmful online materials. As per the new law, any website offering adult content to UK users must implement "highly effective" age checks to verify that visitors are over 18, which may include photo ID uploads, facial recognition, or credit card verification. Websites like RedTube, Pornhub, and social media sites such as X and Reddit must block access to adult content unless users pass strict age verification. The UK's media regulator Ofcom has warned that failure to comply with the law could result in fines of up to £18 million or 10% of global revenue. Some platforms may block UK users entirely instead of implementing these checks. The Independent reported that after the implementation of the strict age verification law, searches for 'VPN' in the UK surged by over 700%, as VPNs allow users to mask their location and access the internet from countries without such restrictions. Legal experts and privacy advocates warn that while Ofcom can geo-block sites, VPNs remain a simple workaround for many users. Critics argue that the new rules could push users toward unregulated or fringe platforms, increasing exposure to unsafe content. Some major adult content providers, such as Aylo, which operates Pornhub and YouPorn, have criticized the checks as "ineffective, haphazard, and dangerous," citing risks to user privacy. They advocate for device-based age verification rather than server-side data collection, arguing that the current approach could jeopardize sensitive personal information. As the UK attempts to create a "safer online life," the rollout of these rules has sparked a fierce debate over privacy, censorship, and digital freedom.

items.title: Auto sector boost: Most car buyers use GST savings to upgrade to premium models; SUVs, EVs lead post-cut demand
items.story: A majority of car buyers have used recent GST reductions not to save money but to upgrade to higher-end models and brands, according to a new study. As per news agency PTI, around 80 per cent of buyers surveyed said they used the tax relief to switch to a better model, brand, or premium add-ons during the festive season. The findings come from the 'Post GST Car Buying Behaviour Trends' study by consumer-intelligence and market-research platform SmyttenPulse AI, which surveyed over 5,000 people in October 2025 across Tier 1, 2 and 3 cities. The report found that SUVs remain the most popular choice among buyers, while growing environmental awareness is significantly increasing electric vehicle (EV) consideration despite challenges such as limited charging infrastructure. 'GST cuts have acted as a catalyst, but the larger story is behavioural: buyers are upgrading, not downsizing,' the study noted. Nearly 79 per cent of respondents said they used GST savings to move up to a higher model, brand, or better-equipped vehicle rather than saving the difference. According to PTI, more than 60 per cent of buyers plan to upgrade to higher variants within the same brand, and 46 per cent have already shifted from hatchbacks to larger vehicles like SUVs. The study also found that 67 per cent of respondents cited ecological benefits as a major reason for considering EVs, even though concerns remain over battery life and replacement costs. Financial confidence appears to be returning, with 53 per cent of respondents ready to make higher down payments or opt for longer loan tenures. The report said that faith in policy support and industry incentives continues to sustain buyer optimism. 'GST cuts have done more than make cars affordable; they've reignited aspiration,' said Swagat Sarangi, cofounder of SmyttenPulse AI, as per PTI. 'The middle-class buyer is using this moment to stretch upward, from base variants to top trims, from budget brands to feature-rich models', Sarangi added.

items.title: Krishna water tribunal gets a year's extension from August 1
items.story: The Centre has extended the tenure of the Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal by another year, effective August 1, due to its failure to reach an acceptable decision despite previous extensions. This tribunal, formed in 2004, adjudicates water-sharing disputes among Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Telangana. Experts suggest amending the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, to incorporate fixed timelines for final decisions. Days after granting an extension to Ravi and Beas Waters Tribunal, the country's oldest water disputes tribunal, the Centre has extended the tenure of Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal as well. Constituted in April 2004 to adjudicate the river water-sharing dispute among Maharashtra, Karnataka and erstwhile Andhra Pradesh, Krishna tribunal has got an extension of another year, with effect from August 1. Krishna tribunal is one of the four active river-water tribunals in India, which have got extensions year after year, as they haven't managed to come up with an acceptable decision despite their extended tenures. "The said tribunals were constituted to adjudicate disputes between two or more states and therefore need to work towards early resolution, particularly since such disputes involve public interest and public welfare. Given the wide-reaching implications of such adjudication, I believe the proceedings should be completed in a time-bound manner while also adhering to the procedural laws," said Khushal Garg, a Delhi high court advocate who has been following the issue. Noting that granting repeated extensions dilutes the essence of justice, he said, "The Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 may be amended to incorporate fixed timelines for final decisions, as it would expedite resolution process." The terms of reference of the 21-year-old Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal were amended last year to accommodate the water-sharing concerns of a fourth state, Telangana, as well, factoring in issues arising out of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.

items.title: Former India spinner Dilip Doshi passes away at 77 | Cricket News - Times of India
items.story: Former Indian left-arm spinner Dilip Doshi passed away in London at the age of 77 due to cardiac arrest. Doshi represented India in 33 Tests and 15 ODIs between 1979 and 1983. The Saurashtra Cricket Association mourned the loss of Doshi, remembering his dedication and skill. He was a match-winner, achieving 114 Test wickets and 898 first-class wickets. Doshi had recently attended the BCCI Awards function and the World Test Championship final at Lord's earlier this month. Doshi was a true and spirited Saurashtrian and a legendary left-arm leg-spinner in the cricket world. Despite his late India debut, he achieved many remarkable milestones and was a pure match-winner. Dilipbhai reached the 100-wicket mark in only 28 Tests. He played 33 Tests and took 114 wickets, including six five-wicket hauls. He played 238 first-class matches, taking a staggering 898 wickets, including 43 five-wicket hauls and six 10-wicket hauls. In 15 ODIs, he took 22 wickets, including two four-wicket hauls. These figures say it all about his class. Dilipbhai’s passion for cricket was exceptional and beyond compare. He rated his five-wicket haul in the Melbourne Test in 1981 against Australia as his best performance. He continued bowling in spite of acute pain due to a fractured toe because he believed Team India would win the match. Such was the depth of his passion for the game. Sir Garfield Sobers had rightly said that 'Dilip Doshi has an immeasurable knowledge to pass on to those who want to follow his path into professional cricket. He has played at all levels over the world and there can be no one more qualified to talk about the art of spin bowling.' Expressing his "profound grief" at Doshi's passing, Niranjan Shah, former secretary of the BCCI, said: “It is an extremely painful and personal loss for me. Dilip was not only one of the legendary cricketers but also one of the finest human beings I have ever known. His noble heart, integrity, and priceless dedication to the game made him truly special. He was family—someone I shared not just cricketing conversations with, but also a deep bond built on mutual respect and affection. His presence always brought warmth, humility, and positive energy. The void he leaves behind is beyond words. It is not just the world of cricket, but my own heart that feels his absence deeply. I shall always cherish the beautiful memories and moments we spent together. His legacy will live on through the many lives he inspired.” SCA president Jaydev Shah stated: “His passing is an irreparable loss to the cricketing fraternity, and to all of us who had the honour of knowing him. His legacy, both as a player and a person, will continue to live in our hearts and in the history of cricket. This is an incredibly painful and personal loss for me. He was not just a legendary cricketer—he was my uncle, my mentor, and someone I looked up to throughout my life. His deep love for the sport, disciplined approach, and graceful conduct made him a role model for generations. For many of us, he was not only a hero on the field but also a guide and a well-wisher off it. Indian cricket has lost a true legend today. Everyone at the SCA conveys his/her heartfelt condolences to the late Dilip Doshi’s family and prays to the Almighty to grant eternal peace to his noble soul."

items.title: Strict action against projects without proper permissions: HYDRAA chief AV Ranganath, flags link between unauthorised construction and urban woes
items.story: At the Times Home Hunt Property Expo, HYDRAA commissioner AV Ranganath issued a warning stating that any new projects lacking proper permissions or constructed on encroached land would face strict action. He clarified that only layouts approved before the formation of HYDRAA on July 19 of the previous year would be exempt from these regulations. Ranganath emphasized that unchecked construction has significantly contributed to urban issues such as flooding and traffic congestion. HYDRAA was established not just as a regulatory body but also as a proactive entity aimed at promoting responsible urban development. Ranganath highlighted that HYDRAA's focus is not solely on demolitions but on fostering a healthier, more environmentally conscious real estate ecosystem.

items.title: Shift high-risk would-be moms to health centres: Uttarakhand govt
items.story: The health department of Uttarakhand is taking proactive measures to relocate high-risk pregnant women from remote villages to health centers at least two weeks before their due dates. This action is due to road blockages and access issues caused by heavy rainfall and landslides during the monsoon season. Approximately 500 women across the state have been identified as needing assistance, with special arrangements made in Kapkot, Bageshwar. In this area, around 150 pregnant women have been identified, and hotels have been requisitioned for free lodging and meals for these women and their attendants. Last year, the health department successfully managed around 650 high-risk pregnancies by taking similar preemptive actions. In some cases, expectant mothers had to be carried on makeshift stretchers due to impassable roads, risking serious complications. To prevent such occurrences, ASHA workers and ANMs are actively compiling lists of pregnant women due in the coming weeks. This initiative aims to ensure safer deliveries during the monsoon season.

items.title: 'In days to come... ': Lingayat seer backs DK Shivakumar for Karnataka CM post; reminds Congress of pre-poll deal
items.story:
A prominent Lingayat seer has publicly endorsed DK Shivakumar for a higher position in Karnataka Congress, fueling speculation about a potential power shift. The seer's remarks, made at a public event, highlighted Shivakumar's contribution to the party's victory in the 2023 elections and hinted at a pre-election agreement regarding the Chief Minister's role.

The ongoing undercurrent of dissent in the Karnataka Congress, between DK Shivakumar's chief ministerial ambitions and CM Siddaramaiah's continuing leadership, received fresh attention on Sunday. This time from the pulpit of a prominent Lingayat seer.

At a public event in Kanakapura Taluk, Rambapuri Seer Rajadeshikendra Shivacharya openly endorsed Shivakumar's bid for greater prominence, saying the Congress state president deserved a higher position after steering the party to a resounding win in the 2023 Karnataka assembly elections.

"He should have got a higher position after the last elections. May he get a higher position in the days to come," the seer said, according to news agency PTI.

The remarks come amid persistent speculation within political circles that the Congress high command may revisit a reported power-sharing deal, often described as a "rotational CM formula", between Siddaramaiah and Shivakumar.

Though never confirmed officially, the formula was believed to include a mid-term leadership switch after two-and-a-half years.

While addressing the gathering at Siddeshwaraswamy hills, the seer praised Shivakumar's organisational acumen and influence over party dynamics in Karnataka.

He further hinted at the supposed pre-election understanding between the top leaders.

"Political leaders must honour their word. If there was an agreement before the elections, it should be respected. Asking Shivakumar to step down as KPCC president without fulfilling the promise is not a principled approach," he said.

The endorsement could further complicate the already delicate balance between the two Congress heavyweights, both of whom had vied for the CM post post-election.

Eventually, the high command persuaded Shivakumar to settle for the deputy CM role.

Reacting cautiously, Shivakumar said he respected the sentiments of both the public and the religious community, but made it clear that he would go by the party's word.

"It's not wrong for party workers, seers, or the public to express their wishes. But AICC President Mallikarjun Kharge has asked us not to speak on the matter. We will follow what the party decides," he told reporters at his Kodihalli residence.

When asked about the seer's backing and the alleged leadership agreement, he declined to go into details.

"Why should I talk about it openly? It's between me and the party. We are all working together," he said.

Despite the united front, the undertones suggest insinuation that Shivakumar remains a contender for the top job, with voices backing his claim growing louder.

items.title: India’s skill education divide: Which states are leading in school-based vocational learning?
items.story:
The recently released PARAKH Rashtriya Sarvekshan 2024 report has highlighted significant disparities in how Indian states are integrating vocational education into their school curriculums. While some states have made considerable progress in offering skill-based courses at the secondary level, others lag in both access and student participation. The survey, conducted under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 framework, assessed learning outcomes in over 75,000 schools involving more than 2.2 million students in Grades 3, 6, and 9. In addition to academics, it evaluated how well schools align with NEP’s goal of providing vocational exposure to at least 50% of learners by 2025, a target that many states are still far from achieving. 

Gujarat leads in school-level implementation with 57% of secondary schools offering vocational courses for Grade 9 and above, followed by Punjab and Odisha with 54% and 50% respectively. However, there's a significant gap between the availability of courses and student enrollment. For example, Bihar has 44% of its schools offering skill-based courses, but only 21% of Grade 9 students are enrolled. Odisha shows a similar trend with only 21% student participation despite half of its schools providing these courses.

In some regions, student demand outpaces the availability of courses. In Delhi, only 42% of schools offer skill education, yet 54% of Grade 9 students are enrolled. Chandigarh shows the most significant contrast with 40% of schools offering courses but an impressive 65% student participation rate, the highest in the country. This suggests that with proper awareness and quality courses, student interest in skill education can increase, even in states with fewer resources.

The report emphasizes that while infrastructure has improved in several states, meaningful participation requires more than just policy compliance. States need to invest in awareness campaigns, offer industry-relevant courses, and employ qualified trainers to make vocational education aspirational. As the next edition of PARAKH is planned, experts say bridging the gap between provision and participation is crucial for achieving the NEP's vision of a skilled, future-ready student population.

items.title: Hyderabad@2047: Here’s an agenda for a global city
items.story: Hyderabad: The philosopher Søren Kierkegaard had said that life can only be understood backwards, but it must be lived forwards. Effectively, if the past must be deciphered, it must be to find the keys to an uncertain future. Keeping this in mind, The Times of India ended its celebrations of completing 25 years in Hyderabad with a conclave that brought together some of the brightest minds in the city to create an agenda for the next 25-odd years. The question we tried to answer at the HYD@25 conclave held on Monday was, what does Hyderabad need to do to become a truly global city when India completes 100 years of independence in 2047. For a quarter-century, The Times of India has recorded Hyderabad's relentless rise into a major metropolis and documented the many milestones that have shaped its streets, skyline, and soul. But the conclave focussed on the future, bringing together thinkers, planners, entrepreneurs, and city leaders to explore the burning questions of the city. Discussions ranged from infrastructure and public transport to healthcare, technology, and sustainable growth. The conclave stressed that planning for 2047 could not ignore the foundations laid over the last 25 years, every decision today is a thread in the fabric of tomorrow's city. The panellists grappled with issues like affordable healthcare and providing quality education, improving infrastructure and the steps needed to attract investments into Hyderabad. Through debate, dialogue, and ideas, HYD@25 offered to paint a vision, rooted in history, for a Hyderabad ready to step into the next chapter of its story. HYD@25 was powered by Renova Hospitals with Shapoorji Pallonji, Bower School of Entrepreneurship and ASKOXY.AI as associate sponsors.

items.title: Pahalgam attack: Terrorist harbourers remanded in 5-day NIA custody
items.story: A Jammu court has granted the National Investigation Agency (NIA) a five-day remand for two men arrested for harboring Pakistani terrorists involved in the Pahalgam massacre on April 22. Parvaiz Ahmad Jothar and Bashir Ahmad Jothar allegedly provided shelter, food, and logistical support to the terrorists at a seasonal hut before the attack in Baisaran Valley. NIA had arrested the duo — Parvaiz Ahmad Jothar from Batkote, Pahalgam, and Bashir Ahmad Jothar from Hill Park, Pahalgam — on Sunday in the first major breakthrough in the investigations into the terror attack that left 26 dead and 16 injured. Both were produced in the court of the Additional Sessions Judge, Jammu, who remanded them in NIA custody till June 27. Before the attack, Parvaiz and Bashir had sheltered three armed terrorists at a seasonal dhok (hut) at Hill Park. They also provided the terrorists with food and logistical support, facilitating them to execute the killings at Baisaran Valley by selectively targeting tourists based on their religious identity, NIA investigation has so far revealed. NIA claimed that the arrested duo, during questioning, had disclosed the identities of the three terrorists involved in the attack, and confirmed that the trio was from Pakistan and was affiliated with the proscribed Lashkar-e-Taiba outfit.

items.title: Indian forces ready to face any hostile nation boldly, says Rajnath Singh
items.story: NEW DELHI: Describing the UN Security Council's recent decision to appoint Pakistan as the vice chair of its counter-terrorism committee as "a cruel joke", defense minister Rajnath Singh said the world must put strategic, diplomatic, and economic pressure on Islamabad which continues to provide safe haven to terror organizations. Initiating the debate on Operation Sindoor in RS, Singh also said the "day is not far" when the people of Pakistan-occupied-Kashmir will willingly "return home" and become a part of India. Though he did not name China, which actively helped Pakistan during the May 7-10 cross-border hostilities with even "live" satellite inputs on Indian military deployments, Singh said, "We know which country was doing what during Operation Sindoor." "Not only Pakistan, but every country that looks at India with ill-intent should understand that today, our armed forces have the strength & capability to deal with any situation...Through Op Sindoor, we have also sent a message to the powers that were encouraging Pakistan," he added. While repeating most of what he said in Lok Sabha on Monday, including that Operation Sindoor had been only paused for now after achieving politico-military objectives, Singh made special mention of UNSC's decision to make Pakistan vice chair of the counter-terror panel, calling it "very unfortunate" and a "mockery" of the global fight against terrorism. "This panel was formed after 9/11. And we all know who carried out 9/11 attacks. It is also no secret Pakistan harbored the mastermind (Osama bin Laden) of that attack. This is like asking a cat to guard the milk. This decision is not only shocking but also reflects the seriousness of an organization like UN on the issue of terrorism," he said. Pakistan is a country where declared terrorists like Hafiz Saeed and Masood Azhar roam freely and spew venom, and Army officers offer prayers at funerals of terrorists. "Now, the same Pakistan is expected to lead the global community against terrorism. Is this anything less than a cruel joke?" Singh added.

items.title: Telangana: SCCL to build state’s first pumped storage plant at Medipalli mine; Rs 3,000cr green power project to reuse opencast sump water
items.story: Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) is expanding into pumped storage power by planning a 500 MW plant at Medipalli near Ramagundam. SCCL has assigned WAPCOS Limited to prepare a detailed project report for this innovative project, which involves using the existing mine water sump and constructing a new surface reservoir. The project will pump water uphill using solar energy during the day. At night, the water will be released back down through pipes, turning turbines to generate power. This method is known as a pumped storage project (PSP). The Medipalli opencast mine currently has a large water sump about 157 meters deep, holding a substantial volume of water year-round. The proposed project will include building another surface reservoir of similar capacity. Water from the sump will be pumped into this surface reservoir during the day using solar energy, and at night, it will be released back down to generate power. The project is estimated to cost around Rs 3,000 crore.

items.title: Heavy rain in Hyd; officials inspect flood-prone areas
items.story: Hyderabad: Rainfall activity intensified across the state, with Hyderabad experiencing heavy rains starting after midnight on Wednesday and continuing until late afternoon before picking up again in the evening in some areas. According to data from the Telangana Development Planning Society, several parts of the city recorded notable rainfall. Shaikpet had the highest with 86.5 mm, followed by the GHMC Welfare Office in Shaikpet (70.8 mm), Tolichowki Dalit Bhavan (65 mm), Golkonda Tahsildar Office (62 mm), and Gachibowli (61.5 mm). Other zones like Serilingampally, Chandanagar, Kukatpally, Bahadurpura, and Asifnagar also experienced rainfall ranging from 30 mm to 60 mm. The rainfall was even more intense in other parts of Telangana, with Venkatapuram in Mulugu district receiving extremely heavy rainfall of 214.5 mm, followed by Bejjur in Kumuram Bheem with 201.8 mm. Mangapet and Eturnagaram mandals also exceeded 100 mm, while several areas in Bhadradri Kothagudem, Karimnagar, and Jayashankar Bhupalapally reported moderate to heavy rainfall. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has predicted generally cloudy skies over Hyderabad with chances of light to moderate rain or thundershowers accompanied by gusty winds during evening hours on Thursday. Hazy conditions are expected in the morning. In response to the weather conditions, Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) commissioner RV Karnan conducted field inspections in flood-prone areas of the city on Wednesday. The team visited multiple locations in the Serilingampally area, including Jubilee Enclave Kaman near Medicover Hospital, Tammidikunta Lake outlet near Shilparamam, and Yashoda Hospital Road near Smileline Dental. The civic chief instructed officials to construct a stormwater drain along Yashoda Road and remove solid waste dumped near Tammidikunta Lake. He also emphasized the immediate desilting of stormwater drains to prevent accumulation during future showers. HYDRAA officials also conducted site visits across affected areas to monitor road conditions and assess flood-prone areas, coordinating with civic bodies to plan interventions. Their inspections covered areas along Nallagandla, Lingampally, Hafeezpet, and Miyapur, where ongoing drain works were reviewed with instructions to expedite completion before the next spell of heavy showers.

items.title: Stock market today: Nifty50 opens above 26,000; BSE Sensex up around 300 points
items.story: Stock market today: Nifty50 and BSE Sensex, the Indian equity benchmark indices, opened in green on Wednesday. While Nifty50 went above 26,000, BSE Sensex was up around 300 points. At 9:16 AM, Nifty50 was trading at 26,013.30, up 77 points or 0.30%. BSE Sensex was at 84,910.64, up 282 points or 0.33%. Analysts maintain a positive market outlook, considering favourable global indicators, economic data and domestic second quarter performance reports. The US Federal Reserve's FOMC meeting outcome on Wednesday, with anticipated 25 basis points interest rate reduction, remains a key focus for investors. Dr. VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments Limited says, “Globally stock markets continue to be bullish aided by the sustained uptrend in the mother market US where AI related deals and news are driving tech stocks up. Today the market is likely to get another positive news from the Fed which is expected to cut rates by 25 bp. More important than the rate decision will be the Fed commentary on quantitative tightening.” “Nifty’s gain of 1300 points in the October series has strengthened the mildly bullish undertone of the market. This has the potential to continue in November helping the Nifty reach an all time high soon. The fairly-valued Nifty Bankex is well placed to lead the rally in the market. Strong and steady large cap bluechips like Bharti Airtel, RIL and L&T can lend support to the Nifty.” US stock markets saw record closing highs on Tuesday with Nvidia shares gaining after announcing AI supercomputer development for the US energy department. Investor sentiment remained positive ahead of significant megacap results. Asian stocks opened higher, supported by Wall Street's AI-driven technology sector optimism and increased expectations of Federal Reserve rate reductions. (Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India)

items.title: Rlys rationalises fares with minimal increase
items.story:
Hyderabad: Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced that the Indian Railways is offering affordable transport to over 7.2 billion passengers, with some of the lowest train fares globally, including comparisons to neighboring countries. For the fiscal year 2023-24, the passenger travel subsidy was provisionally estimated at 60,466 crore, equating to a 45% subsidy on travel costs. Essentially, if the service cost is 100, the ticket price is set at 55. This subsidy continues for all passengers, with additional concessions for certain groups such as persons with disabilities, various patient categories, and students. 

Effective July 1, 2025, fares were rationalized after more than five years, with minimal increases ranging from half a paisa to two paise per kilometer for premium classes. There is no fare increase for general class up to 500 km, beyond which there's a half paisa increase per passenger per kilometer. The sleeper class and first-class ordinary fares saw a similar increase. 

The fare revision is expected to have a negligible effect on the total subsidy, as the increase per kilometer is minimal. It is estimated that less than half of the trips will experience a slight fare increase. For instance, low-income travelers in general coaches won't see a fare increase for 500 km travel. 

Minister Vaishnaw addressed questions from 12 MPs, including Hyderabad MP Asaduddin Owaisi, in the Lok Sabha, where he also highlighted various schemes and infrastructural improvements by the railway ministry to ensure safe, comfortable, and quality services for passengers.

Additionally, Hyderabad MP Asaduddin Owaisi commented on social media about an incident involving a Kargil War veteran's family in Maharashtra who claimed harassment by Pune police and unidentified individuals demanding proof of citizenship, reflecting concerns over the treatment of veterans and issues of citizenship documentation.

items.title: 2-day TN visit: PM Modi offers prayers at Chola temple; holds roadshow in Gangaikonda Cholapuram
items.story: Prime Minister Narendra Modi celebrated the birth anniversary of Chola emperor Rajendra Chola I at the Gangaikonda Cholapuram Temple in Tamil Nadu. He offered prayers and participated in the Aadi Thiruvathirai Festival. During his two-day visit, he prayed at the Chola-era Lord Brihadeeswara temple, accompanied by Vedic and Saivite chants. PM Modi brought a 'kalasam' (metal pot) thought to contain water from the River Ganga. Dressed in traditional attire, he circumambulated the temple's inner corridor, which is part of the UNESCO heritage site of the great living Chola temples. He also conducted a prayer ceremony called 'deeparathanai.' Additionally, the Prime Minister visited an exhibition by the Archaeological Survey of India on Chola Shaivism and architecture. Earlier, Modi held a roadshow in Gangaikonda Cholapuram, where he waved at the crowd. Gangaikonda Cholapuram was built by Rajendra Chola following his successful maritime expedition to Southeast Asia about 1,000 years ago. The celebration marked 1,000 years since Rajendra Chola's expedition and the beginning of the temple's construction. Rajendra Chola I, who reigned from 1014 to 1044 CE, was a significant ruler in Indian history. Under his rule, the Chola Empire expanded across South and Southeast Asia. The temple he built became a center of Shaiva devotion, architectural brilliance, and administrative excellence for over 250 years. His empire included regions like coastal Burma, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, and the Maldives, and he conquered the kings of Srivijaya (Sumatra, Java, and Malaya) and the Pegu islands.

items.title: REVEALED! Which Test will Jasprit Bumrah play? Shubman Gill finally answers the big question
items.story: India's pace bowler Jasprit Bumrah is set to rejoin the team for the third Test against England. The match will be held at Lord's next week. Shubman Gill confirmed Bumrah's return. Bumrah was rested for the second Test as part of workload management. Three changes were made to the team for the second Test. Bumrah will return to the Indian playing eleven against England in the third Test at Lord's next week after sitting out of the second match, captain Shubman Gill said on Wednesday. Bumrah was rested from the second Test, which began here on Wednesday, as part of his workload management. He played in the first Test at Leeds which India lost by five wickets. After England put India in to bat first, Indian Test skipper Shubman Gill said: "Would've bowled first as well. If there's anything in the wicket, it's in the first day. Three changes - Reddy, Washi and Akash Deep come in." "No Bumrah. Just to manage his workload. We did get a good break and this is an important match for us. But the third Test being at Lord's, we think there'll be more in that pitch so we'll use him there. We were tempted to play Kuldeep but looking at the last match, our lower order didn't do well, so decided to add some depth to the batting," he said. The third Test is scheduled to start on July 10. The Indian team management had declared at the start of the series that Bumrah will only play in three Tests out of five. Teams: India (Playing XI): Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul, Karun Nair, Shubman Gill(c), Rishabh Pant(w), Nitish Kumar Reddy, Ravindra Jadeja, Washington Sundar, Akash Deep, Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna. England (Playing XI): Zak Crawley, Ben Duckett, Ollie Pope, Joe Root, Harry Brook, Ben Stokes(c), Jamie Smith(w), Chris Woakes, Brydon Carse, Josh Tongue, Shoaib Bashir.

items.title: Will get Fortune 500 companies to Future City in 10 yrs: Revanth
items.story:
Hyderabad: Chief minister A Revanth Reddy on Sunday stated that the Congress govt aims to attract Fortune 500 companies to Bharat Future City within 10 years, transforming it into a hub of global investment opportunities with top-tier infrastructure. Plans include bullet train connectivity from Future City to Amaravati-Chennai and Bengaluru, a 12-lane greenfield expressway to the Machilipatnam port, Metro rail connectivity to the international airport, advanced infrastructure such as an underground power supply network, drinking water, skill university, and modern governance facilities.

Addressing the gathering after performing the bhumi puja for the construction of the Future City Development Authority (FCDA) corporate office at Meerkhanpet village in Kandukur mandal of Rangareddy district, and a radial road connecting the Outer Ring Road (ORR) with the proposed Regional Ring Road (RRR), Revanth Reddy noted that currently 85 of the Fortune-500 companies were present in Hyderabad.

"The government's goal is to bring all Fortune 500 companies to Bharat Future City over the next decade," he stated.

The govt has devised ambitious plans to develop the city into a global investment hub, generating employment and providing world-class infrastructure for locals, he said.

"We have got the approval from the Centre for a greenfield 12-lane expressway from the Future City to the Machilipatnam port in AP, and bullet train to Amaravati-Chennai-Bengaluru. How long we will praise New York, Tokyo, Singapore and Dubai. Let's build our own world's best city so that people from New York, Tokyo, Dubai and Singapore will come to see our Future City," Revanth said.

He assured the public that he would work three days a month from the Future City office building starting Dec, and every investment deal would be signed in the Future City rather than the secretariat. Deputy chief minister Bhatti Vikramarka and IT, industries and Future City in charge minister D Sridhar Babu would also visit the proposed city four days a month.

"When we all start working from here, everyone including investors, officials and development will come here. When Qutb Shahs built Hyderabad city, they prayed that it should thrive with people like the countless fish in the waters," Revanth said.

The Future City's corporate office building and the skill university have been scheduled for completion in Dec. The bhumi puja for the Future City project marks a new chapter in Telangana.

Revanth announced the allotment of 10 acres in the Future City to Singareni Collieries Company Limited and instructed deputy CM to ensure its corporate office building is ready by Dec 2026.

He highlighted that while Qutb Shahis developed Hyderabad and the Nizams built Secunderabad, previous govts led by N Chandrababu Naidu and YS Rajasekhara Reddy in the undivided state established Cyberabad, Hi-Tec City, ORR and the international airport.

"In my govt, we are leading in the pharma sector and competing in IT with the world's best. We should learn from our rulers' planning in the past and lay foundations for the future, and this new city is going to be one of the best in the world with no pollution," he added.

items.title: Punjab government rolls out Land Pooling policy; promises farmer welfare and higher compensation
items.story: The Punjab government has introduced a new Land Pooling policy aimed at farmer welfare, prioritizing partnership and transparency. Under this model, farmers will receive an annual compensation of Rs 1 lakh, which is five times the amount previously given. Additionally, the policy includes a 10% annual increment in the rental sum. Farmers joining the scheme will also receive an upfront payment of Rs 50,000. Upon enrollment, they will receive a Rs 50,000 advance cheque for the first year and a Letter of Intent (LOI) within just 21 days. Farmers retain full possession of their land and can continue agricultural activities until development begins. During this time, the government will continue depositing Rs 1 lakh annually into their accounts. The model aims to eliminate middlemen, reduce corruption, and position farmers as stakeholders in the development process. Initial responses have seen significant participation, with more than 50 farmers in Mohali and over 150 acres pooled voluntarily in Patiala. Similar interest has been reported in several other regions, including Amritsar, Moga, and Sangrur. The policy is based on consent without forcible acquisition, aiming to provide fair and consistent compensation while involving farmers in the development process.

items.title: Nadda slams opposition for walkout during Shah's reply on Operation Sindoor; Kharge says protest was over insulting remark
items.story:
J P Nadda criticized the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha for walking out during Amit Shah's reply on Operation Sindoor, accusing them of double standards by demanding a response from the Prime Minister. Mallikarjun Kharge stated the walkout was a protest against Shah's remark. Nadda accused the Opposition parties of displaying double standards by staging the walkout as Amit Shah began replying to the Operation Sindoor debate in the Rajya Sabha, insisting that the reply come from the Prime Minister. Nadda cited a precedent from the UPA government, when discussions on the home ministry's statement on the 2008 terrorist attacks in Mumbai were replied to by the then Prime Minister and Home Minister in the Lok Sabha and the then Home Minister in the Rajya Sabha. 

Leader of Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge, however, said the opposition had not walked out against Shah's replying to the debate but to protest his specific remark that 'main akela hi apko nipat lunga' (I can handle you myself). 'He insulted all of us, and we protested against that,' said Kharge. 'We said the Prime Minister is here, please call him to the House,' he noted. Earlier, Nadda sought to remind the Opposition that the Chair had made it clear during the business advisory committee (BAC) meeting and in the House that it is the prerogative of the government to decide which minister should speak and reply to the discussion in the House. 

'Nadda said the opposition parties had demanded a discussion and to elicit information on Operation Sindoor. However, when the opportunity came, they chose to walk out without listening to the reply by the Home Minister. Their demand yesterday was clearly misplaced and it displays their double standards, given the precedent,' said Nadda. The House was adjourned soon after amid uproar by the opposition parties. The scene was no different post-recess, as the opposition resumed their protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Bihar and demanded that the Prime Minister come to the House. 

Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the Prime Minister had already replied to the debate in the Lok Sabha for 1 hour and 42 minutes on Tuesday. 'He presented all the facts to the nation through the House. The Home Minister is capable of replying to the debate,' Rijiju said. He said the government has a collective responsibility, and the Opposition does not get to decide who will speak. With the opposition members continuing to protest, the House was adjourned first till 4:30 PM and then after Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal made a suo motu statement on the US tariff announcement, asserting that India will take all necessary steps to protect its national interest.

items.title: Pakistan's gold medallist Arshad Nadeem hits out at false promises: 'Every plot announcement was fake'
items.story:
Pakistani Olympic champion Arshad Nadeem, who won gold at the Paris Games with an Olympic record throw of 92.97m, has voiced concerns over unfulfilled promises of land plots made after his victory. Despite receiving cash prizes, the plot announcements remain unfulfilled. Nadeem specifically points to issues regarding these promised land plots, stating that all the plot announcements were fake, which he did not receive. Apart from that, he mentioned receiving all the cash prizes that were announced. This achievement marked Pakistan's first gold medal in track and field, leading to numerous rewards from government authorities, provincial bodies, and private organizations. 

Despite these challenges, Nadeem remains committed to his preparation for the upcoming World Championships in September. He stated that his entire focus is on himself, but also mentioned training any youth who comes for training, which is provided by his coach Salman Butt.

Recent reports indicate that Nadeem has undergone successful muscle surgery in the United Kingdom due to a calf injury that has kept him away from competitions. The surgery was performed in Cambridge under Dr. Ali Bajwa's supervision, where medical experts discovered partial damage to the 28-year-old's calf muscle, requiring immediate surgical intervention. His coach, Butt, expressed uncertainty about the timeline for recovery.

Nadeem is expected to compete against Neeraj Chopra at the Diamond League event in Silesia, Poland, on August 16, marking their first face-off since the Paris Olympics.

items.title: Who has Megan Thee Stallion dated before Klay Thompson? A timeline of her past relationships and rumored flings
items.story: Megan Thee Stallion, a Grammy-winning rapper, is currently dating NBA player Klay Thompson. This news comes after a series of high-profile relationships and rumored flings. Megan has been linked to several athletes and entertainers over the years. Some confirmed relationships include Moneybagg Yo and Pardison Fontaine, while rumored flings involved Romelu Lukaku and G-Eazy. Her relationship with Moneybagg Yo became public in 2019 but ended in 2020. A controversial involvement with Tory Lanez in 2020 ended dramatically after Lanez allegedly shot her in the foot. Despite being seen together, Megan denied dating G-Eazy in 2020, stating they were just friends. She dated Pardison Fontaine from 2021 to 2023, but they split due to cheating allegations. Rumors about her relationship with Romelu Lukaku surfaced in 2023, and with Torrey Craig in 2024, both of which ended. Megan's relationship with Klay Thompson is now confirmed, with the couple making public appearances in New York City, further solidifying their status as a power couple.

items.title: 'We will revoke your US Visa and deport you immediately if you Do Not ...': US Embassy in India
items.story: The US Embassy in India has issued a solemn warning to visa holders, emphasizing that scrutiny continues even after visas are issued. Authorities continuously monitor compliance with US laws and immigration rules, with potential consequences including visa revocation and deportation for any violations. In a recent post on the microblogging platform X (formerly known as Twitter), the embassy stated that US authorities continue to monitor visa holders even after a visa has been granted. The post from the official U.S. Embassy India handle read: "U.S. visa screening does not stop after a visa is issued. We continuously check visa holders to ensure they follow all U.S. laws and immigration rules – and we will revoke their visas and deport them if they don’t." This statement serves as a reminder to Indian nationals, particularly students and workers heading to the US, that visa approval is not a guarantee of permanent entry or stay. It underscores the importance of compliance with US laws, including immigration, academic, and employment regulations. The embassy's post comes at a time when U.S. authorities have reportedly increased scrutiny of international travelers amid concerns over visa fraud, overstaying, and misuse of student and work visas. Although the embassy did not cite specific cases, officials have emphasized in the past that any violation, such as false claims in applications or unauthorized employment, can lead to visa cancellation, detention, or deportation. The embassy previously shared a post stating: "Omitting social media information could lead to visa denial and ineligibility for future visas." The post further added, "Visa applicants are required to list all social media usernames or handles of every platform they have used from the last 5 years on the DS-160 visa application form." The US government has shared new guidelines for F, M, and J non-immigrant visa applicants, requiring them to adjust the privacy settings on all their social media accounts to public to facilitate vetting necessary to establish their identity and admissibility to the United States under U.S. law. This move is likely aimed at reinforcing legal compliance and deterring misuse of the US visa system. Applicants are advised to provide truthful information during the application process and adhere strictly to the terms of their visa while in the US, reporting any changes in status, such as switching jobs or dropping out of a course, to immigration authorities to avoid complications.

items.title: Fans melt over Darnell Nurse’s Wife’s wedding kiss post while the Edmonton Oilers might be planning his exit
items.story:
Darnell Nurse is currently in the spotlight for both a heartwarming occasion and some trade discussions. His wife, Mikayla Nurse, recently shared a beautiful Instagram post featuring a kiss between them at the wedding of former Oilers teammate Warren Foegele. The caption, "It's the season of love [heart emoji]," resonated with fans, highlighting the couple's affection. However, behind this lovely moment, the Edmonton Oilers might be considering a significant move regarding Nurse's future with the team. 

As fans were charmed by the wedding kiss, a different narrative was unfolding behind the scenes. On his "32 Thoughts" podcast, Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman, who is noted for being a top insider in the NHL, revealed that the Edmonton Oilers had approached several players with no-trade clauses, including Darnell Nurse, to assess their willingness to waive these clauses. Friedman mentioned, "I think basically Edmonton went to check with all their guys who had no-trade clauses, who they would want to move and said, ‘Okay, how many of you are willing to go places?’ ... But, you know, Nurse, I don’t think he wants to go anywhere." This revelation marks the first credible indication that the Oilers might be contemplating a trade involving Nurse, a key player in their defense. 

Friedman did not specify that the team explicitly asked Nurse to waive his clause, but the act of checking indicates they are weighing their options. Nurse was drafted seventh overall in the 2013 NHL Draft and has been a foundational player in the team’s defense for over a decade. Across 716 career games—all with Edmonton—he's accumulated 300 points, with 81 goals and 219 assists.

In the 2024-25 season, Nurse had one of his best performances, registering 33 points (5 goals, 28 assists) in 76 games, with a plus-11 rating, 188 shots on goal, and 72 penalty minutes, averaging 22:22 of ice time per game. Despite this success, his $9.25 million per year contract, signed in 2021 and lasting until the 2029-30 season, has sparked discussions. The eight-year, $74 million deal includes a full no-movement clause that transitions into a no-trade clause in the final three years. 

With a fixed salary cap and high expectations, backed by stars like Connor McDavid, the Oilers might be seeking to clear some cap space. Nurse’s $9.25 million AAV is substantial, and trading him could allow the team to bolster their roster for a Stanley Cup run.

items.title: Where no one goes: Inside Delhi's death dive squad; 102 bodies pulled out from waterbodies this year till now
items.story:
In the polluted waters of Delhi, a team of 15 dedicated divers work tirelessly to recover bodies, often without protective gear. These divers, descendants of farmers from the Yamuna floodplain, have retrieved 102 corpses in 2025 alone, facing dangers such as toxic chemicals, snake bites, and hazardous currents. With farming banned due to pollution, diving remains their sole means of livelihood.

From the filth-clogged drains and toxic canals, these bare-bodied divers pull out the capital's deceased, whether drowned, dumped, or disappeared. They dive without gear, gloves, or complaints, retrieving bloated corpses from open drains, battling suffocating foam in polluted rivers, snake bites, and the unbearable stench of decay.

In the first six months of 2025, the team has extracted 102 bodies from Delhi's water bodies, with 32 recoveries in May alone, most from a single canal in northwest Delhi's Bawana. Based at a boat club in Civil Lines, north Delhi, the team responds to calls from the police, fire services, and disaster response teams, often involving suicides or bodies in gunny bags.

These calls come from across the capital, including Jaitpur, Kondli, Najafgarh Drain, Bhalswa Lake, and the entire Yamuna stretch. The divers enter drains filled with garbage and dead animals, closing their eyes underwater due to dirt and chemicals. Shabir Ahmed, diving since age 15, shared, "We shut our eyes and feel our way forward, hoping not to touch a dead animal or sharp object. If it's a body, we hold on tight."

Despite the risks, including currents that trap divers and snake bites, they continue their work. Harish, who oversees the boat club, noted the constant danger but emphasized their commitment, even on holidays. Last year, the team recovered 232 bodies.

The divers, raised on the Yamuna floodplain, inherited this work from their ancestors. With farming banned, diving remains their livelihood. They learned by watching their elders and continue despite the challenges, aiming to bring closure to grieving families.

items.title: Telangana HC notice to IAS officer: Y Srilakshmi gets 5 days to reply; fresh hearing in mining case July 1
items.story: The Telangana High Court has issued a notice to IAS officer Y Srilakshmi, giving her five days to respond to the Central Bureau of Investigation's (CBI) counter-affidavit in an illegal mining case. The CBI has accused Srilakshmi of favoring Gali Janardhan Reddy's Obulapuram Mining Company by facilitating iron ore mining leases in 2004, during her time as secretary of the Andhra Pradesh industries and mines department. The high court made it clear that no further extensions for her response would be granted beyond the given time frame. The case is set for a fresh hearing on July 1, following directions from the Supreme Court.

items.title: Parliamentary panel on I-T Bill backs time-bound resolution of tax cases
items.story:
A parliamentary panel has recommended a time-bound resolution of tax litigation as part of its 285 recommendations on the Income Tax Bill, 2025. This bill aims to simplify and modernize the tax laws and has been reviewed by a select committee from the Lok Sabha. The committee, led by BJP's Baijayant Panda, has already had 250 of its recommendations accepted by the government. The draft legislation is expected to be presented to the House on July 21, the first day of the Parliament's monsoon session. The committee emphasizes the need for quick resolution of tax disputes, noting that there have been significant improvements, particularly in the area of refunds.

The new Income Tax Bill aims to eliminate redundant provisions and has reduced the document size from 850 to 600 pages. It follows three core principles: textual and structural simplification for clarity and coherence, no major tax policy changes to maintain continuity, and no changes to tax rates to ensure predictability for taxpayers. The bill also focuses on removing obsolete provisions and reorganizing sections for better navigation and accessibility, while preserving existing taxation principles. This reflects the government's commitment to making the tax framework simpler and clearer, enhancing the ease of doing business.

Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has stated that the new IT Bill is designed to be relevant for the 21st century. CBDT Chairman Ravi Agrawal also highlighted that the simplification in language and presentation is expected to bring more clarity to the system, reducing litigation.

items.title: 'Sanatan ka apmaan nahi sahenge': Lawyer hurls shoe towards CJI Gavai in SC; how he reacted
items.story: NEW DELHI: A shoe was hurled towards Chief Justice of India (CJI) BR Gavai on Monday, allegedly in protest against his recent 'go ask your deity' remark made while hearing a plea seeking reconstruction of a Lord Vishnu idol in Madhya Pradesh’s Khajuraho. An advocate, who was heard shouting slogans, was quickly escorted out of the courtroom by security personnel. The incident caused a brief interruption for a few minutes in proceedings before the session resumed, reported Live Law. According to lawyers present, the individual shouted, 'Sanatan Dharam ka apmaan nahi sahega Hindustan' ('India will not tolerate disrespect towards Sanatan Dharma') while being removed from the courtroom. Some witnesses claimed he tried to throw a shoe, while others said he appeared to be hurling a roll of paper. The man was reportedly dressed in a lawyer's robe. Reacting to the incident, CJI Gavai said: 'Don't get distracted by all this. We are not distracted. These things do not affect me.' Terming it a 'publicity interest litigation', the Supreme Court last month dismissed a plea seeking directions to reconstruct and reinstall a seven-foot idol of Lord Vishnu at the Javari Temple, part of the UNESCO World Heritage Khajuraho temple complex in MP. A bench headed by Chief Justice B R Gavai and Justice K Vinod Chandran refused to entertain the plea filed by one Rakesh Dalal, who sought the replacement and consecration of the damaged idol at the Javari Temple in Chhatarpur district. 'This is purely publicity interest litigation... Go and ask the deity himself to do something. If you are saying you are a strong devotee of Lord Vishnu, then you pray and do some meditation,' the CJI said. The petitioner's counsel said the idol's head was dilapidated & urged SC to intervene to allow its reconstruction. SC said the issue squarely fell under Archaeological Survey of India's jurisdiction. 'It's an archaeological find, whether ASI would permit such a thing to be done or not... there are various issues,' CJI said. The CJI added, 'In the meantime, if you are not averse to Shaivism, you can go and worship there... there is a very big linga of Shiva, one of the biggest in Khajuraho.'

items.title: 'Govt being bullied by buffoon-in-chief': Owaisi takes dig at Centre over Trump's 25% tariff; questions PM Modi's silence
items.story:
NEW DELHI: AIMIM leader Asaduddin Owaisi criticized the Indian government led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi following US President Donald Trump's announcement of a 25% tariff on India. Owaisi described the situation as 'sad,' pointing out that the current administration is being 'bullied by a buffoon-in-chief in the White House.' Trump's announcement, made on the Truth Social platform, accused India of imposing 'the most strenuous and obnoxious non-monetary Trade Barriers of any Country.' Owaisi questioned PM Modi's silence, asking if the 25% tariff was the result of the '56-inch chest' promise or if the nation would have to wait for tariffs to reach 56%. 

Owaisi expressed his concern that the tariff would impact Indian MSMEs, manufacturers, IT firms, service providers, and even farmers. He also highlighted the potential deterrent effect on FDI, damage to exports, and job losses. Owaisi compared India's situation with other countries, noting that Japan, Vietnam, and Indonesia face lower tariffs of 15%, 20%, and 19% respectively. 

The announcement sparked political controversy in India, with opposition leaders raising questions in Parliament. Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge criticized PM Modi's 'silence' over Trump's statements, describing the tariff as a severe blow to India's National Policy of Strategic Autonomy. Kharge also pointed out the potential negative impact on trade, particularly on MSMEs and farmers, and highlighted previous government efforts to negotiate a trade deal with the US. He questioned the reasons given by Trump for the tariff, including India's oil imports from Russia, weapons purchases from Russia, membership in BRICS, and BRICS' impact on the US dollar. Kharge concluded by reflecting on India's history of non-alignment in foreign policy and the current government's departure from this tradition.

items.title: IND vs ENG: Indian team breaks multiple records — most individual centuries, 350+ totals and more
items.story:
India's batting prowess shone brightly in the Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy, securing a draw in the fourth Test at Old Trafford and rewriting record books. Washington Sundar's century contributed to India equaling their record of 11 centuries in a series, matching their 1978-79 feat against West Indies. The team also set a new record with seven 350-plus totals, surpassing Australia's previous best.

India's batting juggernaut rolled on in the Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy as the team not only salvaged a memorable draw in the fourth Test at Old Trafford but also etched its name across several pages of Test cricket's record books. When Washington Sundar calmly raised his bat after completing his maiden Test century on the final day in Manchester, he wasn't just celebrating a personal milestone — he was helping India equal one of their oldest Test records. His hundred was the 11th individual century by an Indian batter in this series, drawing level with the tally set way back during the 1978-79 home series against West Indies.

From the very start of this five-Test epic, India's batters have stood tall in hostile English conditions. Whether it was the youthful exuberance of Yashasvi Jaiswal, the experienced calm of KL Rahul, or the leadership of Shubman Gill, everyone has made their contributions count. The sheer number of big scores under pressure has helped India mount totals not often associated with touring sides in England.

In fact, India now hold the record for most 350-plus totals in a single Test series by any team. Their seven such scores have eclipsed Australia's previous best of six, achieved thrice during their dominant Ashes campaigns in 1920-21, 1948, and 1989. The fourth Test also witnessed a rare statistical gem: it was the first time three Indian batters – Gill, Jadeja and Washington – scored centuries in the same second innings of a Test. Their composure and grit, especially after India had slumped to 0 for 2 in the first over, was a testament to the maturity this new generation of Indian batters has developed.

Further underlining their dominance, India batted out five sessions without losing a wicket, the most by any team in a single Test match since Pakistan's six-session resistance against Australia in 2022. For a team chasing a 311-run deficit, that kind of application was nothing short of remarkable.

India also became only the fourth team in their own Test history to avoid defeat after conceding a first-innings lead of over 300 — another marker of their fighting spirit. With the series still alive at 2-1 in favour of England and the final Test at The Oval looming, India not only have the chance to level the series but also to break more records — including setting a new benchmark for most hundreds in a single Test series.

items.title: Telangana mulls reintroducing ban on toddy shops within ORR limits
items.story: Following a series of fatalities linked to adulterated toddy, the Telangana government is considering reinstating a ban on toddy compounds within the limits of the Outer Ring Road (ORR). This move mirrors a 2004 ban implemented by the then Chief Minister, the late YS Rajasekhara Reddy, following a similar tragedy. Authorities suggest that eliminating toddy shops within the ORR is necessary to tackle the issue of adulteration. There is a potential plan to revoke Tree for Toddy (TFT) licenses in areas such as Medchal and Shamshabad. The excise department is currently evaluating the situation and will submit a report soon.
