Despite the 2004 ban, the operations resumed after the formation of Telangana, and the BRS government subsequently lifted the prohibition on selling toddy in the city. Presently, there is an extensive network of 454 toddy compounds operated by 390 societies across the region, with a significant presence in Hyderabad, Secunderabad, Malkajgiri, Medchal, Saroornagar, and Shamshabad. Additionally, the state government is considering canceling liquor licenses of several stations in Hyderabad, Secunderabad, and Rangareddy due to the challenges faced in preventing the use of hazardous chemicals in toddy production. The excise department has been tasked with compiling reports on the current situation.

items.title: IND vs ENG 2nd Test: Historic fightback! Shubman Gill's record-breaking 269 powers India's greatest recovery
items.story: India staged a remarkable recovery in the second Test against England by scoring 587 runs after being at a precarious 211/5. Shubman Gill led the charge with a magnificent 269, marking his maiden Test double century. He was supported by Yashasvi Jaiswal, who scored 87, and Ravindra Jadeja, who added 89. This effort helped India surpass their previous record of the most runs scored after the fall of the fifth wicket in a Test innings, previously 370 against West Indies in Kolkata in 2013. This remarkable innings saw Gill become the first Indian and Asian captain to score a Test double hundred in England, surpassing Sunil Gavaskar's 221 at The Oval in 1979. India posted their sixth 500-plus total by a visiting team at Edgbaston, the first since South Africa's 594/5 declared in 2003. In response, England found themselves struggling at 77/3, trailing by 510 runs, after Akash Deep's two quick wickets.

items.title: RBI eases lending norms, tightens financial oversight
items.story: MUMBAI: RBI has set about easing lending norms while tightening its financial oversight. Its latest rules promise cheaper and more flexible loans for borrowers, wider access to credit against gold, and easier capital-raising avenues for banks. Draft proposals, meanwhile, would extend repayment terms, sharpen exposure limits and quicken credit reporting to bureaus to weekly from monthly — measures that collectively modernise bank lending. Late on Monday, RBI unveiled seven directions for lenders — three binding from Oct 1st and four open for consultation until Oct 20. The immediate changes grant banks more leeway in lending. Interest-rate spreads — the gap between the benchmark and loan rate — can be adjusted sooner, with certain borrower charges cut at any time rather than locked in for three years. Banks may also, if they wish, let personal-loan customers switch from floating to fixed rates at reset points — which is a flexibility and not a mandate. Gold and silver lending has been broadened. Working-capital loans, once limited to jewellers, can now flow to all manufacturers using bullion as raw material. Smaller urban co-operatives in tier-3 and -4 cities have been allowed into the business too, extending credit’s reach. Capital rules have been eased. RBI has relaxed restrictions on the use of foreign-currency and overseas-rupee bonds as additional tier-1 capital.

items.title: ED arguments over in Herald case, it's Gandhis' turn now
items.story: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) argued in a Delhi court that the National Herald case is a clear example of money laundering. They alleged Young Indian Pvt Ltd, involving Sonia and Rahul Gandhi, was established to illegally transfer Rs 2,000 crore from Associated Journals Ltd (AJL). According to the ED, Young Indian, where Sonia and Rahul Gandhi held a 76% stake, was created to launder money from AJL, the publisher of the 'National Herald' newspaper. The additional solicitor general, SV Raju, representing the ED, asked the court to acknowledge the chargesheet. The court was considering whether to take cognisance of the charges against Sonia and Rahul Gandhi in the money laundering case. The ED completed its arguments, and Sonia Gandhi's lawyer, Abhishek Manu Singhvi, was scheduled to present on Friday. The ED claimed that Sonia and Rahul Gandhi were the beneficial owners of Young Indian and had ultimate control after other shareholders' deaths. Raju alleged that Sonia and Rahul Gandhi controlled the All India Congress Committee, which facilitated a Rs 90 crore loan to AJL, a company with assets worth Rs 2,000 crore, for only Rs 50 lakh. This debt was reportedly converted into equity in favour of Young Indian. Raju alleged that the shareholding was nominal and that other accused were merely figureheads for the Gandhi family. The ED claimed Young Indian gained Rs 2,000 crore wrongfully, depriving AJL's shareholders of their rights. The court questioned the absence of AJL's shareholders as witnesses. The ASG responded by stating that the evidence spoke for itself, labelling the Gandhis and others as the real culprits once the corporate veil is pierced. Currently, Sonia and Rahul Gandhi hold almost all the shares, making them the company's beneficial owners.

items.title: IND vs ENG 2nd Test: Historic First! India join fabled 1000-club in Tests, smash record for most runs in first two matches of a series
items.story: Led by captain Shubman Gill, Team India made history at Edgbaston by becoming the first Indian side to score over 1,000 runs in a single Test match against England. This achievement, marking only the sixth instance in Test cricket history, saw India amass a total of 1,014 runs across both innings of the second Test. India joins an elite group of teams in the "1000-club," alongside England, Australia, Pakistan, and South Africa. During this historic match, India posted scores of 587 all out in the first innings and 427/6 declared in the second innings, setting England a target of 608 runs. Captain Shubman Gill led with a remarkable 269 runs in the first innings, supported by strong performances from Ravindra Jadeja and Washington Sundar. In the second innings, Gill continued his excellent form, further aided by contributions from Rishabh Pant and KL Rahul. India's total of 1,849 runs in the first two Tests of the series is the highest ever recorded by any team in the initial two matches of a Test series, showcasing their batting dominance.

items.title: ABHISHEK BACHCHAN UNPLUGGED (Part 2): 'For us Amitabh Bachchan is a hero, but he's allowed to be human, he's a father, a grandfather' - EXCLUSIVE
items.story: Abhishek Bachchan reflects on his 25-year career in the film industry, revealing his thoughts on personal growth and artistic evolution. He shares that he would perform better if given the chance to re-shoot the film 'Guru,' and discusses the importance of staying relevant and continuously reinventing oneself. Abhishek talks about his father's influence, Amitabh Bachchan, and the role of family in his life. He acknowledges the challenges of dealing with public failure and social media trolling, emphasizing the need to stay positive and focus on personal growth. The interview also touches on Abhishek's thoughts on fame, the impact of his parents' pride, and his views on the importance of audience validation. He concludes by stating the transient nature of fame and the personal satisfaction derived from his work.

items.title: CM Pushkar Singh Dhami directs IAS officers to adopt villages where they have started service for development
items.story: To include Uttarakhand among the leading states of the country, Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami has taken up the task of comprehensive development of the state's remote villages. CM Dhami directed the officers of the Indian Administrative Service to adopt the villages where they began their service. Under this scheme, officers have started working towards the development of these adopted villages. Many officers have closely understood the villagers' lives and their problems by staying overnight in the villages. Once the officers formulate an action plan, the state government will implement it through a campaign aimed at village development. CM Dhami expected IAS officers with a grade-pay of Rs 8700 or more to adopt their initial work area. Accordingly, 40 senior IAS officers of Uttarakhand have adopted their first place of appointment. An order to this effect was issued by Chief Secretary Anand Bardhan on May 20, 2025. All officers were asked to comment on the changes in their initial work areas, assessing how much development has occurred and how resources such as CSR could further enhance the social and economic development of these villages. The officers also have to prepare an action plan for the full utilization of funds from the district plan, state sector, and finance commission. In line with Chief Minister Dhami's expectations, senior IAS officers have started working on these objectives. By preparing a development plan for remote villages, the officers aim for systematic development. They are also receiving support from local public representatives and voluntary organizations.

items.title: Beyond permitted period: Supreme Court seeks removal of ex-CJI Chandrachud from official residence 'without further delay'; writes to Centre
items.story: In an unprecedented move, the Supreme Court administration has requested the Centre to reclaim the official residence of former Chief Justice of India (CJI) DY Chandrachud at Krishna Menon Marg in New Delhi. A letter dated July 1 was sent to the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) noting that Chandrachud has overstayed beyond the permissible period. Chandrachud served as the 50th CJI from November 2022 to 2024. The current CJI, BR Gavai, assumed office in May as the 52nd CJI. The Supreme Court requested that Bungalow No.5 be returned to the court's housing pool without delay since Chandrachud's permission expired on May 31. According to the Supreme Court Judges (Amendment) Rules, 2022, a retired CJI can retain a type VII bungalow for six months post-retirement. Ex-CJI Sanjiv Khanna, Chandrachud's successor, and current CJI BR Gavai did not move into the official residence. Chandrachud had previously requested to stay in the Krishna Menon Marg residence till April 2025 due to renovation at his new residence. His request was approved with conditions by then-CJI Khanna, and MoHUA approved the extension. The Supreme Court's letter highlighted breaches of timelines and legal frameworks and noted that the residence was permitted due to special circumstances. Informal extensions have been granted to former CJIs in the past. Chandrachud cited the need to make the Tughlak Road Bungalow suitable for his daughters with special needs as a reason for the delay in vacating.

items.title: Compensation for dog bite cases: In Kerala HC, state proposes setting up district-level committees
items.story:
Kochi: The state government has submitted a proposal before the high court to establish district-level committees for managing dog bite compensation cases, replacing the Justice Siri Jagan Committee, which ceased functioning following a 2024 directive from the Supreme Court. According to the proposal, each district-level committee would include the district legal services authority (DLSA) secretary, district medical officer (DMO), and joint director of the local self-government department (LSGD). This suggestion came in response to several petitions seeking the high court's intervention to curb stray dog attack incidents. 
The bench of Justice C S Dias accepted the state's suggestion and directed the government to file a counter-affidavit detailing the estimated stray dog population in Kerala, the actual statistics of dog bite incidents and deaths, the number of local self-government institutions (LSGIs) in the state, and the extent to which they have implemented the Animal Birth Control (ABC) Rules, 2023. 
The high court also inquired whether stray dog attacks could be brought within the purview of the State Disaster Management Act, similar to wild animal attacks, at least for the purpose of compensation payments. The bench involved the state police chief in the matter, seeking details such as how many FIRs have been registered concerning dog bite incidents. It was observed that when an animal attacks a human, the custodian is held responsible, and in the case of stray dogs, the LSGD secretary would be treated as the custodian. 
During the hearing, the court noted that, according to reports, there had been 16 deaths and over one lakh dog bite cases in Kerala in the past six months, and that the stray dog population was said to be around 50 lakh. The court described the situation as very alarming. However, the additional advocate general raised doubts about these figures, claiming that the actual number of stray dogs might be only two to three lakh. The court adjourned the matter to August 11. 
"Humans and animals must coexist," the court remarked. During the hearing, a counsel questioned the implementation of the euthanasia provisions under the ABC Rules, 2023. In response, the high court orally asked, "Have you been bitten by a dog? ...Last month, a child from Kannur died of rabies despite being vaccinated. Only when you are bitten do you truly understand the pain and the suffering. It is very easy to stand outside and say these things." 
The court added that while humans and animals must coexist, a practical solution to the growing problem is essential. It remarked that human rights override animal rights. 
The high court also took note of the apex court, on Monday, initiating suo motu proceedings based on a TOI report regarding the death of a child in Delhi due to rabies.

items.title: IND vs ENG: 211 and counting! Joe Root leaves Rahul Dravid behind - WATCH
items.story: On Day 2 of the third Test at Lord's, Joe Root produced a moment of brilliance to dismiss Karun Nair and etch his name further into cricketing history. Positioned at first slip, Root took a sharp one-handed catch diving to his right after Nair edged a short-of-a-length delivery from Ben Stokes. It was Root’s 211th catch in Test cricket, taking him past India’s Rahul Dravid (210) to top the list for most outfield catches in the format. \nKarun Nair, who looked composed during his stay, made 40 off 62 balls, including four boundaries, before falling to Root’s brilliance. Earlier in the day, India’s pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah delivered a sensational spell to earn his name on the prestigious Lord’s Honours Board, claiming 5 for 74 as England were bowled out for 387 in 112.3 overs. Bumrah, operating with pace and precision, ran through England’s middle order during a fiery morning session. He removed overnight centurions Joe Root and Ben Stokes inside the first half-hour and went on to dismiss Chris Woakes and Jamie Smith to complete his 15th five-wicket haul in Tests — his 13th outside India, surpassing Kapil Dev’s previous record of 12 overseas fifers. \nDespite Root’s majestic 104 — his 37th Test century, 11th against India and eighth at Lord’s — England found themselves in trouble at 271/7. However, Jamie Smith, dropped on 5 by KL Rahul, made the most of the reprieve with a brisk 51. He forged a crucial 84-run stand with Brydon Carse, who registered his maiden Test fifty with a fluent 56, helping England stretch their total. India also contributed to their own woes, conceding 31 extras on a warm and testing day at Lord’s.

items.title: Exclusive | How do T20 league auctions work during a busy calendar? A behind-the-scenes look as ILT20 takes the big leap
items.story:
The International League T20 (ILT20) is set to introduce a player auction for its fourth season, replacing the draft system to refresh team compositions and attract global talent. Scheduled for September, the auction aims to generate buzz and reshape squads, with the teams allowed to retain up to eight players. 

With excitement building around the fourth season of the International League T20 (ILT20), all eyes are now on a major shift in the league’s approach to squad building - the introduction of a player auction. For the first time since its inception, the UAE’s marquee franchise league will hold an auction, scheduled for September, replacing the draft system used in the first three seasons. Auctions have become a signature feature of global T20 leagues, offering drama, intrigue, and promotional buzz ahead of a new season. Player prices, bidding wars, and squad strategies often capture fan and media attention - and ILT20 is now poised to enter that high-stakes space. The upcoming auction not only aims to refresh team compositions but also to reinforce the league’s ambition of becoming one of the most global cricket competitions.

But what does it take to organise such a complex event - from creating a player pool to planning logistics for a multi-national talent assembly? To understand the mechanics and ambitions behind the ILT20's first-ever auction, TimesofIndia.com caught up with Mike Fordham, ILT20's Head of Cricket Operations. In an exclusive interview, Fordham walked us through every detail - from Right to Match to wildcard picks and UAE player development. 

What was the thought process behind introducing the auction format after three seasons of drafts? It was for a few reasons. Most of the players were originally signed on three-year contracts, and we're now at the end of that cycle. So, we felt it was a good opportunity to freshen things up and try something new. We also wanted to open up more opportunities to new players. One of our aims with ILT20 is to be the most global cricket league in the world. We felt an auction was a good way to attract talent from various parts of the world and give teams a chance to reshape their squads. This year, teams were allowed to retain or directly sign up to eight players — including a mix of international and UAE players. All six teams have filled those slots. They’ll complete their squads at the auction and are also allowed to add two wildcard signings later. Some teams have already begun that process. The auction will also serve as the launchpad for Season Four, generating buzz and giving fans something to talk about. It’s scheduled for September, ahead of the league’s December 2 start.

What goes on behind the scenes to streamline the auction process, especially around building the player pool and aligning with player availability? A lot of preparation is involved, and we have a full team managing it. First, we’re launching an online registration portal for players and agents to sign up for the auction. That will remain open for about five to six weeks, leading into late August. Once that closes, we’ll finalise the player pool. Legal documents and contracts are also being prepared. Logistically, the auction will be a large event - venue selection, top-tier auctioneer, and specialised auction software are all being handled. We're working with a leading software firm to ensure everything runs smoothly. People will travel to Dubai for the event, so all associated logistics are also being looked after. We're confident our team will deliver.

Will Right To Match (RTM) influence auction dynamics? And how do wildcard signings work? Wildcard signings occur outside the auction. Each team can sign two additional players beyond the 21-member squad at any point after the direct signing window. Some teams have started signing wildcards; others might wait closer to the season. RTM applies only to UAE players. We’ve been running a development tournament for the last two years, and this year’s edition will happen just before the auction. Each franchise has a development team - Desert Vipers, Dubai Capitals, etc. If a UAE player from a development squad enters the auction and is bid on, the original franchise will have the final right to match. This helps reinforce investment in local talent and gives development squads a tangible reward for grooming players.

Will ILT20 increase the number of UAE or associate players in the playing XI? Yes, this season we're mandating two UAE players and one associate player in the playing XI. That associate player can be from UAE or another associate nation like Namibia, Scotland, Netherlands, Nepal, or the USA. Cricket is growing rapidly, and we want to support that global expansion. Right now, cricket is a top global sport but only truly taken seriously in about a dozen countries. We want ILT20 to serve as a platform for emerging nations. Ideally, five years from now, we’d like to see more UAE and associate players in starting XIs, with overall playing standards continuing to rise.

What are the unique challenges of organising an ILT20 auction compared to other leagues? The structure of auctions is generally similar across leagues, but ILT20 had some unique challenges. Until now, we didn’t have a clearly defined window due to overlapping leagues during January. This season, we've moved it forward - starting early December and ending early January - to reduce conflicts. While the window isn’t entirely clear, availability has improved, which should boost the talent pool. The auction should run smoothly, but the league's uniqueness lies in its international appeal. Players enjoy coming to the UAE, especially during the holiday season. Great weather, world-class facilities, and family-friendly environments make it attractive. We’re leveraging that to build a strong product, and the auction is a vital part of that journey.

Will teams focus more on availability or squad dynamics during the auction? It's a mix. Ideally, teams want players available for the full season. But if a world-class player is only available for part of it, they might still sign him to get off to a strong start. For example, Sharjah Warriors have signed Tim David, one of the world’s best T20 batters. He’ll play the first half before joining the Big Bash League in Australia. Teams will replace such players mid-season if needed. International commitments - like England-Australia Test series (Ashes) - also impact availability. Teams are used to managing this and franchise cricket operates with that flexibility. Players are accustomed to flying in and out on short notice.

What can fans expect from the auction? Will it be live-streamed or offer new innovations? We're working on plans to stream the auction live on our digital platforms. It should be an exciting event for fans to watch as teams finalise their squads. There will likely be surprises and new elements. The RTM for UAE players will be an interesting dynamic. Additionally, we're introducing players from other Gulf countries, making the tournament more pan-Middle Eastern. Overall, we hope the auction provides something fresh for ILT20 and a reason for fans to stay engaged as the season build-up begins.

How has ILT20 contributed to UAE's cricket growth, particularly in player development and infrastructure? Development of local players has been a core objective. Any league, in any sport, must build a strong local base - it can’t be just about overseas stars. The UAE has long had a talented pool, partly due to its diverse population. Now, we're seeing sustained progress. Take Aayan Khan, for example. He’s been part of Gulf Giants since Season One and has worked closely with top professionals like James Vince and Chris Jordan, under Andy Flower. That exposure is invaluable. Each franchise has a minimum of four UAE players per squad - 24 in total across the league - working with coaches like Tom Moody, James Foster, and Dwayne Bravo. That elevated their performance. The UAE’s recent win over Bangladesh in a bilateral series speaks volumes. Players like Muhammad Waseem (MI Emirates) are now winning ICC Player of the Month awards. This progress is directly linked to ILT20’s environment.

items.title: CBI begins probe into custodial torture of J&K constable
items.story: A CBI team arrived in Srinagar on Monday to investigate allegations of custodial torture involving a J&K Police constable named Khursheed Ahmad Chohan in Kupwara in 2023. Following a directive from the Supreme Court, the CBI registered a case on July 26 against six J&K Police personnel, including DSP Aijaz Ahmad Naiko and SI Riyaz Ahmad, who were stationed at the Joint Interrogation Centre in Kupwara in February 2023. The First Information Report (FIR) against these officers includes charges of criminal conspiracy, attempt to murder, voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means, and wrongful confinement for more than three days. This action follows a petition filed by Chohan, which led the Supreme Court to order the CBI to register a case regarding his illegal detention and custodial torture from February 20 to February 26, 2023, at the Joint Interrogation Centre. Chohan had previously approached the J&K High Court to seek registration of an FIR, but his plea was dismissed, prompting him to take the matter to the apex court. The CBI's FIR also includes a translated complaint from Chohan’s wife, Rubeena Akhter, initially filed in Urdu on March 1, 2023. In her complaint, she alleged that her husband was illegally detained and subjected to brutal torture, including beatings with iron rods and wooden sticks, electric shocks, and being left in a near-death condition. She further alleged that his private parts were severed, iron rods were inserted into his body, red chili powder was forced into his rectum, and he was repeatedly electrocuted. The Supreme Court has instructed the CBI to arrest the responsible individuals immediately, with a deadline not exceeding one month, and has given the agency 90 days to complete the investigation.

items.title: 'Refugees or illegal entrants?' SC questions Rohingyas' status in India; outlines other issues raised in related pleas
items.story: The Supreme Court of India is set to determine the status of Rohingyas in the country, focusing on whether they should be classified as refugees or illegal immigrants. This decision is crucial as it will define their rights and protections, including the potential for deportation by the government. A bench comprising Justices Surya Kant, Dipankar Datta, and N Kotiswar Singh emphasized that the primary issue is to establish their status. If they are acknowledged as refugees, the court will then consider what protections and rights they are entitled to. Conversely, if deemed illegal entrants, the legality of their deportation by the central or state governments will be examined. Additionally, the court is addressing whether the Rohingyas residing in refugee camps have been provided with basic amenities such as water, sanitation, and education. This came to light as the bench heard a series of pleas related to the Rohingyas, which have been categorized into three groups for separate hearings scheduled on consecutive Wednesdays. The court also questioned why these petitions were grouped together, to which the petitioners' counsel replied that the issues overlapped, particularly concerning the detention of Rohingyas, which cannot be indefinite.

items.title: Watch: Rescue teams try to pull out truck after Gujarat bridge collapse; 10 dead, several injured
items.story: In Vadodara district of Gujarat, a section of the Gambhira Bridge collapsed, leading to a truck, van, and car plunging into the Mahisagar River. Rescue teams are currently on site, with ten fatalities confirmed and nine individuals hospitalized due to injuries. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has expressed condolences and announced financial aid for the victims' families. The collapse occurred around 7:30 am when the vehicles were crossing the bridge, which is a key route for transport vehicles heading to Saurashtra. The Prime Minister, currently abroad, contacted Gujarat's Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel to assess the situation. An ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh each from the PM’s National Relief Fund has been announced for the families of the deceased, and Rs 50,000 for each injured person. The Gujarat Congress criticized the state government, holding it accountable for the incident.

items.title: Component of Pulwama IED was ordered via Amazon: FATF
items.story: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF), a global organization focused on combating money laundering and terrorist financing, has expressed concerns regarding the use of e-commerce platforms and online payment services to facilitate terrorist activities. One of the cases highlighted is the 2019 Pulwama attack in India, where the Jaish-e-Muhammed (JeM) purchased a chemical via Amazon that was later used in an explosive device (IED) to kill CRPF troopers. In another instance, the lone accused in the 2022 attack on security personnel at Gorakhnath temple in UP was found to have transferred funds to the Islamic State using PayPal. These incidents reflect a growing trend of terrorists using online platforms to support their activities. The FATF report on the Pulwama attack detailed the cross-border movement of explosives into India, noting that a crucial component of the IED, aluminum powder, was procured through Amazon. Furthermore, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) found that an accused named Waiz-ul-Islam used his Amazon account to buy chemicals and accessories for making IEDs, which he then delivered to JeM terrorists. The chargesheet in this case, filed in a special court in Jammu, accused JeM chief Moulana Masood Azhar, his brothers, and others. The FATF report also mentioned the use of VPNs and third-party transactions to evade detection, with one individual making 44 payments to the Islamic State.

items.title: Olympic skier Audun Groenvold tragically dies at 49 after being struck by lightning
items.story: Norwegian Olympic ski cross medalist Audun Groenvold tragically passed away at 49 after being struck by lightning while traveling to a cabin. Despite immediate transport to the hospital, his injuries were fatal. Groenvold, known for his 2010 Vancouver Winter Olympics bronze medal, had a successful career in both alpine and freestyle skiing, leaving a significant void in Norway's skiing community. After being hit by lightning during a cabin vacation, Norwegian Olympic skier Audun Groenvold died on Tuesday evening, July 16, 2025. On Wednesday, July 17, the Norwegian Ski Federation validated the bad news. Shortly after the strike, they claimed he did not live with the injuries and was brought to the hospital. Most people know Groenvold for his ski cross bronze medal finish at the 2010 Vancouver Winter Olympics. His skiing career was long and very successful. Beginning in alpine skiing, he came third in the downhill race in Sierra Nevada, Spain, and received a World Cup podium in 1999. Claiming yet another bronze at the 2005 World Championships, later he changed to freestyle and ski cross and finished first overall in the Ski Cross World Cup in 2007. The Ski Federation described Groenvold’s passing as a huge loss to both Alpine and freestyle skiing. Federation president Tove Moe Dyrhaug said he was not just a great athlete but someone who deeply shaped Norway’s skiing culture. Audun Groenvold stayed close to the sport even after quitting professional skiing. He became a television pundit and national team coach by publicising his knowledge and passion for winter sports. For many young Norwegian skiers, he was a teacher and inspiration. His surprise demise left a hole in the Norwegian sports scene. People will remember his physical capacity in addition to his passion for the game and personality. Many Norwegians thought he was a hero for his accomplishments, which include his Olympic ski cross bronze medal in 2010. The death of Audun Groenvold has startled fans and athletes all around. Among Norway's most talented and respected Olympic athletes, he will be remembered in the skiing scene.

items.title: Destruction of CDRs raises serious doubts over integrity of 11/7 probe: HC
items.story:
The Bombay High Court has raised questions about the integrity of the Anti-Terrorism Squad's (ATS) investigation into the 11/7 Mumbai train blasts, following the destruction of crucial call data records (CDRs). The court expressed concern that the reluctance of the prosecution to present CDRs and their subsequent destruction cast doubt on the prosecution's case. The prosecution claimed that conspiracy meetings were held at a planter's residence in Bandra, attended by four accused. A witness testified about a meeting near Shams Masjid in Mira Road, where instructions were allegedly given to contact another accused. Two accused confessed to handing over a mobile phone at Lucky Hotel, Bandra. 

The High Court noted that the destroyed CDRs could have established the accused's locations and movements, which was crucial in proving the conspiracy. The first arrest in the case was linked to a mobile number from which a suspicious religious SMS was sent. The court criticized the prosecution for failing to corroborate the witness's claims with CDRs and pointed out inconsistencies in the recorded statements. The prosecution argued that the accused were trained not to use mobile phones for operational purposes. However, the absence of direct evidence and unreliable eyewitness accounts weakened the conspiracy claims.

The defense argued that the right to a fair trial was compromised due to the destruction of CDRs, which could have provided essential evidence. The court highlighted the lack of records about who ordered the CDRs' deletion and noted the prosecution's opposition to the defense's request for CDR copies under the RTI Act.

items.title: Bigg Boss 19 comes back with a new season and a new logo; watch video
items.story: Bigg Boss season 19 is set to premiere on August 30, introducing a fresh, AI-influenced theme and an extended duration. Hosted by Salman Khan, the show unveils a brand-new logo after many years, sparking excitement among fans. The redesigned house will be ready by August 20, with housemates now having a say in evictions. Season 19 of Bigg Boss has been announced and now the makers have also revealed the new logo, giving a new look to the show. The house has been redesigned and the new theme is also in talks. All the fresh details of the show have created a craze amongst the fans. Season 19 is announced to air from August 30. The theme is totally said to be integrated and influenced by Artificial Intelligence, making the show the most talked-about topic. The duration of the show has also been said to be extended. The name itself creates excitement for the fans. The promo video has been released. As tradition continues, Salman Khan will be hosting the show once again. The new logo which has been brought into action after many years is giving the show a brand-new visual, and the audience, increasing excitement. An announcement post is made by the channel on social media, unveiling the bold, new appearance and is in the spotlight. The caption of the post was, "Countdown hogaya hai shuru, hoga chaos unlock soon! Stay tuned!" It is to be seen how the logo changes the aesthetic of the show with the also powerful other significant changes. The logo is a mix of various colours like blue, white, yellow, pink, purple and more. The logo will play a crucial role in including the redefined changes added to the show. Along with other changes, it also has been decided that now, the housemates are going to have a say on who gets evicted. The Bigg Boss house will be ready by August 20 according to reports. As of yet, there has been no official confirmation on who the contestants will be or about the contestants' act date. Although the grand premiere is said to be shot with Salman Khan reportedly on August 27.

items.title: Why wasn't any FIR slapped on Justice Varma, MPs ask govt
items.story: Members of Parliament in India have questioned the government on why no First Information Report (FIR) was filed against Justice Yashwant Varma, who was allegedly found with unaccounted cash at his residence. They also raised concerns about the lack of action against Allahabad High Court Justice Shekhar Kumar Yadav, who is accused of making a hate speech. These issues are expected to be discussed in the upcoming monsoon session of Parliament. During a meeting of the parliamentary standing committee on personnel, grievances, and law and justice, several MPs advocated for legislation that would make the code of conduct for judges legally binding. The government, represented by the Department of Justice, has been asked to prepare a report on these matters for the next meeting. The committee is currently deliberating on judicial reforms and the code of conduct for the judiciary. The Justice Department’s secretary presented at the meeting, but MPs expressed concerns about whether the code is effectively implemented. They discussed issues like post-retirement employment of judges, political statements, affiliations with ideological groups, accountability, and asset declarations. Some MPs pointed out that relatives of judges are still practicing in the same courts, which they argue should not be allowed. It was suggested that judges should not accept government positions within five years of retirement, and that the President should refrain from appointing retired judges to parliamentary positions or other tasks. The MPs questioned why there had been no police case against Justice Varma and why the Supreme Court had not acted against Justice Yadav. Although the government announced plans to propose a motion to remove Justice Varma in the monsoon session, MPs believe he should have already been removed. There is currently no update on the opposition's notice in the Rajya Sabha filed last December to remove Justice Yadav.
items.relevanceReason: Moderately relevant. This news highlights potential judicial misconduct and accountability, aligning with Dr. Shashidhar’s legal background and law-and-order stance. However, it doesn’t directly involve his constituency or immediate opponents. Still, a statement emphasizing integrity in the judiciary and strict action against corruption could resonate with his support base as a law scholar and Hindutva advocate.

items.title: IND vs ENG: After Lord's defeat, Sourav Ganguly makes huge prediction on Ravindra Jadeja's Test future
items.story: Following India's narrow loss at Lord’s in the third Test against England, former India captain Sourav Ganguly shared his views on the defeat, pointing out the missed opportunity despite the batting depth in the side. He also lauded Ravindra Jadeja for his resilient knock, backed by tailenders Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Siraj in a tense finish. India suffered one of their most heartbreaking Test defeats in recent times, going down by 22 runs and falling 1-2 behind in the five-match series. Chasing 193, India were in deep trouble at 82/7 before Jadeja launched a fightback with help from Nitish Kumar Reddy, Bumrah, and Siraj. The last two batters faced a combined 84 deliveries but could only add nine runs. Siraj was eventually bowled in unfortunate fashion, ending India’s spirited chase. Speaking during a press event of the 2025 season Indian Racing Festival (IRF) Driver Draft, Ganguly admitted he was “a little bit disappointed” with India’s batting, given their performances earlier in the series. "They should have got this 190, and when you saw Jadeja guts it out and fight and score the runs, the batting quality in this team is absolutely brilliant, and I think they will be more disappointed than I am because it was an opportunity to get 2-1 up in the series against England. Two more matches to go. I am sure they have left disappointed not getting 190. Especially with the quality of batsmanship there is in the dressing room." Ganguly added that even a small contribution from the top-order could have made the difference in India’s favour. "Sad from a team's point of view, but Jadeja has been exceptional. He is going to continue to play for India as long as he bats and performs like this. He has been around for a long time. Almost 80 Test matches and more than 200 one-day games." "And now you can see if batting, bowling, fielding, you know, he's a special player and his batting has really improved over the years with experience and quality. He was actually a top-order batsmen for Saurashtra in his younger days and then became a left-arm spinner. So he has a special player and is a very important part of this team," he concluded. During the match, Jadeja also crossed a significant milestone by completing 7,000 international runs. In 361 appearances for India, he has scored 7,018 runs at an average of 33.41, including four centuries and 39 fifties in 302 innings, with a highest score of 175*. In Test cricket, Jadeja has scored 3,697 runs in 83 matches at an average of 36.97, including four hundreds and 26 fifties. His top score of 175* came in this format, which remains his most productive with the bat. So far in this series, he has scored 327 runs in six innings at a staggering average of 109.00, with four fifties and a top score of 89. He is currently the fifth-highest run-scorer in the series.

items.title: IND vs ENG: Shubman Gill shuts down Harry Brook's 'draw' talk with epic reply - WATCH
items.story: Shubman Gill's exceptional performance in the second Test match at Edgbaston has placed India in a strong position to level the series against England. Gill scored centuries in both innings, becoming the third Indian captain to achieve this feat in Test cricket, joining the ranks of Sunil Gavaskar and Virat Kohli. His efforts have helped India gain a massive lead after losing the first Test. In a light-hearted exchange, England's Harry Brook suggested accepting a draw due to impending rain, to which Gill humorously replied 'bad luck for us.' Gill's remarkable achievement also includes a double century in the first innings, making him only the ninth player in Test history to accomplish a double hundred and a century in the same match. This performance highlights Gill's impact as a captain and places him among cricket legends.

items.title: Ahmedabad plane crash: AI171 prelim report reveals 'fuel to engines cut off in 3 seconds'
items.story:
A preliminary report on the Air India AI171 crash reveals a potential fuel supply cutoff to both engines shortly after takeoff. The investigation highlights conflicting pilot statements and a possible mechanical fault with the fuel control switches, as indicated in a 2018 safety bulletin.

The investigation into the Air India flight AI171 crash in Ahmedabad has revealed an unsettling detail. Three seconds after take-off, fuel supply to both engines of the Boeing 787 Dreamliner was cut off, either by a faulty fuel supply switch or manually by one of the two pilots. The report is ambiguous on what starved the engines, but it referred to a 2018 safety bulletin that instructed airlines to look out for a possible mechanical fault with the fuel control switches, which could cut off fuel supply to the engines.

In the cockpit voice recording, one of the pilots is heard asking the other why he cut off the fuel supply. The other pilot responded that he did not do so. This is the most crucial information in the 15-page preliminary report released early Saturday by India’s Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB). The June 12 AI-171 crash killed 270 people, including 19 on the ground.

Aviation safety experts criticized the report for paraphrasing the pilots’ exchange. The accidental flip of the fuel switch was ruled out due to a lock mechanism. The report highlights a single-point failure or tampering with a critical flight system, the fuel supply cutoff switch. The possibility of inadvertent movement of the fuel control switch from "run" to "cut off" position was ruled out. The fuel control switch has a locking mechanism for added safety.

The final report into the accident, to be released on or before June 12, 2026, will likely give answers and reveal the probable cause of the crash. Most crashes are caused by a combination of several factors and multiple failures, such as the AI Express Calicut or Mangalore crash in 2020 and 2010, respectively.

While the commander of AI-171 had 15,000 hours of flying experience, including 8,600 hours on the B787, the co-pilot had 3,400 hours of experience. Senior commanders referred to another service bulletin issued jointly by the FAA and GE (engine manufacturer) in 2021. Service Bulletin FAA-2021-0273-0013 recommends the replacement of the "MN4 microprocessor on ECU" with respect to engine fuel and control. This recommendation is to address a condition that may affect flight safety.

The report said CCTV footage obtained from the airport showed the ram air turbine (RAT) being deployed during initial climb immediately after lift-off. No significant bird activity was observed in the vicinity of the flight path. The aircraft started to lose altitude before crossing the airport perimeter wall.

At this stage of the probe, no definitive cause has been determined, and no immediate safety recommendations have been issued to B787-8 or GEnx-1B engine operators.

items.title: Pahalgam attack: Two locals helped Pakistani attackers for a few thousands
items.story: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has arrested two Kashmiris for allegedly assisting Pakistani terrorists in the Pahalgam attack that led to the massacre of 26 civilians. The two locals, Parvaiz Ahmad Jothar and Bashir Ahmad Jothar, are accused of providing shelter and logistical support to three Pakistani terrorists affiliated with Lashkar. They allegedly harbored the attackers in their 'dhok' (hut) in Hill Area, located about 2 km from Baisaran, for two days before the attack. The NIA claims the locals tipped off the terrorists about the deployment of security personnel near the attack site, receiving a few thousand rupees in return. The accused were produced in the NIA court in Jammu and have been remanded to NIA custody for five days. The agency is analyzing evidence, including eyewitness accounts and video footage, but has yet to publicly disclose the attackers' identities. A source revealed that the accused actively facilitated the attack by sharing information on security deployments and helping the terrorists plan their approach and escape. Despite claiming ignorance of the tourists being the target, the accused admitted to assisting in the attack for money. The investigation is ongoing.

items.title: Evening news wrap: Shashi Tharoor’s cryptic post stirs political buzz; Shubhanshu Shukla makes space history, and more
items.story: Today's evening news wrap includes several significant updates across various domains. Shubhanshu Shukla has made history as the first Indian in space after 40 years. He will be at the International Space Station tomorrow. The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has approved a new policy to conduct Class 10 board exams twice a year starting 2026, allowing the best score to be retained. Politically, Shashi Tharoor has stirred a buzz with a cryptic post on social media after a comment by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, who hinted at Tharoor's favor towards Prime Minister Narendra Modi. In sports, Rishabh Pant has achieved his career-high ICC Test ranking, while Jasprit Bumrah maintains his position. In financial news, the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has increased the auto-settlement withdrawal limit to Rs 5 lakh.

items.title: Wipro to pay 2 lakh to ex-staffer for 'defamatory' relieving letter
items.story: The Delhi High Court has ordered Wipro to pay Rs 2 lakh to an ex-employee due to defamatory remarks made in a relieving letter. The court instructed Wipro to issue a new letter that removes these damaging statements. The original letter accused the employee of having a 'malicious' conduct that resulted in an 'irreparable breakdown in the employer-employee relationship'. The court emphasized that such remarks could negatively impact the employee's career prospects and professional dignity. Wipro is required to compensate the former employee for reputational damage, emotional distress, and loss of professional credibility caused by the defamatory content. Additionally, Wipro must issue a fresh termination letter, free of any defamatory content, although this does not change the fact of the employee's termination.

items.title: Stone-pelting at trains: Children, vagrants are usual suspects; jail term up to 5 years under Railways Act
items.story: Pelting stones at trains has become a troubling trend, causing risk to passengers and train delays. Officials note that this behavior is not only dangerous but also illegal, with legal repercussions for those involved. The trend is attributed to a general disregard for public safety and ignorance of the legal consequences. Some locals engage in stone-pelting for amusement, damaging trains and railway infrastructure in the process. Vulnerable areas include sections from Falaknuma to Budvel, Sitaphalmandi to Lallaguda, Hafeezpet to Lingampally, and near Mahabubnagar and Malkajgiri stations. Due to the rise in incidents, the Railway Protection Force (RPF) has appealed to the public to refrain from such anti-social activities and to report any such acts by calling 139. The railway security staff is conducting awareness campaigns in nearby schools and villages to educate children and locals about the seriousness of stone-pelting and its punishments. Regular drives are conducted against anti-social elements and drunkards in affected areas. Notices are served to local leaders where incidents frequently occur. Dedicated staff are deployed at black spots to monitor and prevent such acts. Offenders are prosecuted under relevant sections of the Railways Act, with penalties including imprisonment up to 5 years under Section 153, and up to 1 year or fines under Section 154.

items.title: On HYDRAA’s first anniversary, Hyderabad police vow to restore more city lakes
items.story:
HYDRAA celebrated its first anniversary with Commissioner AV Ranganath announcing plans to restore more lakes in Hyderabad. He highlighted the successful revival of Bathukamma Kunta, transforming it from an encroached and neglected water body into a thriving ecosystem. Collector Harichandana Dasari lauded the project's rapid completion in just four months. 

With HYDRAA completing one year on Saturday, commissioner AV Ranganath announced plans to restore more lakes across the city in the coming year. Speaking at an event held at Bathukamma Kunta in Amberpet on Friday, he said that the restored lake is an example of how encroached-upon and neglected bodies of water can be transformed into vibrant ecosystems. Ranganath recalled the challenges faced in reviving Bathukamma Kunta, including clearing encroachments and coordinating with multiple departments, such as the Revenue, the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC), the Irrigation, and Hyderabad Metropolitan Development Authority. He said that this effort had been successful and that the current environment around the lake speaks for itself. 

Hyderabad collector Harichandana Dasari also praised the project, calling the completion of the lake restoration in just four months a record-worthy achievement.

items.title: Shah: India's rising stature to invite new security challenges
items.story: Home Minister Amit Shah announced that the Modi government has shown strong political will and reinforced its zero-tolerance policy against terrorism through Operation Sindoor. Speaking at the National Security Strategies Conference, Shah urged security agencies to create a reliable system for real-time data sharing to tackle the increasing challenges faced by India as a rapidly emerging economy. Shah emphasized the need for a 'security-first' approach, habitual alertness, and coordination among all agencies. He noted that India's economy has risen to the fourth position globally, making it a leader in technologies, start-ups, and green energy. Shah warned that this rising stature would invite new national security challenges. He called for better coordination between central and state agencies and urged young officers to use national databases like Natgrid, Nidaan, iMoT, and the CBI's fugitive database in their training.

items.title: ‘Put it on hold’: Delhi government pushes back on fuel ban for older vehicles; writes to pollution control body
items.story: Delhi Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa has asked the Commission for Air Quality Management to suspend Direction No. 89, which bars fuel stations from providing fuel to End-of-Life vehicles in Delhi. He has argued that the order should be paused until the Automatic Number Plate Recognition system is fully implemented across the National Capital Region, as he believes it is unfair to vehicle owners. Sirsa also accused the Aam Aadmi Party of working against Delhi’s car owners and mentioned that new norms were introduced in 2024 to scrap vehicles. He claimed that the Delhi government is already making efforts to tackle air pollution, and this move is causing discontent among people. From July 1, the Delhi government banned fuel supply to end-of-life vehicles — diesel vehicles over 10 years old and petrol vehicles over 15 years old — that have been deregistered and are not permitted on roads as per court orders.

items.title: Need to involve urban & transport planner in highway projects passing through cities & towns: Experts
items.story: Experts at a conference held at IIT-Delhi emphasized the importance of involving urban and transport planners in highway projects that pass through urban areas. The Director of the School of Planning and Architecture, Virendra Kumar Paul, pointed out that highway engineers often lack the capability to evaluate detailed project reports (DPRs). During the conference titled "Crash Safety and Physical Planning," Paul mentioned that many highway engineers are either too bureaucratic or outsource the task of dealing with DPRs to external consultants. This lack of competence and interest can lead to higher rates of fatal crashes in urban areas due to the conflicting presence of different road users. SPA and IIT-Delhi have proposed to the ministry to undertake pilot projects for evaluating DPRs prepared for the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and other agencies. They also suggested setting up a Centre of Excellence for crash investigation. Minister of State for Road Transport and Highways, Ajay Tamta, called for a shift from reactive construction methods to proactive, innovation-led planning. He highlighted the need for innovations that not only improve safety but also address chronic issues such as land acquisition challenges, urban traffic congestion, poor last-mile connectivity, and cost overruns in road projects.

items.title: Eknath Chitnis passes away: Isro pioneer was 100; built India’s first telecom satellite
items.story: Isro scientist Dr Eknath Chitnis has passed away at the age of 100. He was a foundational figure at the Indian Space Research Organisation. Dr Chitnis worked with Dr Homi Bhabha in the early days. He was instrumental in developing India's first telecommunication satellite, INSAT. This satellite advanced the nation's space communication capabilities. NEW DELHI: Renowned Isro scientist Dr Eknath Chitnis passed away in Pune on Thursday at the age of 100. He was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1985. Dr Chitnis was one of the key figures behind the founding of the Indian Space Research Organisation, working closely with Dr Homi Bhabha in its early years. He played a crucial role in developing India’s first telecommunication satellite, INSAT, which laid the foundation for the country’s progress in space communication. Maharashtra deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar mourned his death, calling it the loss of a visionary in India’s scientific community. Pawar noted that Dr Chitnis’s initiatives in the 1970s made television accessible across the country, marking a new era of information.

items.title: No pollution data from Haryana as all state AQI stations offline since April
items.story:
Haryana's air quality monitoring network has been mostly offline since April due to a lapsed maintenance contract. This situation forces reliance on minimal data from just two India Meteorological Department stations, which may impede pollution control efforts during peak smog seasons. Without real-time data, it becomes difficult to issue alerts, enforce regulations, or provide public warnings, thereby compromising the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP). 

All 29 air quality monitoring stations operated by the Haryana State Pollution Control Board (HSPCB) have been offline since April 2, 2025. The state's data now relies on two stations from the India Meteorological Department, one in Gurgaon and the other in Panchkula. The issue arose from a lapsed maintenance contract, leaving no interim solution. By the end of last year, half of the stations had stopped recording data, which is crucial for pollution bulletins and strategy formulation. 

Efforts to restore the system faced delays. A tender issued in May 2025 received only one bid, which was automatically disqualified due to procurement rules. A second round of tenders is in preparation, with a late August deadline, followed by evaluations that could take 60 to 90 days. Thus, Haryana may enter the peak smog season without real-time AQI data, affecting the GRAP, which typically starts on October 15.

Officials admit there should have been a contingency plan. Experts emphasize the importance of timely decisions on new contracts to maintain critical infrastructure like air quality monitoring. 

The blackout could have serious consequences, particularly during the winter when pollution levels often reach "very poor" or "severe" categories. Without functional monitors, local authorities can't track AQI levels, identify pollution spikes, or decide when to implement pollution controls. This also affects the ability to track improvements under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP).

The limited data from Gurgaon and Panchkula covers only a small fraction of the state's urban and industrial areas. Different regions have varied pollution sources and weather patterns, making it difficult to extrapolate the data. A CREA analysis found that by January 19, 2025, Gurgaon's PM 2.5 levels were already so high that even a drastic reduction would not meet WHO limits, ranking it the fifth most polluted city in India for the first half of 2025.

items.title: ‘No extension without consensus’: Manipur groups tell Centre in Delhi talks
items.story:
Three civil society organizations from Manipur, including the Coordinating Committee on Manipur Integrity (COCOMI), held a round of dialogue with the Central government's representatives led by interlocutor A K Mishra in Delhi on Monday. They sought the preservation of the state's territorial integrity, steps to ensure the free movement of people, and phased resettlement of those displaced by ethnic violence by the end of the year. The Meitei-dominated groups, COCOMI, All Manipur United Clubs' Organisation (AMUCO), and Federation of Civil Society Organisations (FOCS), also advocated for the implementation of a national register of citizens (NRC) or a similar mechanism to address the issue of illegal migration effectively.

Concerns were raised over the home ministry's recent directive to detect illegal immigrants within a 30-day timeframe, emphasizing the need for proper mechanisms and safeguards. The 19-member delegation, including representatives of COCOMI, AMUCO, and FOCS, urged advisor (northeast) Mishra, assisted by IB and MHA officials, to formulate a phased and time-bound roadmap to address ethnic tensions in Manipur and find lasting solutions.

The Manipur groups clearly stated their opposition to any extension of suspension of operations (SOO) agreements without a comprehensive understanding among all stakeholders. They expressed concerns over the security and safety of farmers owning land in the peripheral areas of the Imphal Valley, which have experienced ethnic clashes in the past.

The delegation conveyed their willingness to participate in future meetings with all stakeholders, provided these initiatives serve the larger interest of restoring lasting peace and normalcy in Manipur. They also requested that future rounds of dialogue be held in Imphal.

Other issues raised included the release of the long-pending report on the Gwaltabi incident involving security forces covering Manipur's name on a bus and the construction of a 343 km-long illegal road along the Churachandpur-Kangpokpi axis. The MHA officials assured the delegation that the matters raised are being seriously considered and will be forwarded to the appropriate authorities for action.

items.title: Amarnath Yatra: Officials conduct mock drill at Yatri Niwas base camp; yatra set to begin on July 3
items.story: Security forces in Jammu and Kashmir are gearing up for the Amarnath Yatra by conducting a series of mock drills to ensure the safety and preparedness for the pilgrimage. On Monday, a comprehensive joint mock drill was performed at Yatri Niwas, the base camp for the Amarnath Yatra, as a preemptive measure to guarantee safety during the upcoming event. This involved testing the transportation of buses under full security cover to assess readiness. The first batch of pilgrims is scheduled to depart from the Jammu base camp on July 2, with the Yatra officially commencing on July 3 via the Baltal and Pahalgam routes. Deputy Commissioner of Jammu, Sachin Kumar Vaishy, assured that all preparations were complete and encouraged people to participate in large numbers, promising all necessary facilities and a smooth experience. The drills aimed to evaluate emergency responses to potential disasters like landslides during the pilgrimage, ensuring prompt and effective action in case of any incidents. This included rescuing stranded vehicles and providing immediate aid to injured pilgrims. The security and disaster response teams coordinated efficiently to ensure evacuation and medical assistance were promptly delivered. On Sunday, the Indian Army, CRPF, J&K Police, and the Jammu and Kashmir State Disaster Response Force conducted a mock landslide drill in Samroli and Toldi Nallah along the Jammu-Srinagar National Highway, a critical route for the Yatra. The CRPF has intensified surveillance by deploying K-9 squads and enhancing highway patrols, focusing on sensitive areas such as the Udhampur sector. Additionally, the Director General of Police in J&K, Nalin Prabhat, held a security review meeting in Udhampur to enhance coordination among agencies responsible for ensuring the safety of pilgrims. He emphasized the need for close coordination and real-time deployment of special teams like Drone Units, Bomb Disposal Squads, and Quick Response Teams to ensure an incident-free Yatra.

items.title: 'Morale of criminals sky-high': After meeting JP Nadda, Chirag Paswan slams ally Nitish Kumar; third time a month
items.story:
Chirag Paswan, Union minister and chief of the Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas), has criticized the deteriorating law and order situation in Bihar, highlighting a recent shooting at Paras Hospital as evidence of criminals openly challenging the administration. He expressed serious concerns about the rising crime rate, especially in the context of upcoming elections, and urged the government to take immediate action. Paswan mentioned that the morale of criminals is extremely high and that the daily occurrence of murders is incomprehensible, as is the functioning of the police and administration.

In a social media post, Paswan commented on the incident where criminals fired shots inside Paras Hospital, located in a residential area of Patna, stating that this is a direct challenge to law enforcement. He emphasized the urgency of the situation, particularly with the approaching Bihar Legislative Election, and expressed hope that the administration would soon implement strong measures to restore law and order.

This marks the third time Paswan has voiced concerns about Bihar's law and order situation, with his latest remarks following a meeting with BJP president J P Nadda. Earlier, on July 12, Paswan criticized the state's law enforcement as being beyond understanding. His ongoing criticism comes ahead of the Bihar elections, where he has declared his intention to contest.

Paswan's recent comments also referenced the killing of Sushila Devi, a 60-year-old hospital worker in Nalanda, raising questions about the responsibility of the Bihar Police.

items.title: ‘Sitaare Zameen Par’ box office collection day 5: Aamir Khan and Genelia D’Souza starrer maintains a steady pace on Tuesday, collects Rs 75.15 crores net in India
items.story: Aamir Khan and Genelia D’Souza's film 'Sitaare Zameen Par' has successfully captured audience attention, amassing over Rs. 70 crore within just five days of its release. Despite witnessing a dip in collections on Monday, the film maintained its momentum on Tuesday, with total collections reaching Rs. 75.15 crore. Directed by R.S. Prasanna, this movie is considered a spiritual sequel to 'Taare Zameen Par.' The plot centers on Aamir Khan's character, Gulshan Arora, a basketball coach who faces suspension for hitting the head coach and is troubled by potential jail time due to a drunk driving incident. As part of his community service, he is assigned to coach a team of athletes with intellectual disabilities for a national basketball tournament. The journey is fraught with challenges but ultimately leads to personal growth and valuable life lessons. The film balances sentiment with humor and avoids being overly preachy, making it an engaging watch. The film's box office performance is detailed as follows: Day 1 (Friday) - ₹ 10.7 Cr, Day 2 (Saturday) - ₹ 20.2 Cr, Day 3 (Sunday) - ₹ 27.25 Cr, Day 4 (Monday) - ₹ 8.5 Cr, Day 5 (Tuesday) - ₹ 8.5 Cr, totaling ₹ 75.15 Cr. With a promising start, the film is steadily moving towards the Rs. 100 crore mark.
items.relevanceReason: This film’s box office success lacks direct political, ideological, or constituency-level linkage with Dr. Shashidhar’s Hindutva or security-focused agenda. While Aamir Khan’s involvement might occasionally spark cultural debates, there is no compelling angle here to further Dr. Shashidhar’s core messaging or to attack opponents. Minimal strategic benefit in responding publicly.

items.title: Covid-19 Tablighi Jamaat congregation case: HC quashes charges against nationals for sheltering foreigners; 16 cases junked
items.story: The Delhi High Court has quashed 16 chargesheets that were registered against several citizens accused of sheltering foreign attendees of the Tablighi Jamaat congregation during the Covid-19 pandemic. The chargesheets were dismissed, as quoted by Live Law from the judge's statement. In January 2022, the Delhi Police opposed petitions seeking the quashing of these charges, arguing that the Indian nationals not only defied prohibitory orders imposed by the Delhi government but also contributed to the spread of Covid-19. The Delhi Police's status report in response to the accused's petitions stated that members of the Jamaat, who were staying at the Nizamuddin Markaz from March 26 to March 31, 2020, were later found in the Chandni Mahal area of Central Delhi on April 1, 2020. The investigating agency further alleged that the accused knowingly admitted and hosted the Jamaat assembly on their premises despite prohibitory orders on movement issued by the authorities.

items.title: Don't worry, we can mix languages: PM Modi eases translator's English slip, then uses same language to deliver fierce message Khalistani extremism
items.story:
During a joint press conference, Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed a minor translation error with humor and grace. When the translator hesitated after unintentionally mixing Hindi and English, PM Modi reassured her by saying, "Don't worry. We can use English words in between. Don't worry about it," which brought laughter from the audience. This light-hearted moment set a relaxed tone in the formal setting. 

Later on, Modi himself switched to English while speaking about global terrorism to emphasize his strong message to Khalistani groups and Western nations. He stated, "Those who misuse democratic freedoms to undermine democracy itself must be held to account." 

Modi has previously used English strategically to ensure his messages on terrorism reach a global audience. Following a deadly terror attack in Pahalgam, he emphasized that India would "identify, track, and punish every terrorist and their backers" during a rally in Bihar. A few days later, India conducted Operation Sindoor against terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir, avenging the attack.

items.title: IND vs ENG: Sanjay Manjrekar warns KL Rahul ahead of 2nd Test - 'Can't be a one-hundred wonder'
items.story:
Former India cricketer Sanjay Manjrekar has urged KL Rahul to demonstrate more consistency in Test cricket, especially as he steps into a senior role following the retirements of Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma. Manjrekar expressed confidence in Rishabh Pant, who has strengthened his position in India's batting lineup by becoming only the second wicketkeeper in history to score twin centuries in a Test match, following Andy Flower. As one of the most experienced players in India's relatively young batting order, Rahul is now expected to provide stability and leadership while delivering consistent performances with the bat. 

Pant's achievement of scoring two centuries in the Leeds Test particularly impressed Manjrekar, who praised Pant's dedication to Test cricket. According to Manjrekar, any batter who scores two hundreds in a Test match demonstrates exceptional ability and mental strength. 

Manjrekar emphasized that KL Rahul must avoid being known for stop-start performances and should maintain consistency throughout the series. He stressed that Indian cricket needs Rahul to be more than a one-hundred wonder or a one-Test-match performer. 

The spotlight is now on Rahul, with increased expectations as he assumes the role of the senior-most batter in India's Test lineup. Pant's recent performance has set a high standard, demonstrating the ability to deliver consistently in Test cricket. As the team undergoes transition, more experienced players like Rahul are expected to guide the younger players through this phase.

items.title: Parliament security breach: HC grants bail to 2 accused; bars them from giving interviews, posting on social media about case
items.story: The Delhi High Court has granted bail to Neelam Azad and Mahesh Kumawat, who were among those charged in connection with a security breach incident at the Parliament. The incident took place on December 13, 2023, coinciding with the anniversary of the 2001 Parliament attack. During the breach, individuals, including Amol Shinde and Neelam Azad, sprayed colored gas outside the Parliament while shouting slogans. The high court set bail at Rs 50,000 each, with two sureties of equal value, and imposed conditions prohibiting the accused from speaking to the media or posting about the case on social media. The bail was granted after an appeal against a lower court's decision to deny bail. The case is ongoing, with other accused, including Lalit Jha and Mahesh Kumawat, also in police custody for interrogation.

items.title: Olympic skier Audun Groenvold tragically dies at 49 after lightning strike during cabin trip
items.story: Norwegian Olympic ski cross medalist Audun Groenvold tragically passed away at 49 after being struck by lightning while traveling to a cabin. Despite immediate transport to the hospital, his injuries were fatal. Groenvold, known for his 2010 Vancouver Winter Olympics bronze medal, had a successful career in both alpine and freestyle skiing, leaving a significant void in Norway's skiing community. The ski community is in great shock and mourning as a result of his passing. After being hit by lightning during a cabin vacation, Norwegian Olympic skier Audun Groenvold died on Tuesday evening, July 16, 2025. On Wednesday, July 17, the Norwegian Ski Federation validated the bad news. Shortly after the strike, they claimed he did not live with the injuries and was brought to the hospital. Most people know Groenvold for her ski cross bronze medal finish at the 2010 Vancouver Winter Olympics. His skiing career was long and very successful. Beginning in alpine skiing, he came third in the downhill race in Sierra Nevada, Spain, and received a World Cup podium in 1999. Claiming yet another bronze at the 2005 World Championships, later he changed to freestyle and ski cross and finished first overall in the Ski Cross World Cup in 2007. The Ski Federation described Groenvold's passing as a huge loss to both Alpine and freestyle skiing. Federation president Tove Moe Dyrhaug said he was not just a great athlete but someone who deeply shaped Norway’s skiing culture. Audun Groenvold stayed close to the sport even after quitting professional skiing. He became a television pundit and national team coach by publicising his knowledge and passion for winter sports. For many young Norwegian skiers, he was a teacher and inspiration. His surprise demise left a hole in the Norwegian sports scene. People will remember his physical capacity in addition to his passion for the game and personality. Many Norwegians thought he was a hero for his accomplishments, which include his Olympic ski cross bronze medal in 2010. The death of Audun Groenvold has startled fans and athletes all around. Among Norway's most talented and respected Olympic athletes, he will be remembered in the skiing scene.

items.title: "Saiyaara" box office collection day 7 (LIVE): Mohit Suri, Ahaan Panday and Aneet Padda’s film takes a slow start on Thursday
items.story:
Mohit Suri's romantic drama 'Saiyaara' has turned into a blockbuster, gathering an impressive Rs 155.24 crore net in India within its first week. The film, which features fresh talent and soulful music, exceeded expectations with remarkable daily collections and sustained its performance even on weekdays. 'Saiyaara's' success is especially significant because it was achieved without established superstars.

The film opened with a strong Rs 21.5 crore on Friday, marking one of the highest debuts ever for a film led by newcomers. Positive audience feedback helped 'Saiyaara' witness a significant surge on Saturday with Rs 26 crore, followed by a spectacular Sunday with Rs 35.75 crore — its biggest single-day figure. Unlike many films that see a steep drop on Monday, 'Saiyaara' maintained its momentum, earning more than its first day with Rs 24 crore. Its Tuesday collection saw a slight increase at Rs 25 crore, thanks to steady attendance in urban centers and a strong connection with the youth. By midweek, the momentum slowed slightly but remained healthy, with Wednesday bringing in Rs 21 crore.

In its first six days, the film earned more than Rs 20 crore each day — a rare feat for post-pandemic films. By noon on its seventh day — Thursday — 'Saiyaara' had already earned Rs 1.99 crore, suggesting a potential final day figure of around Rs 10-12 crore, making it the lowest day for the film that week. However, with the weekend approaching, significant growth is expected, potentially pushing the film past the Rs 200 crore mark.

What makes 'Saiyaara's' performance even more noteworthy is that it achieved this without the appeal of an established superstar. The lead pair, Ahaan Panday and Aneet Padda, have resonated with younger audiences, while Mohit Suri's signature mix of intense romance and chartbuster music has worked wonders at the box office.

With a total of Rs 155.24 crore in just seven days, 'Saiyaara' now stands among the biggest first-week grossers for a film led by debutants. It has surpassed industry benchmarks set by films like 'Student of the Year' and 'Heropanti' in their opening weeks, and the future looks promising.

items.title: IND vs ENG: 'I actually thought of three celebrations' - Rishabh Pant reveals as signature somersault goes viral
items.story: Rishabh Pant lit up Day 2 of the Headingley Test not just with his bat but also with a touch of theatrical flair, celebrating his seventh Test century with a gravity-defying somersault that sent social media into a meltdown. But as it turns out, the flamboyant wicketkeeper-batter had options. Speaking to Cheteshwar Pujara on the broadcaster’s post-match show, Pant revealed that he had actually planned three possible celebrations for the occasion. "I had actually thought of three celebrations. One was the 'let-the-bat-do-the-talking' one. Then I realised I should stick to my own style of celebration," he said with a grin. Pant brought up his hundred in typical fashion - by launching Shoaib Bashir for a six over deep midwicket, one hand off the bat, full intent in swing. Then followed the now-viral somersault, a move reminiscent of his celebratory leap in the IPL earlier this year. His hundred - his fourth against England - came off 146 balls and included 10 boundaries and 4 sixes. Teaming up with captain Shubman Gill (147), Pant stitched a 209-run partnership that powered India past the 400-run mark. Having endured a long injury layoff, Pant’s return has been nothing short of spectacular. From hospital bed to Headingley flips, his comeback arc is now etched with yet another viral twist.

items.title: 'Udaipur Files': Delhi HC stays release of film; urges petitioners seeking ban to approach Centre
items.story: The Delhi High Court has put a hold on the release of the film 'Udaipur Files: Kanhaiya Lal Tailor Murder,' which was scheduled for release on July 11. This decision was made as Jamiat Ulema-i-Hind seeks a review of the film's certification, arguing that it could stir communal discord. The stay will remain in effect until the Central Government addresses the revision application. The petitioners, who are also accused in the 2022 murder of Udaipur-based tailor Kanhaiya Lal, argued that the film’s release would endanger their right to a fair trial and incite communal disharmony, challenging the CBFC’s certification.

items.title: Gold price prediction: What's the gold rate outlook for July 7, 2025 week - should you buy or sell?
items.story: Gold prices are expected to remain volatile due to uncertainties surrounding US President Donald Trump's tariff policies, the upcoming July 9 deadline, and the potential imposition of additional tariffs on BRICS countries perceived to be aligned with 'anti-American policies.' Manav Modi, a senior analyst at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd, shared insights on the outlook for gold prices. Over the last week, gold prices experienced notable fluctuations, ultimately settling at a six-week low as global tensions eased and investor sentiment shifted. The softening of US-China trade hostilities, including agreements on rare earth shipments, reduced the demand for gold as a safe haven. Meanwhile, a tentative ceasefire between Iran and Israel and Trump's decision to postpone tariffs on multiple countries contributed to a decrease in geopolitical risk premiums. Despite a weakened US dollar, gold prices were pressured by stronger-than-expected US nonfarm payroll data and mixed labor market signals, leading to doubts about potential Federal Reserve rate cuts in the near term. President Trump advocated for lower rates, even sending annotated global rate comparisons to Federal Reserve Chair Powell, who remained cautious with a 'wait and see' approach.
