Political developments further complicated the situation: Senate Republicans passed Trump's tax-and-spending bill, and trade negotiations picked up pace over the weekend. The US is close to finalizing several trade agreements, with higher tariff rates scheduled to take effect on August 1. Trump's decision on tariffs targeting BRICS nations will be crucial to monitor. Additionally, the first round of indirect ceasefire talks between Hamas and Israel in Qatar ended without a conclusive agreement, as the Israeli delegation lacked sufficient mandate to negotiate with Hamas. The USD-INR exchange rate hovered just below 86, influencing domestic gold prices. With FOMC minutes and tariff deadlines approaching, market attention remains focused on Federal Reserve policy cues and global trade dynamics. Gold is expected to trade sideways to lower, with a price range of Rs 96,000 – 98,000, and a break below the lower range could lead to prices falling to Rs 94,000.

items.title: UoH student bags record Rs 46L package amid tough job market
items.story: A student from the University of Hyderabad (UoH) has achieved a record-breaking salary package of Rs 46 lakh per annum during campus placements for the academic year 2024-25. This is the highest package ever secured by a student from the university. The MTech student from the School of Computer and Information Sciences secured the job at a leading product-based company. This year's top offer is more than double the previous year's highest package of Rs 17.89 lakh per annum. Another MTech student from the same school received the second-highest offer of Rs 38 lakh. Despite a challenging job market, the students have performed exceptionally well, showcasing the growing recognition of UoH talent, said Professor Chetan Srivastava, chairman of the placement guidance advisory bureau. He also noted that the previous record was around Rs 37 lakh per annum. In total, 550 students were placed across 180 organizations this season, with roles in IT, analytics, finance, research, education, and consulting. Top recruiters included Tata Consultancy Services, Deloitte, Oracle, Teradata, Intel, and Lloyds. Prerna Akhouri, training and placement coordinator, highlighted shifts in hiring practices, noting that despite delays in some in-person recruitment processes, excellent outcomes were achieved. She mentioned that upskilling programs and more placement drives are planned for the coming months to assist more students.

items.title: Bihar polls: No SIRround sound; Election Commission silent on number of 'aliens' deleted
items.story:
NEW DELHI: Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, when asked on Monday to share the number of illegal foreign immigrants deleted from the Bihar electoral rolls on account of the special intensive revision (SIR), did not elaborate on the figure, saying that the relevant data field was not available with EC. 'The 7.4 crore electors of Bihar have reposed confidence in EC with their full participation in the SIR exercise and EC reciprocates confidence in them... I appeal to the people of Bihar to participate enthusiastically in the ensuing polls,' Kumar said while announcing the Bihar poll schedule.

The CEC said the data on illegal foreigners removed from the rolls for failure to provide proof of citizenship would be available at the assembly constituency level with electoral registration officers (EROs) or assistant EROs concerned, given the 'decentralised' nature of preparation of rolls. The ERO, he explained, is the final authority on inclusion or exclusion of names. Kumar, however, said the names deleted from the Bihar rolls - 65 lakh at the draft roll publication stage, and 3.7 lakh more at the final roll publication stage - were found 'ineligible' on account of reasons like death, having permanently shifted, remaining untraced during enumeration, for being non-citizens, or having been enrolled at multiple places.

'All these lists have been shared, at the level of the assembly constituency, the district level, and state level, and have been shared with the statistics,' the CEC said. 'That is why, all these different lists that you are talking about are not at the level of EC, but at the level of the ERO, district election officer (DEO) and chief electoral officer (CEO),' he added.

EC had given a break-up of the electors covered in different categories at the time of publication of draft roll, but did not have any separate category for those deleted on account of being non-citizens. Of the 65 lakh deletions, 22 lakh were on account of being deceased, 7 lakh due to being enrolled at multiple places, and 36 lakh on account of having permanently shifted or not being found. Though the last category of 36 lakh voters is inclusive of foreign illegal immigrants, possibly covered under the category 'not found' or 'untraced', their exact number was not disclosed.

In earlier press notes, EC had put the number of 'untraced/not found' voters at 1 lakh, when the overall figure of dead, permanently shifted, enrolled at multiple places and untraced/not found was around 60 lakh. A further 3.7 lakh voters were removed at the time of final publication of roll, but no breakup has been provided yet on why they were deleted.

items.title: NBA Trade News: Los Angeles Lakers Add Villanova’s 6-foot-8 All-Time Scorer to Support Luka-LeBron Power Duo and Improve Title Odds
items.story:
The Los Angeles Lakers have officially signed Eric Dixon, a 6-foot-8 forward and Villanova's all-time leading scorer, along with three other players: RJ Davis, Arthur Kaluma, and Augustas Marciulionis. These signings aim to build a strong roster around star players LeBron James and Luka Doncic ahead of the 2025-26 NBA season. Dixon's addition was delayed due to a foot injury, but he is known for his impressive scoring ability and may start in the NBA G-League. 

The Lakers confirmed the signings via a press release, highlighting Dixon's standout college scoring career at Villanova University. Despite not being drafted in the 2025 NBA Draft, Dixon agreed to terms with the Lakers in late June, although his status was uncertain due to his injury.

Eric Dixon's senior season statistics emphasize his scoring prowess, including 23.3 points per game, a field goal percentage of 45.1%, and a three-point percentage of 40.7%. Over his college career, he became Villanova's highest scorer with 2,314 points. Although he was undrafted, Dixon's versatility and scoring ability are expected to benefit the Lakers as they focus on development and depth.

items.title: ‘He didn’t speak to me for three months’: Sourav Ganguly reveals fallout with VVS Laxman, shares details
items.story:
Former India captain Sourav Ganguly has shared a personal experience from his cricketing career, revealing that VVS Laxman did not speak to him for three months following his exclusion from India's squad for the 2003 ODI World Cup. At that time, Ganguly, who was leading the team, confessed that the choice to leave out Laxman in favor of all-rounder Dinesh Mongia caused a significant rift between them. Ganguly explained that Laxman's exclusion was due to strategic reasons, despite his impressive ODI record. This decision led to controversy, as former selection committee chief Kiran More later revealed that all five selectors supported Laxman's inclusion, but Ganguly and then-head coach John Wright had differing opinions.

Despite having 2,338 runs from 86 ODIs, Laxman never played in a World Cup match for India. However, Ganguly emphasized that Laxman's return to the team after the World Cup showcased his value. He stated that Laxman was outstanding in subsequent series, particularly in Pakistan and Australia, and reiterated that the decision was not personal.

India eventually reached the finals of the 2003 World Cup but lost to Australia. Ganguly noted that although Laxman was initially hurt by the exclusion, he understood that the decision was not personal, and they reconciled after the World Cup.

items.title: 'Bhayankar chori': Rahul Gandhi promises big exposé on poll 'theft'; 'probes Lok Sabha seat in Karnataka'
items.story: Rahul Gandhi has made allegations of significant electoral fraud, which he described as a "massive theft," after investigating a Lok Sabha seat in Karnataka. He has promised to present a detailed exposé with evidence to the Election Commission, claiming that similar electoral malpractices have occurred in Maharashtra and Bihar. Gandhi accuses the Election Commission of withholding voter lists and manipulating regulations. He claims that the INDIA bloc will combat voter disenfranchisement through both protests and parliamentary action. His investigation revealed that the electoral roll in Bihar's Special Intensive Revision found over 52 lakh voters missing from their registered addresses and another 18 lakh had died. Gandhi alleges that in Maharashtra, one crore new voters were added, leading to an election being "stolen." The opposition has been staging protests in Parliament, accusing the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision exercise of being a deliberate attempt to disenfranchise voters in Bihar ahead of assembly elections.

items.title: TCS to axe 12,000 jobs; IT giant’s biggest layoff ever
items.story: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), India's largest IT company, has announced plans to lay off 12,261 employees, roughly 2% of its workforce, due to disruptions caused by artificial intelligence (AI) and uncertainties in business demand. This marks TCS's largest layoff to date. The job cuts will primarily affect mid-level and senior executives. The layoffs are part of TCS's efforts to transform into a future-ready organization by embracing AI and automation. These changes reflect a strategic shift in the company's approach and highlight the impact of AI on the service model that traditionally relied on a large workforce. This restructuring is seen as a response to the challenging demand environment, with clients increasingly demanding price reductions of 20-30% in deals. TCS's CEO, K Krithivasan, acknowledged the impact on employees and expressed gratitude for their service, committing to support them through the transition. Other Tata Group companies, such as Tata Steel and Tata Motors, have also periodically reduced their workforce to cut costs and increase profitability.

items.title: India growing by leaps and bounds in space sector: PM Modi
items.story:
Ahead of the National Space Day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted India's growing capabilities in the space sector. He cited Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla's recent journey to the International Space Station (ISS) and the emergence of more than 200 startups in the sector. Discussing Shukla, who was one of the four crew members of the Axiom-4 mission to the ISS, Modi, in his 124th 'Mann Ki Baat' episode, said that when the astronaut returned to Earth, the entire nation felt a 'wave of happiness' and pride. 

He also mentioned that the success of ISRO's Chandrayaan-3 mission created an atmosphere of curiosity in the country about space endeavors. Modi recalled that when Chandrayaan-3 successfully landed in August 2023, it sparked a new curiosity among children about science and space. He noted that children now say they want to go to space and become space scientists. 

The Prime Minister particularly mentioned the 'INSPIRE-MANAK Abhiyan', which promotes innovation among children by providing them a platform to develop innovative ideas based in science. Under this initiative, five children are selected from each school to present new ideas. Since the Chandrayaan-3 mission, participation has doubled.

Regarding India's space startups, Modi pointed out their number has quadrupled in the last five years, growing from fewer than 50 to more than 200. As for the upcoming National Space Day on August 23, he asked for suggestions on how to celebrate it and encouraged people to send ideas on the NaMo App. Modi also acknowledged recent achievements of students in science and mathematics, applauding the country's brightest minds.

items.title: Boost to Government Medical Education
items.story: The central government recently announced that 75,000 new medical education seats will be made available across the country in the next five years. In this process, the National Medical Commission (NMC) has eased several regulations to further promote medical education. It has relaxed the qualifications for teachers in medical colleges. The Postgraduate Medical Education Board (PGMEB), which operates under the NMC, announced the relaxed regulations on Saturday. Government non-teaching hospitals with 220 beds can now be converted into teaching hospitals. Doctors with ten years of experience can be appointed as associate professors, and those with two years of experience can be appointed as assistant professors. In the state, those with a year of experience are already being appointed as assistant professors, but they are required to work as senior residents. The new regulations have relaxed this requirement, allowing them to be appointed as assistant professors even without being senior residents. Until now, the rule was that a medical college must complete one MBBS batch before starting PG courses. From now on, UG and PG courses can be started simultaneously. This provides an opportunity to start PG courses in all newly established medical colleges by the state government, significantly increasing the number of PG seats. The age limit for senior residents has been increased from 40 to 50.

items.title: 'Why would I': Hunter Biden denies bringing cocaine to White House, says he didn't touch a drop of alcohol or drug since 2019
items.story:
Hunter Biden denied any involvement with the cocaine found at the White House in 2023 during an interview on Monday. He stated he has been sober since 2019. The FBI recently reopened the case, and former President Donald Trump also insinuated, without any evidence, that the cocaine pouch might have belonged to either Joe Biden or Hunter.

Joe Biden's son, Hunter, in an interview, denied that a bag of cocaine found in the White House in 2023 belonged to him after the FBI reopened the case. "I have not touched a drop of alcohol or a drug, and I'm incredibly proud of that," he said during the interview with Channel 5, a popular YouTube channel created by YouTuber Andrew Callaghan. "Why would I bring cocaine into the White House and stick it into a cubby outside of the situation room in the West Wing?"

On July 2, 2023, the United States Secret Service found a small plastic bag containing less than a gram of powder cocaine inside the White House, leading to an immediate evacuation. Joe Biden and his family were at Camp David in Maryland when the cocaine was discovered. The Secret Service's investigation remained inconclusive as it did not yield any forensic evidence. The case was closed within 11 days.

FBI Deputy Director Dan Bongino recently announced the reopening of the case, as Trump earlier speculated that the cocaine could be from either Joe or Hunter.

Hunter spoke about his addiction in his memoir "Beautiful Things," but he said in the interview that he has not touched drugs or alcohol for years, being sober since 2019. In 2024, he was found guilty of felony charges related to the purchase of a handgun. Joe Biden gave him a presidential pardon before leaving office for any crime he "committed or may have committed" from January 1, 2014, to December 1, 2024.

Biden took a jab at Donald Trump Jr. and Georgia Representative Marjorie Taylor Greene for frequently attacking his past. "So, I think for those that wanted to use it as a bludgeon, it was just easier when you slap the word 'crack addict' onto it," he said. "It made me a lot easier target for the Don Juniors of the world, the Marjorie Taylor Greenes of the world, just because of their inherent, kind of, meanness about things."

items.title: Thin ecosystem & low visibility keep Telangana startups away from big funding
items.story: Hyderabad: Telangana, despite being known as a tech hub, has seen only 37 startups secure funding through the Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS) scheme under the Startup India initiative. These startups received a total of Rs 600 crore through Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), a figure significantly lower compared to top-performing states. Karnataka leads with 396 startups backed and Rs 7,348 crore in funding, followed by Maharashtra with Rs 5,606 crore and Delhi with Rs 3,689 crore. In all, 1,282 startups across India have received Rs 23,679 crore in funding through AIFs, according to data presented in the Lok Sabha. Ramesh Loganathan, COO of the Centre for Innovation & Entrepreneurship (CIE), one of the largest academic incubators in the country, stated that the funding process lacks transparency and favors cities like Bengaluru and Noida. He mentioned the difficulty in obtaining investments through the Fund of Funds scheme due to limited transparency and a clear bias towards certain cities, contributing to a lack of a robust startup ecosystem in Telangana. While Telangana has a fair number of startups, many do not meet quality benchmarks, leading top-tier startups to relocate to cities like Bengaluru in search of better environments and visibility. AIFs are pooled investment vehicles that invest in unlisted companies, including startups, in phases following thorough evaluations. Startup founders in Hyderabad echoed these concerns. Saketha Pingali, founder of Smart Pharma, criticized the lengthy and uncertain process of applying for Startup India schemes, pointing out the lack of visibility and investor presence in Telangana as a significant challenge. The data underscores the urgent need to strengthen Telangana's startup ecosystem to compete with the country's leading innovation hubs.

items.title: ‘Aggressive US pressure can force…’: GTRI warns India against one-sided trade deal; says don’t fall into same trap’ as Indonesia
items.story: The Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) warns India against following the US-Indonesia trade deal model, which is heavily favorable to the US. The deal allows significant access to Indonesia's markets while imposing tariffs on Indonesian goods. GTRI advises India to be cautious in trade negotiations with the US, particularly concerning agriculture, digital trade, and product standards. The US-Indonesia trade agreement is seen as an example of how aggressive US pressure can lead to unbalanced trade commitments. The agreement stipulates that Indonesia will remove 99% of its tariffs on American exports, providing almost complete access for US industrial, technological, and agricultural products. In return, the US will implement a 19% tariff on Indonesian goods, lowered from an initially proposed 40%. Indonesian exports will still face US MFN tariffs. Indonesia has committed to purchasing American goods valued at $22.7 billion, including energy products, agricultural commodities, and Boeing aircraft. The deal forces Indonesia to give up domestic regulations that have long protected its industries, food safety, and digital space. US companies can operate without sourcing from local suppliers, impacting Indonesian MSMEs. Indonesia must adopt American vehicle safety and emissions standards, allowing direct export from US manufacturers, while Indonesian manufacturers must meet US regulations for exporting. The elimination of restrictions on remanufactured goods opens Indonesia to low-cost, second-hand machinery from the US, affecting local firms. The GTRI emphasizes that these agreements should serve as caution for India in its trade talks with the US, which currently faces similar demands. India needs to ensure trade agreements are transparent, fair, and aligned with its development needs. Concessions should be reciprocal and maintain control over critical areas like food, health, digital, and IP.

items.title: Maharashtra: Uddhav Sena's men trace & assault autowala over Marathi
items.story: After a video went viral showing an autorickshaw driver refusing to speak Marathi, a group of men, allegedly from Shiv Sena (UBT), assaulted him. The driver, Raju Patwa, was traced and forced to apologize for his defiance. The incident occurred after a video of Raju Patwa, who operates from Virar (east) autorickshaw stand, stating his refusal to speak Marathi went viral. He had said he would only speak Bhojpuri and Hindi. The video gained attention on the day the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena was holding a rally in Mira Road. Following the video's circulation, a group allegedly led by Shiv Sena (UBT) member Uday Jadhav tracked down Patwa and coerced him into apologizing to a passenger he had refused to speak Marathi with. The passenger, Bhavesh, had asked Patwa to be careful after the rickshaw brushed past him, to which Patwa responded in Hindi, refusing to speak Marathi. A video of the assault shows Patwa apologizing while being physically attacked. Police have filed a case of rioting against eight or nine individuals involved in the assault.

items.title: Op Sindoor debate: Nadda vs Kharge sparks RS uproar; BJP chief withdraws remark, apologises
items.story: The Rajya Sabha experienced a tumultuous session during the debate on Operation Sindoor and the Pahalgam terror attack. JP Nadda, the leader of the House, engaged in a heated exchange with the leader of the opposition, Mallikarjun Kharge. Tensions escalated following Kharge's lengthy and intense speech which was critical of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. In response, Nadda accused Kharge of having "lost his mental balance," a comment that provoked significant backlash from opposition members. This remark was immediately condemned by Kharge, who demanded a retraction, calling it a "matter of shame." Kharge stated, "JP Nadda and Rajnath Singh are among the few Ministers in the House for whom I have immense respect as they say things without losing their 'balance'. But I'll not spare them if he doesn't apologise." Despite initial resistance, Nadda retracted his statement and apologized, saying, "I have already taken back my words, but if they have hurt his (Kharge's) feelings, I apologize for the same. However, Kharge did cross his limits and made certain remarks against the prime minister in passion and out of emotion, which need to be expunged." Nadda further added that "Prime Minister Narendra Modi is the most popular leader in the world and not just the BJP takes pride in it, the entire nation does," emphasizing that Kharge's choice of words did not reflect his stature. He urged the chair to expunge Kharge's remarks that were deemed objectionable.

items.title: Centre eyes revival of Tulbul project: How India plans to maximize Indus water? Here's why it matters
items.story:
The Indian government is considering reviving the Tulbul Navigation Project to better utilize its share of water from the western rivers as outlined in the Indus Waters Treaty. This initiative aims to address India's limited water storage capacity and optimize dam management. The central government is looking to restart this long-delayed project as part of a strategy to maximize India's utilization of water from the western rivers under the treaty, according to senior official sources. A comprehensive project report is in the works and is expected to take about a year to finalize.

The government's move comes amidst Prime Minister Narendra Modi's repeated commitments to use Indus waters for India. The plan involves utilizing Indus river water for domestic purposes in four states: Rajasthan, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, and Delhi. India faces challenges in water-storage capacity, particularly during the monsoon season, impacting its ability to fully utilize its share of water from the western rivers allocated under the treaty.

During the rainy season, storage capacity is limited, and excess water flows downstream to Pakistan. The government aims for better dam and reservoir management to address this. PM Modi has criticized the treaty for restrictions preventing India from desilting dams in Jammu and Kashmir, which has led to reservoirs using only a small fraction of their capacity.

Reports of the Tulbul project's revival come after Union Home Minister Amit Shah dismissed any chances of restoring the Indus Waters Treaty. The treaty with Pakistan was put 'under abeyance' after a terror attack. Officials are exploring proposals to enhance India's utilization of its entitled share from the rivers, including potential water diversion to Punjab and Haryana. The Kishanganga hydropower project, previously challenged by Pakistan, has been completed, while the construction of the Ratle project is being fast-tracked.

items.title: Uttarakhand: 22-year-old merchant navy’s senior deck cadet goes missing at sea
items.story:
DEHRADUN: A 22-year-old senior deck cadet, Karandeep Singh Rana, from Uttarakhand has gone missing from aboard a merchant navy vessel on its way to China from Iraq, said his family on Friday.

According to his father, Narendra Rana, the last contact with Karandeep came on Sept 20 morning. "Later that day, we received a call from the shipping company, Executive Ship Management Pvt Ltd, informing us that he went missing," said the father.

"The ship first went to Iraq and was later headed to China via Sri Lanka and Singapore. Karandeep reportedly disappeared somewhere on the Sri Lanka–Singapore route. He might be on the vessel, but we don't have complete information," said Narendra Rana to TOI.

The father said he has written to Uttarakhand chief minister, and also lodged a request on the Prime Minister's portal, seeking urgent intervention to trace his son.

Meanwhile, the shipping company has confirmed the development and said a 96-hour search operation was conducted, and a "full investigation" would be carried out once the vessel arrives in China in the next few days.

Executive Ship Management Pvt Ltd maintained: "It is with profound sadness that we announce the tragic loss of cadet Karandeep Singh Rana. It is suspected that he was lost overboard on Sept 20 evening while on the vessel Front Princess. The ship's crew searched for Rana for four days, and the Sri Lankan defence helicopters and other vessels also assisted in the search. Sadly, Rana could not be found."

The company added, "Our hearts go out to Karandeep's family and friends at this tragic hour, as well as his shipmates who worked hard searching for him. Tragic incidents like this are complex and speculation can cause additional distress to both the family and friends of Karandeep. We should be mindful of this until the investigation is complete."

items.title: We crashed AI 171: Chennai techie creates hundreds of fake emails, uses 80 phone numbers across 11 states to trap colleague
items.story:
A 30-year-old robotics engineer named Rene Joshlida from Chennai has been arrested for sending hoax bomb threats across 11 states in India. The threats were part of an elaborate scheme to frame a former colleague, Divij Prabhakar, who did not reciprocate her romantic feelings. To execute her plan, Joshlida created multiple fake email IDs and used virtual private networks (VPNs) and the dark web to avoid detection. She targeted schools, hospitals, and stadiums in 21 locations, and even claimed responsibility for an Air India plane crash in Ahmedabad on June 12, which killed at least 274 people.

The police investigation revealed that Joshlida's actions were fueled by her unrequited love for Prabhakar, whom she met during a project in Bengaluru. After he married someone else, she allegedly began sending bomb threats using variations of his name to frame him. Joshlida also harassed women she suspected of being interested in Prabhakar.

Her sophisticated tactics kept her hidden for months, but she made a crucial error by logging into both her real and fake email accounts from the same device, which allowed police to trace her IP address and arrest her. She had reportedly bought at least 80 phone numbers over the past two years to create the fake email accounts and sent hundreds of threat emails through the Tor browser and the dark web.

items.title: Cricket | Asia Cup 2025: How India and Pakistan could clash three times in UAE showdown
items.story: The Asia Cup 2025 schedule has been announced, with the tournament set to take place in the United Arab Emirates from September 9 to 28. The tournament will be played in the T20 format and is seen as a vital preparation for the T20 World Cup scheduled in India and Sri Lanka next year. India and Pakistan, both placed in Group A along with UAE and Oman, are expected to be strong contenders and could potentially face each other three times during the tournament. These potential encounters include the group stage match on September 14, a possible Super 4s face-off on September 21, and a potential final match on September 28. The matches will be hosted across venues in Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, and Dubai. The fixtures are highly anticipated due to the long-standing rivalry between the two cricketing nations.

items.title: Gunmen kill murder convict in Patna hospital
items.story: In a bold incident, five armed men broke into a hospital in Patna and fatally shot Chandan Mishra, a murder convict on parole. This audacious execution, captured on CCTV, underscores growing concerns about escalating crime in the city. On Thursday morning, five men, each armed with a pistol, entered a room in a leading private hospital and shot dead the convict who was undergoing treatment on parole, escaping without any resistance. The boldness of the execution has alarmed a city already grappling with a series of killings in July. CCTV footage showed the last gunman leaving casually. Chandan Mishra, 36, was serving a life sentence at Beur Central Jail for the 2011 murder of a businessman and was recovering from liver surgery at Paras HMRI Hospital on Bailey Road. His parole was set to end on July 18. No arrests have been made so far; however, some individuals have been detained for questioning in connection with the Patna shooting. Around 7:15 am, CCTV footage captured five men with pistols approaching Room 209 on the hospital’s second floor and firing at close range. Their faces were clearly visible in the footage, which is now widely circulated on social media. Mishra succumbed to multiple gunshot wounds. A case has been registered, and forensic and canine units were deployed to the scene. The body has been sent for autopsy. 'Some people have been detained for questioning, but no arrests have been made yet,' stated Patna SP (Central) Diksha. Mishra had over two dozen cases against him, and his 2011 conviction was related to the murder of businessman Rajendra Kesari. Police reported that Mishra often declared his intentions openly and had told Kesari, 'I will kill you tomorrow,' after Kesari refused to pay extortion money. Kesari was shot dead the following day. Patna SSP Kartikeya K Sharma indicated preliminary evidence suggested gang rivalry. 'There was a gang called Chandan-Sheru. The manner of shooting suggests a targeted hit by a rival group, potentially due to personal enmity or gang warfare,' he said. Mishra had allied with Omkarnath, alias Sheru Singh, to form the Chandan-Sheru gang, which dominated organized crime in western Bihar. Their rise led to police crackdowns and a Rs 50,000 bounty on both men. Power struggles over money and leadership eventually split the gang, with Sheru forming his own faction. Both had clashed when they were inmates at Bhagalpur Jail.

items.title: Historic Compensation for Farmers in India: Private Seed Companies Set Precedent
items.story: In a historic move, 671 maize farmers in the Mulugu district of Telangana, India, received compensation from four private seed companies, including a multinational corporation, for significant crop losses due to substandard seeds. This unprecedented action, likely the first of its kind in Telangana and possibly India, was a result of sustained government pressure and compelling video evidence. The farmers were compensated with amounts ranging from ₹60,000 to ₹1.25 lakh per acre, depending on the severity of damage and input costs. The crisis unfolded a few months ago in the mandals of Wajedu, Venkatapuram, Kannaigudem, and Tadwai in Mulugu district, where maize farmers experienced drastically low yields despite using genetically modified seeds provided by the companies. They were promised yields of four tonnes per acre but ended up harvesting barely one tonne or less. The resulting losses led to widespread protests, with farmers demanding accountability and compensation. The situation gained momentum when local officials conducted a thorough investigation by visiting each affected farmer, documenting losses on video, and gathering testimonial evidence in the presence of company representatives. After considerable effort, the government officials issued notices demanding compensation, leading to the companies complying. The compensation cheques were distributed at a public event attended by Telangana's agriculture minister, Tummala Nageswara Rao, and panchayat raj minister, Seethakka. This event highlights the gaps in India's seed regulation framework, governed by the Central Seed Act of 1966 (amended in 1972), which imposes minimal penalties of ₹500 for a first offense and ₹1,000 or six months of imprisonment for repeat violations. Farmers often have no choice but to approach consumer courts, which can be a prolonged process. S. Anvesh Reddy, chairman of the Telangana Seeds Development Corporation, stated that this is possibly the first instance in the country where hundreds of farmers received compensation from seed companies.

items.title: Income Tax Return: Are capital gains from MFs taxed differently under new & old regime? What taxpayers should know about new LTCG, STCG rules
items.story: When filing income tax returns for AY 2025-26, understanding capital gains taxation from mutual funds is crucial. Both old and new tax regimes tax these gains. Long-term gains from equity funds are taxed at 12.50% (exceeding Rs 1.25 lakh), while short-term gains are taxed at 20%. Income Tax Return Filing AY 2025-26: One important aspect of income tax return filing, apart from reporting income from salary, is also filling in details of any capital gains - short-term or long-term - that you have made during the financial year. If you are wondering whether taxation of capital gains made from mutual funds differs between the new and the old income tax regime, we have you covered. Capital gains from sale of mutual funds (MFs) are taxable In India, under both the old and new income tax regimes. The categorization of the MF, method of computation of capital gains, is not impacted by the choice of the income tax regime by an individual. All the deductions available while computing the capital gains, including towards reinvestment in the specified new asset, continue to be equally available under both the new and old income tax regimes. In general, from a taxability perspective, MFs are broadly categorized into equity MFs and non-equity MFs. There is also a special category of specified MFs within the non-equity MFs. Effective 23 July 2024, gains from sale of equity MFs, if held for more than 12 months, are classified as Long-term (LTCG) and gains (exceeding Rs 1.25 lakh) are taxable at 12.50%. Short Term Capital Gains (STCG) from sale of equity MFs are taxable at 20%. Gains from sale of non-equity MFs, held for more than 24 months, are considered LTCG and taxable at 12.50%. STCG from sale of non-equity MFs are taxable as per the income tax slab rates. Further, gains from specified MFs are deemed to be STCG irrespective of the holding period and taxable as per the tax slab rates. Applicable surcharge and cess apply on the above tax rates. The tax slab rates, surcharge rates and applicable rebates, will apply qua the tax regime chosen. The maximum surcharge under the old tax regime is 37% (triggers beyond income of Rs 5 crore) while under the new regime it is restricted to 25% (triggers beyond income of Rs 2 crore). It may be noted that under both tax regimes, surcharge is restricted to 15% on all LTCG and STCG on equity MF.

items.title: Hyderabad woman dies 6 days after suicide attempt; financial issues suspected
items.story: Mamatha, a 34-year-old vegetable vendor from Hyderabad, tragically passed away at Gandhi Hospital six days after attempting suicide at her home. She had alerted a family friend via video call on June 25 before being discovered unconscious by neighbors. It is suspected that financial difficulties were the primary cause of her distress. The incident took place in Aditya Nagar Colony, Mansoorabad, and her husband, Srinivas Reddy, a driver, was on duty at the time. The couple had been married for 17 years and have a 16-year-old daughter. Following the distress call, Mamatha was first taken to a private hospital in Vanasthalipuram and later referred to Gandhi Hospital for better treatment, where she died on the morning of July 1, 2025. Based on a complaint from her husband, the police registered a case under Section 194 of the BNSS, and the body was handed over to the family after a post-mortem examination.

items.title: Govt to compensate highway operators, investors for losses due to annual pass scheme
items.story: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) will introduce a compensation framework for private highway operators and investors, including overseas pension funds, to cover losses incurred due to the introduction of an 'annual pass' for private vehicles on national highways and expressways starting August 15. This move is significant as the highway sector has shown strong results in the government's monetization program, and NHAI is expected to receive more attention in the coming five years. A committee in the road transport ministry will develop the framework within a month after discussions with stakeholders. Companies such as Cube Mobility, IRB Infrastructure, and the Adani Group, as well as sovereign funds and asset managers like NIIF, and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, have heavily invested in the sector. Additionally, there are several highway stretches where private developers are collecting tolls under existing contracts. Concerns have been raised by private investors regarding potential losses since they have paid upfront based on projected traffic and toll revenue. However, the NHAI insists on keeping the August 15 deadline, emphasizing the need to consider the interests of all stakeholders, including users. The NHAI has monetized projects through three models: Toll Operate Transfer (TOT), infrastructure investment trusts (InvITs), and securitization. Work on the annual pass scheme began months ago, and all implications have been assessed using past toll collection data. NHAI has achieved 71% of the monetization target in the highway sector, raising Rs 1.2 lakh crore out of the targeted Rs 1.6 lakh crore until FY2024-25.

items.title: Telangana HC seeks fresh affidavit from heritage director on construction near Golconda fort
items.story: The Telangana High Court has instructed the state’s director of heritage, who also acts as the competent authority under the National Monuments Authority (NMA), to submit a new affidavit about the permission given to a builder for a construction project on a 14-acre site in Qila Mohammed Nagar, next to the outer wall of the protected Golconda fort. This order came from a division bench including Chief Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh and Justice P Sam Koshy during an appeal by a businessman contesting a March 2025 ruling by a single judge of the high court. The single judge had previously directed the director of heritage to approve the builder's project in line with the NMA's guidelines. During the hearing, Chief Justice Singh questioned whether the competent authority was merely a facilitator or had an active role in enforcing the orders, emphasizing the need for thoughtful application. The Chief Justice clarified that there was no objection to authorities implementing orders as long as they complied with the law. The bench noted that previously, the director of heritage had opposed the builder's request in a counter-affidavit submitted on June 21, 2021, but had not provided any further clarifications on whether those concerns were resolved or if the builder met the required conditions. The appellant's counsel informed the court that the no-objection certificate granted to the builder by the NMA in April 2019 is currently under challenge in a public interest litigation pending before the high court. Considering these points and citing relevant sections of the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, the bench asked the competent authority to provide a clear affidavit confirming whether the builder had met all necessary requirements. The case is scheduled for further hearing in two weeks.

items.title: Now, International Federation of Pilots also says AI 171 report 'raises questions, provides no answers'
items.story:
Following the preliminary report on the Air India AI 171 crash in Ahmedabad, the International Federation of Air Line Pilots’ Associations (IFALPA) cautioned against "hasty conclusions," echoing concerns about a suicide theory. The ICPA has also strongly condemned the "reckless and unfounded insinuation of pilot suicide" circulating after the report's release.

The preliminary report into the crash of the June 12 Air India AI 171 crash in Ahmedabad continues to draw criticism. Now, the International Federation of Air Line Pilots’ Associations (IFALPA) has warned against jumping to "hasty conclusions." The report, which was known to a section of the western media 44 hours before being made public in India by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), has led to a suicide theory being proposed, which has been criticized by pilots and other aviation experts.

"Whilst this preliminary report by its very nature raises many questions, it does not provide answers, and any extrapolation of its content can only be regarded as guesswork, which is not helpful to the good conduct of the investigation. IFALPA also notes that the report clearly states that no safety recommendations are being provided at this stage," IFALPA said after reviewing the report.

"The victims, including the families of the crew and passengers of Air India 171, deserve our collective professionalism while the full investigation is conducted," it adds.

Before IFALPA, the India Commercial Pilots' Association (ICPA) had slammed the "reckless and unfounded insinuation of pilot suicide" that has been doing the rounds after the preliminary report into AI 171 crash was made public on Saturday.

While not sharing the cockpit voice recorder transcript, the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) report had this one line: "One of the pilots is heard asking the other why did he cutoff. The other pilot responded that he did not do so."

ICPA, which is the union of erstwhile Indian Airlines, said in a statement issued Sunday: "We are deeply disturbed by speculative narratives, particularly the reckless and unfounded insinuation of pilot suicide. Let us be unequivocally clear: there is absolutely no basis for such a claim at this stage, and invoking such a serious allegation based on incomplete or preliminary information is not only irresponsible—it is deeply insensitive to the individuals and families involved."

Expressing their "unwavering support for the flight crew of Air India flight Al 171," the ICPA statement added: "Pilots undergo extensive psychological and professional screening, recurrent training, and operate under the highest standards of safety, responsibility, and mental fitness. To casually suggest pilot suicide in the absence of verified evidence is a gross violation of ethical reporting and a disservice to the dignity of the profession."

"As aviation professionals, we trust and respect the rigorous investigative protocols established by competent authorities. These inquiries are designed to uncover facts methodically and without bias. Until the official investigation is concluded and the final report is published, any speculation—especially of such a grave nature—is unacceptable and must be condemned.... The crew of Al 171 acted in line with their training and responsibilities under challenging conditions. They deserve support—not vilification based on conjecture," it said.

items.title: 2006 Mumbai train blasts: Supreme Court stays Bombay HC order; clarifies released accused won't return to jail
items.story: The Supreme Court of India has stayed a recent decision by the Bombay High Court that acquitted all individuals previously convicted of planning and executing the July 11, 2006, serial bomb blasts on Mumbai's suburban rail network. This decision was made after Solicitor General Tushar Mehta informed the Supreme Court that the high court's verdict could affect other cases being tried under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA). The Supreme Court clarified that the high court's decision will not serve as a precedent in other cases. The Bombay High Court had previously refused to confirm the death sentences of five men involved in the case and acquitted all 12 accused, citing a lack of evidence regarding the type of explosives used and questioning the admissibility of confessional statements due to allegations of torture. The high court also expressed doubts about witness credibility and procedural issues during the identification process. The accused individuals had been detained under MCOCA and had spent nearly two decades in prison. The high court's ruling has sparked significant debate within political and legal circles regarding its implications on the justice system and the conduct of investigations.

items.title: 2 terrorists killed near LoC, infiltration bid foiled
items.story: In a joint operation based on intelligence inputs, Indian soldiers neutralized two terrorists near the Line of Control (LoC) in Poonch district, Jammu & Kashmir. The gunfight erupted after troops detected suspicious movement in a forested area. Authorities recovered assault rifles, a pistol, ammunition, grenades, IEDs, and communication devices. Soldiers gunned down two terrorists early Wednesday during a fierce gunfight near the LoC, foiling an infiltration attempt based on joint intelligence inputs from military and police sources. The shooting started after troops spotted suspicious movement in a forested area close to the LoC. According to defence PRO Lt Col Suneel Bartwal, the operation was based on credible inputs from military intelligence and J&K police regarding the presence of terrorists in the area. Troops found two assault rifles, a pistol with ammunition, hand grenades, IEDs, and a cache of other war-like stores, including medicines, a communication device, and logistical supplies. The area remains under cordon as a search operation continues. The incident follows the killing of three terrorists linked to the April 22 Pahalgam attack, who were shot dead in Srinagar under 'Op Mahadev' on July 28.

items.title: IND vs ENG Tests: England penalised for slow over rate in Lord's Test win; drop place in WTC standings
items.story: England's cricket team has been penalized for maintaining a slow over-rate during their recent Test match victory over India at Lord's. As a result, England has been docked two ICC World Test Championship points and fined 10% of their match fees. This penalty has caused England's points to drop from 24 to 22 out of 36, reducing their percentage from 66.67% to 61.11%, and consequently, they have slipped from second to third position in the championship standings. The breach was acknowledged by England's captain, Ben Stokes, who accepted the sanctions without contest. The penalties were applied under Article 16.11.2 of the ICC World Test Championship playing conditions, which mandates a deduction of points for each over a team falls short. Additionally, under Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct, a financial penalty of 5% of the match fee is imposed for each over not bowled within the allotted time. The match officials, including on-field umpires Paul Reiffel and Sharfuddoula Ibne Shahid, third umpire Ahsan Raza, and fourth umpire Graham Lloyd, reported the slow over-rate. This ruling has allowed Sri Lanka to move up to second place in the standings. Despite the penalty, England leads the five-match series 2-1 after a closely contested match.

items.title: Police book YouTube channel for defamatory video against Bandi
items.story: Hyderabad: The cyber crime police have registered a case against a YouTube channel for allegedly publishing a defamatory video targeting Union Minister of State for Home, Bandi Sanjay Kumar. The case was filed following a complaint lodged by RV Pavan Maitreya of the BJP's legal cell on Tuesday. According to the complaint, a video uploaded on June 26 by the channel 'Bharat Yuvasena' made baseless and derogatory allegations, accusing the minister of colluding with political rivals. The content was allegedly intended to malign the minister's reputation, the complainant said. Investigators have received both a copy of the video and its web link for examination. Based on the complaint, police registered a case under section 67 of the Information Technology Act and section 336(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which pertains to forgery intended to harm reputation. Cyber crime officials said they will be approaching Google to obtain the details of the individual who uploaded the video and will proceed further based on the findings.

items.title: ACPDC merit list 2025 released for first-year diploma admissions at acpdc.gujarat.gov.in
items.story: The Admission Committee for Professional Diploma Courses (ACPDC) has announced the provisional merit list for first-year diploma admissions in engineering and technology for the 2025 academic session in Gujarat. Candidates can access and download the list from the official ACPDC website, acpdc.gujarat.gov.in. The process for choice filling in the mock round will take place from July 2 to July 5, 2025. The final merit list and results of the mock round are scheduled to be released on July 10, 2025, coinciding with the start of the choice filling for the first round of actual admissions. Students are advised to adhere to the admission timeline to secure their desired diploma seats.

items.title: ‘Operation Narnia’ and 'Red Wedding': How Israel pulled off 'Game of Thrones' on Iran
items.story:
Israel executed strikes against Iran, targeting military leaders and nuclear scientists in an operation referred to as 'Red Wedding' and 'Operation Narnia'. With support from the United States, which provided precision strikes on nuclear sites, the operation inflicted significant damage on Iran's nuclear infrastructure and decimated the leadership of the Revolutionary Guard. Israel's actions exposed Iran's weaknesses in defense and intelligence. As a result of these operations, a ceasefire has been established, but future negotiations are uncertain, and there are concerns that Iran may accelerate its nuclear weaponization.

The operation, described as a high-wire act of deception and assassination, resulted in the death of nine leading nuclear scientists before dawn. The Wall Street Journal reported that Israeli jets eliminated Iran’s top air force leadership in a single night, likening it to a massacre from "Game of Thrones". The events mark a significant shift in the Middle Eastern power balance, with Israel solidifying its regional military dominance.

The operation involved a long-standing intelligence and training effort, with Israeli forces preparing for such missions since the 1990s. To maintain the element of surprise, Israel employed strategic deception, including fake weddings and false narratives about tensions with the US.

Despite the ceasefire, the situation remains tense, with Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei insisting that the strikes achieved nothing significant, although satellite imagery and reports suggest otherwise. Analysts are divided on the long-term impact on Iran's nuclear program, with the potential for future escalations remaining high.

items.title: Balasore student told ex-principal about harassment 6 months ago
items.story: A 20-year-old student from Balasore, Odisha, who committed self-immolation on the college campus on July 12, had previously informed college authorities that her Head of Department (HoD) had solicited sexual favors from her six months ago, according to a recent investigation. During a meeting on June 30 at the then-principal's office, who has since been suspended, the student reported the HoD's inappropriate behavior. Despite the HoD denying the allegations, the issue was forwarded to the college's internal complaints committee for further investigation. The University Grants Commission (UGC), higher education committees, and the criminal branch are conducting investigations into the matter. They are examining all aspects related to the student's self-immolation and her allegations of sexual harassment, as well as the findings of the internal complaints committee. Although classes resumed at the college on Friday following days of protests, student attendance was low, and the campus atmosphere remained somber and tense.

items.title: Sitaare Zameen Par Box Office Collection Day 14: Aamir Khan and Genelia D’Souza Starrer Maintains a Steady Pace on Its Second Thursday; Mints Over Rs 135 Crore in India
items.story: Aamir Khan and Genelia D’Souza's film "Sitaare Zameen Par" continues to perform well at the box office, earning Rs 2.75 crore on its 14th day, bringing its total collection to Rs 135.56 crore in India. Despite a slight dip in audience turnout, the film maintains a strong presence with a touching story and strong performances. The movie is now facing competition from the new release "Metro In Dino." Released on June 20, 2025, "Sitaare Zameen Par" has been a topic of conversation since its debut, showing a solid performance at the box office. It has sustained its earnings even with new films being released, and reports suggest it made Rs 2.75 crore on both its 13th and 14th days. The movie features a cumulative collection of Rs 135.56 crore after 14 days in theaters. The film, directed by RS Prasanna, is a spiritual sequel to the 2007 film "Taare Zameen Par." It tells the story of a suspended basketball coach, played by Aamir Khan, who is ordered to train a team of neurodivergent players as part of community service. Initially considering it an impossible task, he eventually experiences a significant transformation. Genelia D’Souza co-stars, bringing warmth and charm to the narrative. The film also introduces 10 new faces who have delivered strong performances, enhancing the emotional depth of the story.

items.title: Shocking! Radhika Yadav’s friend stunned by disturbing comments: ‘Father did the right thing’
items.story:
Following the tragic murder of tennis player Radhika Yadav by her father, a close friend, Himaanshika Singh Rajput, has condemned online justifications of the crime. Rajput highlighted disturbing comments on social media, where some users appeared to defend the father's actions, citing societal expectations and patriarchal norms.

Himaanshika Singh Rajput, a close friend of the slain tennis player, has alleged in social media videos that people are justifying Radhika's father murdering his own daughter. Deepak Yadav, 49, confessed to the crime and told police he was taunted for living off her income from a tennis academy. The 25-year-old was shot four times, three in the back and one in the shoulder, according to the postmortem report by a board of three doctors, said police.

In a new video, Himaanshika highlighted disturbing comments from her earlier posts, where several men appeared to justify her father's alleged actions. Comments included phrases like "respect for the father," "good father," and "father did the right thing," while some even went as far as accusing her of being dishonest.

"I posted two videos about Radhika Yadav last week, and I was shocked to see my entire comment section filled with men defending men. This is not okay. Justice must be served. Men need to understand that this world doesn't belong to them alone, women exist, women resist, and women will continue to fight for each other," she wrote on her Instagram.

"It is not acceptable for men or parents to impose 'small' restrictions at home, like telling girls what to wear, where to go, or how to behave. These are not small. These are part of the problem. It's time for men to educate other men."

"It's time for parents not just mothers to teach their sons how to respect women. Enough of only teaching daughters how to stay safe. When will men finally learn?"

Himaanshika had earlier said that Radhika was "miserable" 10 days before her death. "She was completely broken and had simply given up. She even told her family that she was ready to live according to their instructions."

She also claimed that Radhika's father had "psychological issues", saying that he appeared to have "lost his mind" as he would walk around with an "expressionless" poker face. Sharing details about the Yadav household, Himaanshika stated that the family was very "orthodox" and was constantly worried about how society perceived them.

"Radhika loved posting videos and reels, but eventually, that stopped. Her family would often pressure her, saying, 'What will people say?' They had a problem with almost everything and restricted Radhika from doing what she liked. She even had a curfew," she said.

items.title: 75+ Kargil Vijay Diwas 2025: Wishes, Messages, Quotes, Images, And WhatsApp to Honour India’s Brave Soldiers
items.story:
Kargil Vijay Diwas, observed annually on July 26th, is a day to commemorate the courage and sacrifice of Indian soldiers during the Kargil War. This day serves as a powerful reminder of their unwavering dedication and unity in defending the nation's integrity under challenging conditions.

Every year on this day, the nation pauses not just to remember but to feel, to honor, and to salute the courage of those who fought in the Kargil War. It's not merely a date on the calendar; it's a reminder of what true courage looks like, high in the mountains where every breath is hard-earned, and every step can cost a life. Kargil Vijay Diwas isn't about glorifying war; it's about remembering the grit, unity, and sacrifice that can't be forgotten.

The Kargil War wasn't a distant chapter from history; it was real, recent, and raw. Many of us still remember those days—the news reports, the grainy footage, and the unfamiliar place names that suddenly became headlines. Families sat in front of the TV, trying to make sense of it all, hoping for an end, and praying for the safety of loved ones.

The soldiers weren't just people in uniform; they were young, just like us. Sons who had just left home, brothers who hadn't even grown a beard, friends who joked until the last minute. Ordinary people who did something unimaginable: they walked into danger and never looked back, simply because it was their job to protect their country. They asked for nothing in return, just the hope that they would be remembered.

Kargil Vijay Diwas matters because it reminds us that patriotism isn't about loud slogans; it's about quiet strength. It's about standing firm against adversity, with the awareness of real fear, but the duty is greater. This day brings back the faces of heroes we've never met but owe so much to. It inspires us to be better, kinder, and more grateful—because someone else paid the price for our peace.

Sharing wishes, messages, and quotes on this day isn't just for social media updates. It's a small way to keep those stories alive, a way to say: We remember. We're grateful. We won't forget. Whether it's a status update, a short quote, or a simple thank you—it all counts. It's about keeping the memory alive and passing it forward.

items.title: EXCLUSIVE | 'Country over my child': KL Rahul's first words before England Tests
items.story: KL Rahul chose national duties over personal moments after becoming a father recently. As he prepared for the England Test series, he demonstrated his commitment by scoring a century in an unofficial Test and another in the first official Test match. With senior players like Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma retired from Tests, Rahul stepped up to guide the younger team. His dedication was evident when he expressed his willingness to prioritize the team over spending time with his newborn. Rahul's performance, including scores of 116 and 51 in practice matches, highlighted his importance as a senior player and leader. His actions and statements emphasized his focus on leading the team in this transitional phase, balancing responsibility with the opportunity to mentor the next generation of players. His journey reflects a bridge between India's cricket past and its promising future.

items.title: RERA fines agent Rs 6L for promoting unregistered flats, fraud transactions
items.story: The Telangana Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA) has fined a real estate agent Rs 6.17 lakh for promoting an unregistered real estate project and issuing receipts by impersonating the builder. The case involved Aaditri Housing Pvt. Ltd and two agents, Jakkepalli Sri Lakshmi and Jakkepalli Appa Rao. Venkata Naga Sai Gupta Chegu, a bank manager, filed the complaint, alleging that he and his wife transferred over Rs 1.2 crore between 2019 and 2023 for two flats. However, only Rs 44.9 lakh was credited to Aaditri Housing's account, while the agents received the rest through various transactions without informing the developer. The receipts and documents were fabricated in the builder's name. RERA directed Aaditri Housing to complete and register the flat in the complainant's name and warned of further penalties for delays.

items.title: ‘Include 40 T backward castes in central OBC list’
items.story: Hyderabad: The chairman of the Telangana State Backward Classes Commission, G Niranjan, has urged the Union government to add 40 backward castes to the central Other Backward Classes (OBC) list. He sent a letter to this effect to the Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Virendra Kumar. Niranjan highlighted that when Telangana was established, the central OBC list for the state was declared in 2016. However, while the state had 112 castes recognized in its list, the central government included only 90 castes in its list. Since then, the state has added orphans and 17 additional castes, bringing the total in the state BC list to 130. Consequently, there are now 40 castes that need to be added to the central list. Niranjan stressed that the state government has consistently requested the inclusion of these castes in the central list since 2016. The former principal secretary of BC Welfare sent numerous letters between 2016 and 2020. Furthermore, a hearing was conducted in December 2021 in Delhi under the National BC Commission to discuss this inclusion. Another hearing was held on September 5, 2023, in New Delhi, chaired by the National BC Commission chairman, Hansraj Gangaram Ahir. However, the central government has yet to announce a decision on the inclusion of these 40 castes. Niranjan noted that individuals from these castes are missing out on opportunities in central government educational institutions and jobs.

items.title: Donald Trump says more tariff letters coming! US President warns no extension on August 1 deadline; ‘there has been no change…’ - Times of India
items.story: US President Donald Trump has announced that new tariffs on foreign imports will commence on August 1, 2025, with no extensions granted. Letters detailing these tariffs have been sent to various countries, including Japan and South Korea. The tariffs will range from 25% to 40% unless trade agreements are reached before the deadline. Trump made this announcement on Truth Social, stating that there will be no changes to the implementation date. This contradicts his previous statements that suggested the deadline was flexible. Earlier, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent mentioned that the tariffs would not be enforced until August 1 to allow more time for negotiations. Trump had indicated that letters would be sent to over a dozen countries, including Japan, South Korea, Indonesia, Bangladesh, Thailand, South Africa, and Malaysia, outlining the tariffs. Key US trading partners, Japan and South Korea, have already received notices of 25% duties. Negotiations with India are ongoing, with Trump indicating they are close to finalizing a trade deal. The initial tariffs announced on April 2 included a 10% duty on most imports, but these were postponed for 90 days, with a new enforcement date of August 1 set.

items.title: WATCH: Shahid Afridi watches on as India Champions refuse to play Pakistan, his previous remarks come back to hurt him
items.story: Yuvraj Singh's India Champions team has withdrawn from the World Championship of Legends semi-final against the Pakistan Champions. This decision was made to protest the strained relations following the Pahalgam terror attack. Despite Shahid Afridi's anticipation and previous provocative remarks, India refused to play, even after their victory against the West Indies Champions. Consequently, the Pakistan Champions advanced to the final due to India's withdrawal. Afridi had previously commented, suggesting that India would be compelled to play against Pakistan. However, India's stance remained firm, prioritizing their principles over the semi-final match, leading to their exit from the tournament.

items.title: ‘Tell the truth!’: Meghan Markle's three-word grenade at Buckingham Palace - Serena Williams’s sage mantra, a delivery-room dance and the royal family's collective shrug
items.story: Amidst royal celebrations, Meghan Markle's podcast appearance sparked a media storm as she encouraged people to "tell the truth," reviving tensions with Buckingham Palace. This follows the Sussexes' pattern of sharing personal narratives and facing scrutiny. Serena Williams' advice, "A lie can't live forever," highlights Meghan's approach. The podcast, aired in Los Angeles, saw Meghan confronting the royal institution she once served by emphasizing truthfulness. Meghan's statement was part of a broader media strategy, reflecting the Sussexes' ongoing conflict with the royal family, characterized by revealing personal stories and challenging established narratives. Meghan's truth-bomb was not merely about correcting headlines; it was another move in an eight-year information war where silence itself becomes a weapon. Serena Williams, a close friend of Meghan, supports her with the mantra "A lie can't live forever," which Meghan uses to counter tabloid criticism. The timing of Meghan's statement adds pressure on palace aides managing King Charles's health updates and Princess Kate's cautious return, as her words continue to make headlines despite claims of her irrelevance by royal commentators. Meghan's podcast appearance also coincided with her 2021 "Baby Mama Dance" video going viral, which she used to showcase an authentic, fun life away from the cameras. Critics, however, accused her of seeking attention. The podcast reinforced Meghan's brand strategy, demonstrating her lifestyle label's authenticity while providing insight into her life. Buckingham Palace has chosen silence in response, hoping to starve the story of attention, though Serena's mantra continues to resonate.

items.title: Can't win today's warfare with yesterday's weapons, desi drone tech must: CDS General Anil Chauhan
items.story:
General Anil Chauhan, India's Chief of Defence Staff, emphasized the importance of developing indigenous drone and counter-UAS technologies to maintain a strategic advantage in modern warfare. Speaking at the Manekshaw Centre in Delhi, he stressed that relying on outdated foreign systems is not viable, as demonstrated during Operation Sindoor. In this operation, Pakistan utilized unarmed drones and loiter munitions on May 10, but they failed to cause any damage to Indian military or civilian infrastructure. Most of these threats were neutralized through a combination of kinetic and non-kinetic means. 

General Chauhan highlighted the need for India to accelerate the development of homegrown drone technology and counter-UAS grids, as foreign systems often have widely known specifications that adversaries can anticipate. He pointed out that recent global conflicts have shown how drones can significantly alter the tactical balance, making self-reliance in UAVs and C-UAS a strategic imperative for India. 

The general noted that drones, despite being smaller and less aerodynamic, are reshaping conventional warfare by being cheaper, harder to detect, and yet sophisticated. This shift in warfare dynamics necessitates securing lower airspace and developing integrated counter-UAV systems. The global trend towards drone-dominated conflicts, as seen in the Israel-Iran and Russia-Ukraine situations, underscores the urgency for India to advance its indigenous drone capabilities.

items.title: Your 'action' will kill 8 million kids: Microsoft founder Bill Gates warns US government
items.story: Bill Gates, the founder of Microsoft and former CEO, has raised concerns over the US government's decision to cut funding for global health initiatives. He warns that these cuts could lead to an additional 8 million child deaths by 2040, citing a study from The Lancet. Gates emphasizes the importance of aid in saving lives, drawing from his 25 years of experience in global health. He highlights that abrupt withdrawal of aid without a plan leads to loss of lives. Gates has been involved in global health for over 25 years, working alongside scientists and public health experts to strengthen healthcare delivery across continents. He mentions that cuts are already affecting programs like tuberculosis testing and malaria prevention. Gates, who recently visited Nigeria and Ethiopia, observed the impact of these funding cuts on healthcare services. He urges the US Congress to restore funding for programs like PEPFAR and the Global Fund, stating, 'It's not too late to change course.'

items.title: SC: Police can’t serve notice or summon through WhatsApp or other electronic means
items.story: The Supreme Court of India has ruled that police and other investigating agencies cannot serve notices or summons to an accused through WhatsApp or other electronic means. This decision was made while rejecting a plea from the Haryana government, which sought to use electronic means for serving notices. The court emphasized that such practices could adversely affect an individual's liberty. The Haryana government had argued that the new Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita allowed the use of electronic means for court proceedings, including the issuance and service of summons and warrants, and should be applicable to police as well. However, a bench of Justices M M Sundresh and N K Singh noted that summons issued by a court are judicial acts, whereas notices issued by investigating agencies are executive acts, and the procedures for judicial acts cannot be applied to executive acts. The court clarified that the issue of liberty is involved in police summons as non-compliance could lead to arrest. Therefore, it is appropriate for such notices to be served in person rather than through electronic communication. The bench accepted the submission of senior advocate Siddharth Luthra, acting as amicus curiae, that summons should be served personally. The bench highlighted that the protection of an individual's liberty is a fundamental right guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution. Section 35(6) of the BNSS, 2023, aims to secure this right from being encroached upon by relevant authorities, and any attempt to interpret this provision as merely procedural would amount to rewriting the provision itself. The legislature has specifically excluded the service of a notice under Section 35 of the BNSS from procedures permissible through electronic communication, reflecting a clear legislative intent. The court concluded that electronic communication is not a valid mode of serving notice under Section 35 of the BNSS, as its omission indicates legislative intent, and introducing such a procedure would violate this intent.

items.title: 'Not favourable': VP Dhankhar criticises India's political atmosphere; calls for 'greater decorum'
items.story: Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar expressed concern over India's current political climate, describing it as unfavorable for democracy. He stressed that political opponents should not be viewed as enemies and called for greater decorum among lawmakers. Speaking at an event organized by the Rajasthan Pragatisheel Manch in Jaipur, Dhankhar highlighted that the intensity and tone of political exchanges are harming the democratic and social fabric of the nation. He emphasized that political opponents are not enemies and warned that public dissatisfaction with lawmakers' conduct could undermine trust in democratic institutions. Dhankhar also pointed out the importance of opposition parties in a democracy, stating they are not adversaries of the ruling parties. He advocated for constructive debate and listening to opposing views to strengthen one's own stance.

items.title: '6 balls, 6 different actions': Ishan Kishan imitates MS Dhoni, Harbhajan Singh and Shane Warne in 1 over - WATCH
items.story: Ishan Kishan, during his playing stint with Nottinghamshire in the County Championship, has been making headlines not just for his batting, but for an unexpected display of bowling skills. Known primarily as a wicketkeeper-batsman, Kishan turned heads when he took on the bowling role in a rain-affected match against Somerset at Taunton. During one of his overs, he humorously imitated legendary cricketers’ styles, including MS Dhoni, Harbhajan Singh, and Shane Warne. The over featured a mix of off-spin and leg-spin deliveries, and his mimicry of these cricket icons amused both teammates and fans. A clip of his performance was shared on social media by the official County Championship account, bringing a lighthearted moment to the match. Kishan’s last appearance in a Test match for India was during the West Indies tour in July 2023, and his performance in the IPL 2025 with Sunrisers Hyderabad was moderate, scoring 354 runs in 14 games. However, his red-ball form in England appears more promising, with strong batting performances in his two outings so far, scoring 87 and 77 runs in recent matches.

items.title: Monsoon season ends; India gets 8% more than normal rainfall - 5th highest since 2001
items.story:
India's southwest monsoon season concluded with 8% above-normal rainfall, the fifth-highest since 2001. Conversely, East and North-East India experienced a severe deficit, recording their second-lowest rainfall since 1901. Despite localized disasters, robust rains significantly increased Kharif crop acreage, raising hopes for record foodgrain output. Above-normal rainfall is anticipated for October-December, potentially delaying the winter monsoon's onset.

NEW DELHI: The four-month summer (southwest) monsoon season ended on Tuesday, with India reporting 8% more than normal rainfall. East and North-East India, however, reported a huge deficit of more than 20% and witnessed the second-lowest rainfall in the rainy season since 1901. The country as a whole, on the other hand, saw the fifth-highest rainfall this year since 2001 and the 38th highest since 1901.

“Bihar, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam and Meghalaya saw deficient rainfall in three of the four monsoon months. The lowest rainfall in the monsoon season in the region was recorded in 2013,” IMD chief Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said. “Rainfall over east and northeast India has been deficient in many years in recent times. There is a trend that shows that rainfall over this region has been decreasing since 2020.”

Though the ‘above normal’ monsoon season was marked by many disasters, including cloudbursts, landslides, floods and mudslides, especially in northwest India, the good rains helped farmers increase their acreage of Kharif (summer sown) crops over not just last year but also over the normal sown area of the season.

The agriculture ministry’s latest data shows the country reported an overall acreage of 1,120 lakh hectares this Kharif season, which is 24 lakh hectares more than the normal acreage. This raises hopes of record foodgrain output during the 2025-26 crop year.

The season technically ended on Tuesday, but certain parts of the country will continue to report rainfall for a couple of more weeks, till the complete withdrawal of the monsoon in mid-Oct. The delay may delay the onset of northeast (winter) monsoon in Peninsular India.

Mohapatra said most parts of the country are expected to receive above-normal rainfall during the post-summer monsoon season (Oct to Dec). In Oct alone, the country is expected to receive 15% more than normal rainfall. The forecast suggests the winter monsoon (Oct to Dec) rainfall over south Peninsular India, is most likely to be above normal. The IMD chief said maximum (day) temperatures in Oct are likely to be above normal in most parts of east-northeast and northwest, whereas “normal to below-normal” maximum temperatures are expected in other regions of India during the month.

items.title: Telangana HC junks plea to halt construction of toilets in Jogulamba Gadwal district
items.story: The Telangana High Court has dismissed a petition that sought to halt the construction of toilets at a Zilla Parishad High School located in Undavelly village, Jogulamba Gadwal district. The petitioner, Nutan Kumar Reddy, argued that the construction of the toilets near residential homes and borewells infringed upon fundamental rights. Reddy requested the court to order the relocation of the toilets to another area within the school premises, in consultation with the affected villagers and following the instructions of the additional collector. The school, which spans over 7 acres, is building 12 toilets on its campus. Justice K Lakshman noted that the petitioner did not provide any substantial reasons beyond vague allegations. The court refrained from interfering in the construction process, emphasizing the importance of these facilities for the school, which accommodates approximately 350 students, including 250 girls, and subsequently dismissed the petition.

items.title: Air India crash: What AAIB report confirms, what it rules out, what still remains unanswered
items.story:
A preliminary report on the Air India Flight 171 crash in Ahmedabad reveals a dual engine failure caused by fuel cutoff switches being inexplicably moved. Cockpit recordings capture confusion among the pilots, with one denying responsibility. Despite engine restarts, the plane crashed shortly after takeoff.

In its first official account of the June 12 crash that killed 260 people in Ahmedabad, the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has released a 15-page preliminary report into Air India Flight 171. The Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner plunged into a medical college hostel moments after takeoff, becoming one of India’s worst aviation tragedies in decades and the first fatal crash of a Dreamliner globally.
